column3: But when the Order comes from the Primal Lord God, O Nanak, even an ant can take away his breath of life. ||7||

column2: sabadha(n) rata(n) hita(n) miaa keerata(n) kalee karam kiratuaa ||
column3: To be imbued and attuned to the Word of the Shabad; to be kind and compassionate; to sing the Kirtan of the Lord's Praises - these are the most worthwhile actions in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga.

column2: miTa(n)t tatraagat bharam moha(n) ||
column3: In this way, one's inner doubts and emotional attachments are dispelled.

column2: bhagavaan ramana(n) sarabatr thaaniye(n) ||
column3: God is pervading and permeating all places.

column2: dhirasaT tuya(n) amogh dharasana(n) basa(n)t saadh rasanaa ||
column3: So obtain the Blessed Vision of His Darshan; He dwells upon the tongues of the Holy.

column2: har har har hare naanak pria(n) jaap japanaa ||8||
column3: O Nanak, meditate and chant the Name of the Beloved Lord, Har, Har, Har, Haray. ||8||

column2: ghaTa(n)t roopa(n) ghaTa(n)t dheepa(n) ghaTa(n)t rav saseear nakhayetr gagana(n) ||
column3: Beauty fades away, islands fade away, the sun, moon, stars and sky fade away.

column2: ghaTa(n)t basudhaa gir tar sikha(n)dda(n) ||
column3: The earth, mountains, forests and lands fade away.

column2: ghaTa(n)t lalanaa sut bhraat heeta(n) ||
column3: One's spouse, children, siblings and loved friends fade away.

column2: ghaTa(n)t kanik maanik maiaa savairoopa(n) ||
column3: Gold and jewels and the incomparable beauty of Maya fade away.

column2: neh ghaTa(n)t keval gopaal achut ||
column3: Only the Eternal, Unchanging Lord does not fade away.

column2: asathira(n) naanak saadh jan ||9||
column3: O Nanak, only the humble Saints are steady and stable forever. ||9||

column2: neh bila(n)b dharama(n) bila(n)b paapa(n) ||
column3: Do not delay in practicing righteousness; delay in committing sins.

column2: dhiraRa(n)t naama(n) taja(n)t lobha(n) ||
column3: Implant the Naam, the Name of the Lord, within yourself, and abandon greed.

column2: saran sa(n)ta(n) kilabikh naasa(n) praapata(n) dharam lakhiyen ||
column3: In the Sanctuary of the Saints, the sins are erased. The character of righteousness is received by that person,

column2: naanak jeh suprasa(n)n maadhaveh ||10||
column3: O Nanak, with whom the Lord is pleased and satisfied. ||10||

column2: mirat moha(n) alap budhaye(n) racha(n)t banitaa binodh saaha(n) ||
column3: The person of shallow understanding is dying in emotional attachment; he is engrossed in pursuits of pleasure with his wife.

column2: jauaban bahikaram kanik ku(n)ddaleh ||
column3: With youthful beauty and golden earrings,

column2: bachitr ma(n)dhir sobha(n)t basatraa itaye(n)t maiaa bayeaapita(n) ||
column3: wondrous mansions, decorations and clothes - this is how Maya clings to him.

column2: he achut saran sa(n)t naanak bho bhagavaane nameh ||11||
column3: O Eternal, Unchanging, Benevolent Lord God, O Sanctuary of the Saints, Nanak humbly bows to You. ||11||

column2: janama(n) ta marana(n) harakha(n) ta soga(n) bhoga(n) ta roga(n) ||
column3: If there is birth, then there is death. If there is pleasure, then there is pain. If there is enjoyment, then there is disease.

column2: uoocha(n) ta neecha(n) naan(h)aa su moocha(n) ||
column3: If there is high, then there is low. If there is small, then there is great.

column2: raaja(n) ta maana(n) abhimaana(n) ta heena(n) ||
column3: If there is power, then there is pride. If there is egotistical pride, then there will be a fall.

column2: pravirat maaraga(n) varata(n)t binaasana(n) ||
column3: Engrossed in worldly ways, one is ruined.

column2: gobi(n)dh bhajan saadh sa(n)gen asathira(n) naanak bhagava(n)t bhajanaasana(n) ||12||
column3: Meditating and vibrating on the Lord of the Universe in the Company of the Holy, you shall become steady and stable. Nanak vibrates and meditates on the Lord God. ||12||

column2: kirapa(n)t hareea(n) mat tat giaana(n) ||
column3: By the Grace of God, genuine understanding comes to the mind.

column2: bigaseedhiye budhaa kusal thaana(n) ||
column3: The intellect blossoms forth, and one finds a place in the realm of celestial bliss.

column2: basiye(n)t rikhia(n) tiaag maana(n) ||
column3: The senses are brought under control, and pride is abandoned.

column2: seetala(n)t ridhaya(n) dhiraR sa(n)t giaana(n) ||
column3: The heart is cooled and soothed, and the wisdom of the Saints is implanted within.

column2: raha(n)t janama(n) har dharas leenaa ||
column3: Reincarnation is ended, and the Blessed Vision of the Lord's Darshan is obtained.

column2: baaja(n)t naanak sabadh beenaa(n) ||13||
column3: O Nanak, the musical instrument of the Word of the Shabad vibrates and resounds within. ||13||

column2: kaha(n)t bedhaa guna(n)t guneeaa suna(n)t baalaa bahu bidh prakaaraa ||
column3: The Vedas preach and recount God's Glories; people hear them by various ways and means.

column2: dhiraRa(n)t subidhiaa har har kirapaalaa ||
column3: The Merciful Lord, Har, Har, implants spiritual wisdom within.

column2: naam dhaan jaacha(n)t naanak dhainahaar gur gopaalaa ||14||
column3: Nanak begs for the Gift of the Naam, the Name of the Lord. The Guru is the Great Giver, the Lord of the World. ||14||

column2: neh chi(n)taa maat pit bhraateh neh chi(n)taa kachh lok keh ||
column3: Do not worry so much about your mother, father and siblings. Do not worry so much about other people.

column2: neh chi(n)taa banitaa sut meeteh pravirat maiaa sanaba(n)dhaneh ||
column3: Do not worry about your spouse, children and friends. You are obsessed with your involvements in Maya.

column2: dhiaal ek bhagavaan purakheh naanak sarab jeea pratipaalakeh ||15||
column3: The One Lord God is Kind and Compassionate, O Nanak. He is the Cherisher and Nurturer of all living beings. ||15||

column2: anitaye vita(n) anitaye chita(n) anitaye aasaa bahu bidh prakaara(n) ||
column3: Wealth is temporary; conscious existence is temporary; hopes of all sorts are temporary.

column2: anitaye heta(n) aha(n) ba(n)dha(n) bharam maiaa malana(n) bikaara(n) ||
column3: The bonds of love, attachment, egotism, doubt, Maya and the pollution of corruption are temporary.

column2: fira(n)t jon anek jaTharaagan neh simara(n)t maleen budhaye(n) ||
column3: The mortal passes through the fire of the womb of reincarnation countless times. He does not remember the Lord in meditation; his understanding is polluted.

column2: he gobi(n)dh karat miaa naanak patit udhaaran saadh sa(n)gameh ||16||
column3: O Lord of the Universe, when You grant Your Grace, even sinners are saved. Nanak dwells in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy. ||16||

column2: gira(n)t gir patit paataala(n) jala(n)t dhedheepaye baisavaiaa(n)tareh ||
column3: You may drop down from the mountains, and fall into the nether regions of the underworld, or be burnt in the blazing fire,

column2: baha(n)t agaeh toya(n) tara(n)ga(n) dhukha(n)t greh chi(n)taa janama(n) ta maraneh ||
column3: or swept away by the unfathomable waves of water; but the worst pain of all is household anxiety, which is the source of the cycle of death and rebirth.

column2: anik saadhana(n) na sidhayete naanak asatha(n)bha(n) asatha(n)bha(n) asatha(n)bha(n) sabadh saadh savaijaneh ||17||
column3: No matter what you do, you cannot break its bonds, O Nanak. Man's only Support, Anchor and Mainstay is the Word of the Shabad, and the Holy, Friendly Saints. ||17||

column2: ghor dhukhaye(n) anik hataye(n) janam dhaaridhra(n) mahaa bikhayeaadha(n) ||
column3: Excruciating pain, countless killings, reincarnation, poverty and terrible misery

column2: miTa(n)t sagal simara(n)t har naam naanak jaise paavak kaasaT bhasama(n) karot ||18||
column3: are all destroyed by meditating in remembrance on the Lord's Name, O Nanak, just as fire reduces piles of wood to ashes. ||18||

column2: a(n)dhakaar simarat prakaasa(n) gun rama(n)t agh kha(n)ddaneh ||
column3: Meditating in remembrance on the Lord, the darkness is illuminated. Dwelling on His Glorious Praises, the ugly sins are destroyed.

column2: ridh basa(n)t bhai bheet dhooteh karam karat mahaa niramaleh ||
column3: Enshrining the Lord deep within the heart, and with the immaculate karma of doing good deeds, one strikes fear into the demons.

column2: janam maran raha(n)t srotaa sukh samooh amogh dharasaneh ||
column3: The cycle of coming and going in reincarnation is ended, absolute peace is obtained, and the Fruitful Vision of the Lord's Darshan.

column2: saran joga(n) sa(n)t pria naanak so bhagavaan khema(n) karot ||19||
column3: He is Potent to give Protection, He is the Lover of His Saints. O Nanak, the Lord God blesses all with bliss. ||19||

column2: paachha(n) karot agraneeveh niraasa(n) aas pooraneh ||
column3: Those who were left behind - the Lord brings them to the front. He fulfills the hopes of the hopeless.

column2: niradhan bhaya(n) dhanava(n)teh rogeea(n) rog kha(n)ddaneh ||
column3: He makes the poor rich, and cures the illnesses of the ill.

column2: bhagataye(n) bhagat dhaana(n) raam naam gun keerataneh ||
column3: He blesses His devotees with devotion. They sing the Kirtan of the Praises of the Lord's Name.

column2: paarabraham purakh dhaataareh naanak gur sevaa ki(n) na labhayete ||20||
column3: O Nanak, those who serve the Guru find the Supreme Lord God, the Great Giver||20||

column2: adhara(n) dhara(n) dhaaraneh niradhana(n) dhan naam narahareh ||
column3: He gives Support to the unsupported. The Name of the Lord is the Wealth of the poor.

column2: anaath naath gobi(n)dheh balaheen bal kesaveh ||
column3: The Lord of the Universe is the Master of the masterless; the Beautiful-haired Lord is the Power of the weak.

column2: sarab bhoot dhayaal achut dheen baa(n)dhav dhaamodhareh ||
column3: The Lord is Merciful to all beings, Eternal and Unchanging, the Family of the meek and humble.

column2: sarabagaye pooran purakh bhagavaaneh bhagat vachhal karunaa mayeh ||
column3: The All-knowing, Perfect, Primal Lord God is the Lover of His devotees, the Embodiment of Mercy.

column2: ghaT ghaT basa(n)t baasudheveh paarabraham paramesureh ||
column3: The Supreme Lord God, the Transcendent, Luminous Lord, dwells in each and every heart.

column2: jaacha(n)t naanak kirapaal prasaadha(n) neh bisara(n)t neh bisara(n)t naaraineh ||21||
column3: Nanak begs for this blessing from the Merciful Lord, that he may never forget Him, never forget Him. ||21||

column2: neh samaratha(n) neh sevaka(n) neh preet param purakhotama(n) ||
column3: I have no power; I do not serve You, and I do not love You, O Supreme Sublime Lord God.

column2: tav prasaadh simarate naama(n) naanak kirapaal har har gura(n) ||22||
column3: By Your Grace, Nanak meditates on the Naam, the Name of the Merciful Lord, Har, Har. ||22||

column2: bharan pokhan kara(n)t jeeaa bisraam chhaadhan dheva(n)t dhaana(n) ||
column3: The Lord feeds and sustains all living beings; He blesses them gifts of restful peace and fine clothes.

column2: siraja(n)t ratan janam chatur chetaneh ||
column3: He created the jewel of human life, with all its cleverness and intelligence.

column2: varata(n)t sukh aana(n)dh prasaadheh ||
column3: By His Grace, mortals abide in peace and bliss.

column2: simara(n)t naanak har har hare ||
column3: O Nanak, meditating in remembrance on the Lord, Har, Har, Haray,

column2: anitaye rachanaa niramoh te ||23||
column3: the mortal is released from attachment to the world. ||23||

column2: dhaana(n) paraa pooraben bhu(n)cha(n)te maheepate ||
column3: The kings of the earth are eating up the blessings of the good karma of their past lives.

column2: bipareet budhaye(n) maarat lokeh naanak chira(n)kaal dhukh bhogate ||24||
column3: Those cruel-minded rulers who oppress the people, O Nanak, shall suffer in pain for a very long time. ||24||

column2: birathaa anugraha(n) gobi(n)dheh jasaye simaran ridha(n)tareh ||
column3: Those who meditate in remembrance on the Lord in their hearts, look upon even pain as God's Grace.

column2: aarogaye(n) mahaa rogaye(n) bisimrite karunaa mayeh ||25||
column3: The healthy person is very sick, if he does not remember the Lord, the Embodiment of Mercy. ||25||

column2: ramana(n) kevala(n) keeratana(n) sudharama(n) dheh dhaaraneh ||
column3: To sing the Kirtan of God's Praises is the righteous duty incurred by taking birth in this human body.

column2: a(n)mirat naam naarain naanak peevata(n) sa(n)t na tirapayete ||26||
column3: The Naam, the Name of the Lord, is Ambrosial Nectar, O Nanak. The Saints drink it in, and never have enough of it. ||26||

column2: sahan seel sa(n)ta(n) sam mitrasaye dhurajaneh ||
column3: The Saints are tolerant and good-natured; friends and enemies are the same to them.

column2: naanak bhojan anik prakaaren ni(n)dhak aavadh hoi upatisaTate ||27||
column3: O Nanak, it is all the same to them, whether someone offers them all sorts of foods, or slanders them, or draws weapons to kill them. ||27||

column2: tirasakaar neh bhava(n)t neh bhava(n)t maan bha(n)ganeh ||
column3: They pay no attention to dishonor or disrespect.

column2: sobhaa heen neh bhava(n)t neh poha(n)t sa(n)saar dhukhaneh ||
column3: They are not bothered by gossip; the miseries of the world do not touch them.

column2: gobi(n)dh naam japa(n)t mil saadh sa(n)geh naanak se praanee sukh baasaneh ||28||
column3: Those who join the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, and chant the Name of the Lord of the Universe - O Nanak, those mortals abide in peace. ||28||

column2: sainaa saadh samooh soor ajita(n) sa(n)naaha(n) tan ni(n)mrataeh ||
column3: The Holy people are an invincible army of spiritual warriors; their bodies are protected by the armor of humility.

column2: aavadheh gun gobi(n)dh ramana(n) oT gur sabadh kar charamaneh ||
column3: Their weapons are the Glorious Praises of the Lord which they chant; their Shelter and Shield is the Word of the Guru's Shabad.

column2: aarooRate asavai rath naageh bujha(n)te prabh maarageh ||
column3: The horses, chariots and elephants they ride are their way to realize God's Path.

column2: bicharate nirabhaya(n) satr sainaa dhaaya(n)te guopaal keerataneh ||
column3: They walk fearlessly through the armies of their enemies; they attack them with the Kirtan of God's Praises.

column2: jitate bisavai sa(n)saareh naanak vasaye(n) karot pa(n)ch tasakareh ||29||
column3: They conquer the entire world, O Nanak, and overpower the five thieves. ||29||

column2: mirag tirasanaa ga(n)dharab nagara(n) dhrum chhaayaa rach dhuramateh ||
column3: Misled by evil-mindedness, mortals are engrossed in the mirage of the illusory world, like the passing shade of a tree.

column2: tateh kuTa(n)b moh mithayeaa simara(n)t naanak raam raam naameh ||30||
column3: Emotional attachment to family is false, so Nanak meditates in remembrance on the Name of the Lord, Raam, Raam. ||30||

column2: nach bidhiaa nidhaan nigama(n) nach gunagaye naam keerataneh ||
column3: I do not possess the treasure of the wisdom of the Vedas, nor do I possess the merits of the Praises of the Naam.

column2: nach raag ratan ka(n)Tha(n) neh cha(n)chal chatur chaatureh ||
column3: I do not have a beautiful voice to sing jewelled melodies; I am not clever, wise or shrewd.

column2: bhaag udhim labadhaye(n) maiaa naanak saadhasa(n)g khal pa(n)dditeh ||31||
column3: By destiny and hard work, the wealth of Maya is obtained. O Nanak, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, even fools become religious scholars. ||31||

column2: ka(n)Th ramaneey raam raam maalaa hasat uooch prem dhaaranee ||
column3: The mala around my neck is the chanting of the Lord's Name. The Love of the Lord is my silent chanting.

column2: jeeh bhan jo utam salok udharana(n) nain na(n)dhanee ||32||
column3: Chanting this most Sublime Word brings salvation and joy to the eyes. ||32||

column2: gur ma(n)tr heenasaye jo praanee dhiraga(n)t janam bhrasaTaneh ||
column3: That mortal who lacks the Guru's Mantra - cursed and contaminated is his life.

column2: kookareh sookareh garadhabheh kaakeh sarapaneh tul khaleh ||33||
column3: That blockhead is just a dog, a pig, a jackass, a crow, a snake. ||33||

column2: charanaarabi(n)dh bhajana(n) ridhaya(n) naam dhaaraneh ||
column3: Whoever contemplates the Lord's Lotus Feet, and enshrines His Name within the heart,

column2: keeratana(n) saadhasa(n)gen naanak neh dhirasaTa(n)t jamadhootaneh ||34||
column3: and sings the Kirtan of His Praises in the Saadh Sangat, O Nanak, shall never see the Messenger of Death. ||34||

column2: nach dhuralabha(n) dhana(n) roopa(n) nach dhuralabha(n) savairag raajaneh ||
column3: Wealth and beauty are not so difficult to obtain. Paradise and royal power are not so difficult to obtain.

column2: nach dhuralabha(n) bhojana(n) bi(n)jana(n) nach dhuralabha(n) savaichh a(n)bareh ||
column3: Foods and delicacies are not so difficult to obtain. Elegant clothes are not so difficuilt to obtain.

column2: nach dhuralabha(n) sut mitr bhraat baa(n)dhav nach dhuralabha(n) banitaa bilaaseh ||
column3: Children, friends, siblings and relatives are not so difficult to obtain. The pleasures of woman are not so difficult to obtain.

column2: nach dhuralabha(n) bidhiaa prabeena(n) nach dhuralabha(n) chatur cha(n)chaleh ||
column3: Knowledge and wisdom are not so difficult to obtain. Cleverness and trickery are not so difficult to obtain.

column2: dhuralabha(n) ek bhagavaan naameh naanak labadhiye(n) saadhasa(n)g kirapaa prabha(n) ||35||
column3: Only the Naam, the Name of the Lord, is difficult to obtain. O Nanak, it is only obtained by God's Grace, in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy. ||35||

column2: jat kateh tateh dhirasaTa(n) savairag marat payaal lokeh ||
column3: Wherever I look, I see the Lord, whether in this world, in paradise, or the nether regions of the underworld.

column2: sarabatr ramana(n) gobi(n)dheh naanak lep chhep na lipayete ||36||
column3: The Lord of the Universe is All-pervading everywhere. O Nanak, no blame or stain sticks to Him. ||36||

column2: bikhayaa bhaya(n)t a(n)mrita(n) dhrusaTaa(n) sakhaa savaijaneh ||
column3: Poison is transformed into nectar, and enemies into friends and companions.

column2: dhukha(n) bhaya(n)t sukhaye(n) bhai bheeta(n) ta nirabhayeh ||
column3: Pain is changed into pleasure, and the fearful become fearless.

column2: thaan bihoon bisraam naama(n) naanak kirapaal har har gureh ||37||
column3: Those who have no home or place find their place of rest in the Naam, O Nanak, when the Guru, the Lord, becomes Merciful. ||37||

column2: sarab seel mama(n) seela(n) sarab paavan mam paavaneh ||
column3: He blesses all with humility; He has blessed me with humility as well. He purifies all, and He has purified me as well.

column2: sarab karatab mama(n) karataa naanak lep chhep na lipayete ||38||
column3: The Creator of all is the Creator of me as well. O Nanak, no blame or stain sticks to Him. ||38||

column2: neh seetala(n) cha(n)dhr dheveh neh seetala(n) baavan cha(n)dhaneh ||
column3: The moon-god is not cool and calm, nor is the white sandalwood tree.

column2: neh seetala(n) seet ruten naanak seetala(n) saadh savaijaneh ||39||
column3: The winter season is not cool; O Nanak, only the Holy friends, the Saints, are cool and calm. ||39||

column2: ma(n)tra(n) raam raam naama(n) dhayeaana(n) sarabatr pooraneh ||
column3: Through the Mantra of the Name of the Lord, Raam, Raam, one meditates on the All-pervading Lord.

column2: gayeaana(n) sam dhukh sukha(n) jugat niramal niravairaneh ||
column3: Those who have the wisdom to look alike upon pleasure and pain, live the immaculate lifestyle, free of vengeance.

column2: dhayaala(n) sarabatr jeeaa pa(n)ch dhokh bivarajiteh ||
column3: They are kind to all beings; they have overpowered the five thieves.

column2: bhojana(n) gopaal keeratana(n) alap maayaa jal kamal rahateh ||
column3: They take the Kirtan of the Lord's Praise as their food; they remain untouched by Maya, like the lotus in the water.

column2: aupadhesa(n) sam mitr satreh bhagava(n)t bhagat bhaavanee ||
column3: They share the Teachings with friend and enemy alike; they love the devotional worship of God.

column2: par ni(n)dhaa neh srot sravana(n) aap tiyeaag sagal renukeh ||
column3: They do not listen to slander; renouncing self-conceit, they become the dust of all.

column2: khaT lakhayen poorana(n) purakheh naanak naam saadh savaijaneh ||40||
column3: Whoever has these six qualities, O Nanak, is called a Holy friend. ||40||

column2: ajaa bhoga(n)t ka(n)dh moola(n) basa(n)te sameep kehareh ||
column3: The goat enjoys eating fruits and roots, but if it lives near a tiger, it is always anxious.

column2: tatr gate sa(n)saareh naanak sog harakha(n) biaapate ||41||
column3: This is the condition of the world, O Nanak; it is afflicted by pleasure and pain. ||41||

column2: chhala(n) chhidhra(n) koT bighana(n) aparaadha(n) kilabikh mala(n) ||
column3: Fraud, false accusations, millions of diseases, sins and the filthy residues of evil mistakes;

column2: bharam moha(n) maan apamaana(n) madha(n) maayaa biaapita(n) ||
column3: doubt, emotional attachment, pride, dishonor and intoxication with Maya

column2: mritaye janam bhrama(n)t narakeh anik upaava(n) na sidhayete ||
column3: these lead mortals to death and rebirth, wandering lost in hell. In spite of all sorts of efforts, salvation is not found.

column2: niramala(n) saadh sa(n)geh japa(n)t naanak gopaal naama(n) ||
column3: Chanting and meditating on the Name of the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, O Nanak, mortals become immaculate and pure.

column2: rama(n)t gun gobi(n)dh nit prateh ||42||
column3: They continually dwell upon the Glorious Praises of God. ||42||

column2: taran saran suaamee raman seel paramesureh ||
column3: In the Sanctuary of the Kind-hearted Lord, our Transcendent Lord and Master, we are carried across.

column2: karan kaaran samaratheh dhaan dhet prabh pooraneh ||
column3: God is the Perfect, All-powerful Cause of causes; He is the Giver of gifts.

column2: niraas aas karana(n) sagal arath aalayeh ||
column3: He gives hope to the hopeless. He is the Source of all riches.

column2: gun nidhaan simara(n)t naanak sagal jaacha(n)t jaachikeh ||43||
column3: Nanak meditates in remembrance on the Treasure of Virtue; we are all beggars, begging at His Door. ||43||

column2: dhuragam sathaan sugama(n) mahaa dhookh sarab sookhaneh ||
column3: The most difficult place becomes easy, and the worst pain turns into pleasure.

column2: dhurabachan bhedh bharama(n) saakat pisana(n) ta surajaneh ||
column3: Evil words, differences and doubts are obliterated, and even faithless cynics and malicious gossips become good people.

column2: asathita(n) sog harakha(n) bhai kheena(n) ta nirabhaveh ||
column3: They become steady and stable, whether happy or sad; their fears are taken away, and they are fearless.

column2: bhai aTaveea(n) mahaa nagar baasa(n) dharam lakhayen prabh miaa ||

column3: He set out on a journey to meet the Lord, but his consciousness failed him half-way. ||96||

column2: kabeer kaaran bapuraa kiaa karai jau raam na karai sahai ||
column3: Kabeer, what can the poor creature do, if the Lord does not give him assistance?

column2: jeh jeh ddaalee pag dharau soiee mur mur jai ||97||
column3: Whatever branch he steps on breaks and collapses. ||97||

column2: kabeer avareh kau upadhesate mukh mai par hai ret ||
column3: Kabeer, those who only preach to others - sand falls into their mouths.

column2: raas biraanee raakhate khaayaa ghar kaa khet ||98||
column3: They keep their eyes on the property of others, while their own farm is being eaten up. ||98||

column2: kabeer saadhoo kee sa(n)gat rahau jau kee bhoosee khaau ||
column3: Kabeer, I will remain in the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, even if I have only coarse bread to eat.

column2: honahaar so hoihai saakat sa(n)g na jaau ||99||
column3: Whatever will be, will be. I will not associate with the faithless cynics. ||99||

column2: kabeer sa(n)gat saadh kee dhin dhin dhoonaa het ||
column3: Kabeer, in the Saadh Sangat, love for the Lord doubles day by day.

column2: saakat kaaree kaa(n)baree dhoe hoi na set ||100||
column3: The faithless cynic is like a black blanket, which does not become white by being washed. ||100||

column2: kabeer man moo(n)ddiaa nahee kes mu(n)ddaae kaa(n)i ||
column3: Kabeer, you have not shaved your mind, so why do you shave your head?

column2: jo kichh keeaa so man keeaa moo(n)ddaa moo(n)dd ajaa(n)i ||101||
column3: Whatever is done, is done by the mind; it is useless to shave your head. ||101||

column2: kabeer raam na chhoddeeaai tan dhan jai ta jaau ||
column3: Kabeer, do not abandon the Lord; your body and wealth shall go, so let them go.

column2: charan kamal chit bedhiaa raameh naam samaau ||102||
column3: My consciousness is pierced by the Lord's Lotus Feet; I am absorbed in the Name of the Lord. ||102||

column2: kabeer jo ham ja(n)t bajaavate TooT giee(n) sabh taar ||
column3: Kabeer, all the strings of the instrument I played are broken.

column2: ja(n)t bichaaraa kiaa karai chale bajaavanahaar ||103||
column3: What can the poor instrument do, when the player has departed as well. ||103||

column2: kabeer mai moo(n)ddau teh guroo kee jaa te bharam na jai ||
column3: Kabeer, shave the mother of that guru, who does not take away one's doubt.

column2: aap ddube chahu bedh meh chele dhe'ee bahai ||104||
column3: He himself is drowning in the four Vedas; he drowns his disciples as well. ||104||

column2: kabeer jete paap ke'ee raakhe talai dhurai ||
column3: Kabeer, whatever sins the mortal has committed, he tries to keep hidden under cover.

column2: paragaT bhe nidhaan sabh jab poochhe dharam rai ||105||
column3: But in the end, they shall all be revealed, when the Righteous Judge of Dharma investigates. ||105||

column2: kabeer har kaa simaran chhaadd kai paalio bahut kuTa(n)b ||
column3: Kabeer, you have given up meditating on the Lord, and you have raised a large family.

column2: dha(n)dhaa karataa reh giaa bhaiee rahiaa na ba(n)dh ||106||
column3: You continue to involve yourself in worldly affairs, but none of your brothers and relatives remain. ||106||

column2: kabeer har kaa simaran chhaadd kai raat jagaavan jai ||
column3: Kabeer, those who give up meditation on the Lord, and get up at night to wake the spirits of the dead,

column2: sarapan hoi kai aautarai jaae apune khai ||107||
column3: shall be reincarnated as snakes, and eat their own offspring. ||107||

column2: kabeer har kaa simaran chhaadd kai ahoiee raakhai naar ||
column3: Kabeer, the woman who gives up meditation on the Lord, and observes the ritual fast of Ahoi,

column2: gadhahee hoi kai aautarai bhaar sahai man chaar ||108||
column3: shall be reincarnated as a donkey, to carry heavy burdens. ||108||

column2: kabeer chaturaiee at ghanee har jap hiradhai maeh ||
column3: Kabeer, it is the most clever wisdom, to chant and meditate on the Lord in the heart.

column2: sooree uoopar khelanaa girai ta Thaahar naeh ||109||
column3: It is like playing on a pig; if you fall off, you will find no place of rest. ||109||

column2: kabeer suoiee mukh dha(n)n hai jaa mukh kaheeaai raam ||
column3: Kabeer, blessed is that mouth, which utters the Lord's Name.

column2: dhehee kis kee baapuree pavitr hoigo graam ||110||
column3: It purifies the body, and the whole village as well. ||110||

column2: kabeer soiee kul bhalee jaa kul har ko dhaas ||
column3: Kabeer, that family is good, in which the Lord's slave is born.

column2: jeh kul dhaas na uoopajai so kul ddaak palaas ||111||
column3: But that family in which the Lord's slave is not born is as useless as weeds. ||111||

column2: kabeer hai gi baahan saghan ghan laakh dhajaa faharaeh ||
column3: Kabeer, some have lots of horses, elephants and carriages, and thousands of banners waving.

column2: eiaa sukh te bhikhayeaa bhalee jau har simarat dhin jaeh ||112||
column3: But begging is better than these comforts, if one spends his days meditating in remembrance on the Lord. ||112||

column2: kabeer sabh jag hau firio maa(n)dhal ka(n)dh chaddai ||
column3: Kabeer, I have wandered all over the world, carrying the drum on my shoulder.

column2: koiee kaahoo ko nahee sabh dhekhee Thok bajai ||113||
column3: No one belongs to anyone else; I have looked and carefully studied it. ||113||

column2: maarag motee beethare a(n)dhaa nikasio aai ||
column3: The pearls are scattered on the road; the blind man comes along.

column2: jot binaa jagadhees kee jagat ula(n)ghe jai ||114||
column3: Without the Light of the Lord of the Universe, the world just passes them by. ||114||

column2: booddaa ba(n)s kabeer kaa upajio poot kamaal ||
column3: My family is drowned, O Kabeer, since the birth of my son Kamaal.

column2: har kaa simaran chhaadd kai ghar le aayaa maal ||115||
column3: He has given up meditating on the Lord, in order to bring home wealth. ||115||

column2: kabeer saadhoo kau milane jaieeaai saath na leejai koi ||
column3: Kabeer, go out to meet the holy man; do not take anyone else with you.

column2: paachhai paau na dheejeeaai aagai hoi su hoi ||116||
column3: Do not turn back - keep on going. Whatever will be, will be. ||116||

column2: kabeer jag baadhio jeh jevaree teh mat ba(n)dhahu kabeer ||
column3: Kabeer, do not bind yourself with that chain, which binds the whole world.

column2: jaiheh aaTaa lon jiau son samaan sareer ||117||
column3: As the salt is lost in the flour, so shall your golden body be lost. ||117||

column2: kabeer ha(n)s uddio tan gaaddio sojhaiee sainaeh ||
column3: Kabeer, the soul-swan is flying away, and the body is being buried, and still he makes gestures.

column2: ajahoo jeeau na chhoddiee ra(n)kaiee nainaeh ||118||
column3: Even then, the mortal does not give up the cruel look in his eyes. ||118||

column2: kabeer nain nihaarau tujh kau sravan sunau tua naau ||
column3: Kabeer: with my eyes, I see You, Lord; with my ears, I hear Your Name.

column2: bain ucharau tua naam jee charan kamal ridh Thaau ||119||
column3: With my tongue I chant Your Name; I enshrine Your Lotus Feet within my heart. ||119||

column2: kabeer surag narak te mai rahio satigur ke parasaadh ||
column3: Kabeer, I have been spared from heaven and hell, by the Grace of the True Guru.

column2: charan kamal kee mauj meh rahau a(n)t ar aadh ||120||
column3: From beginning to end, I abide in the joy of the Lord's Lotus Feet. ||120||

column2: kabeer charan kamal kee mauj ko keh kaise unamaan ||
column3: Kabeer, how can I even describe the extent of the joy of the Lord's Lotus Feet?

column2: kahibe kau sobhaa nahee dhekhaa hee paravaan ||121||
column3: I cannot describe its sublime glory; it has to be seen to be appreciated. ||121||

column2: kabeer dhekh kai keh kahau kahe na ko pateeaai ||
column3: Kabeer, how can I describe what I have seen? No one will believe my words.

column2: har jaisaa taisaa uhee rahau harakh gun gai ||122||
column3: The Lord is just as He is. I dwell in delight, singing His Glorious Praises. ||122||

column2: kabeer chugai chitaarai bhee chugai chug chug chitaare || jaise bachareh koo(n)j man maiaa mamataa re ||123||
column3: Kabeer, the flamingo pecks and feeds, and remembers her chicks. She pecks and pecks and feeds, and remembers them always. Her chicks are very dear to her, just like the love of wealth and Maya is dear to the mortal's mind. ||123||

column2: kabeer a(n)bar ghanahar chhaiaa barakh bhare sar taal ||
column3: Kabeer, the sky is overcast and cloudy; the ponds and lakes are overflowing with water.

column2: chaatirak jiau tarasat rahai tin ko kaun havaal ||124||
column3: Like the rainbird, some remain thirsty - what is their condition? ||124||

column2: kabeer chakiee jau nis beechhurai aai milai parabhaat ||
column3: Kabeer, the chakvi duck is separated from her love through the night, but in the morning, she meets him again.

column2: jo nar bichhure raam siau naa dhin mile na raat ||125||
column3: Those who are separated from the Lord do not meet Him in the day, or in the night. ||125||

column2: kabeer rainair bichhoriaa rahu re sa(n)kh majhoor ||
column3: Kabeer: O conch shell, remain in the ocean.

column2: dheval dheval dhaahaRee dheseh ugavat soor ||126||
column3: If you are separated from it, you shall scream at sunrise from temple to temple. ||126||

column2: kabeer sootaa kiaa kareh jaag roi bhai dhukh ||
column3: Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Wake up and cry in fear and pain.

column2: jaa kaa baasaa gor meh so kiau sovai sukh ||127||
column3: Those who live in the grave - how can they sleep in peace? ||127||

column2: kabeer sootaa kiaa kareh uTh k na japeh muraar ||
column3: Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Why not rise up and meditate on the Lord?

column2: eik dhin sovan hoigo laa(n)be godd pasaar ||128||
column3: One day you shall sleep with your legs outstretched. ||128||

column2: kabeer sootaa kiaa kareh baiThaa rahu ar jaag ||
column3: Kabeer, what are you doing sleeping? Wake up, and sit up.

column2: jaa ke sa(n)g te beechhuraa taa hee ke sa(n)g laag ||129||
column3: Attach yourself to the One, from whom you have been separated. ||129||

column2: kabeer sa(n)t kee gail na chhoddeeaai maarag laagaa jaau ||
column3: Kabeer, do not leave the Society of the Saints; walk upon this Path.

column2: pekhat hee pu(n)neet hoi bheTat japeeaai naau ||130||
column3: See them, and be sanctified; meet them, and chant the Name. ||130||

column2: kabeer saakat sa(n)g na keejeeaai dhooreh jaieeaai bhaag ||
column3: Kabeer, do not associate with the faithless cynics; run far away from them.

column2: baasan kaaro paraseeaai tau kachh laagai dhaag ||131||
column3: If you touch a vessel stained with soot, some of the soot will stick to you. ||131||

column2: kabeeraa raam na chetio jaraa pahoo(n)chio aai ||
column3: Kabeer, you have not contemplated the Lord, and now old age has overtaken you.

column2: laagee ma(n)dhir dhuaar te ab kiaa kaaddiaa jai ||132||
column3: Now that the door of your mansion is on fire, what can you take out? ||132||

column2: kabeer kaaran so bhio jo keeno karataar ||
column3: Kabeer, the Creator does whatever He pleases.

column2: tis bin dhoosar ko nahee ekai sirajanahaar ||133||
column3: There is none other than Him; He alone is the Creator of all. ||133||

column2: kabeer fal laage falan paakan laage aa(n)b ||
column3: Kabeer, the fruit trees are bearing fruit, and the mangoes are becoming ripe.

column2: jai pahoocheh khasam kau jau beech na khaahee kaa(n)b ||134||
column3: They will reach the owner, only if the crows do not eat them first. ||134||

column2: kabeer Thaakur poojeh mol le manahaTh teerath jaeh ||
column3: Kabeer, some buy idols and worship them; in their stubborn-mindedness, they make pilgrimages to sacred shrines.

column2: dhekhaa dhekhee savaiaa(n)g dhar bhoole bhaTakaa khaeh ||135||
column3: They look at one another, and wear religious robes, but they are deluded and lost. ||135||

column2: kabeer paahan paramesur keeaa poojai sabh sa(n)saar ||
column3: Kabeer, someone sets up a stone idol and all the world worships it as the Lord.

column2: eis bharavaase jo rahe boodde kaalee dhaar ||136||
column3: Those who hold to this belief will be drowned in the river of darkness. ||136||

column2: kabeer kaagadh kee obaree mas ke karam kapaaT ||
column3: Kabeer, the paper is the prison, and the ink of rituals are the bars on the windows.

column2: paahan boree pirathamee pa(n)ddit paaRee baaT ||137||
column3: The stone idols have drowned the world, and the Pandits, the religious scholars, have plundered it on the way. ||137||

column2: kabeer kaal kara(n)taa abeh kar ab karataa sui taal ||
column3: Kabeer, that which you have to do tomorrow - do it today instead; and that which you have to do now - do it immediately!

column2: paachhai kachhoo na hoigaa jau sir par aavai kaal ||138||
column3: Later on, you will not be able to do anything, when death hangs over your head. ||138||

column2: kabeer aaisaa ja(n)t ik dhekhiaa jaisee dhoiee laakh ||
column3: Kabeer, I have seen a person, who is as shiny as washed wax.

column2: dheesai cha(n)chal bahu gunaa mat heenaa naapaak ||139||
column3: He seems very clever and very virtuous, but in reality, he is without understanding, and corrupt. ||139||

column2: kabeer meree budh kau jam na karai tisakaar ||
column3: Kabeer, the Messenger of Death shall not compromise my understanding.

column2: jin ih jamooaa sirajiaa su japiaa paravidhagaar ||140||
column3: I have meditated on the Lord, the Cherisher, who created this Messenger of Death. ||140||

column2: kabeer kasatooree bhiaa bhavar bhe sabh dhaas ||
column3: Kabeer, the Lord is like musk; all His slaves are like bumble bees.

column2: jiau jiau bhagat kabeer kee tiau tiau raam nivaas ||141||
column3: The more Kabeer worships Him, the more the Lord abides within his mind. ||141||

column2: kabeer gahagach pario kuTa(n)b kai kaa(n)Thai reh gio raam ||
column3: Kabeer, the mortal has fallen into the grip of family life, and the Lord has been set aside.

column2: aai pare dharam rai ke beecheh dhoomaa dhaam ||142||
column3: The messengers of the Righteous Judge of Dharma descend upon the mortal, in the midst of all his pomp and ceremony. ||142||

column2: kabeer saakat te sookar bhalaa raakhai aachhaa gaau ||
column3: Kabeer, even a pig is better than the faithless cynic; at least the pig keeps the village clean.

column2: auh saakat bapuraa mar giaa koi na laihai naau ||143||
column3: When the wretched, faithless cynic dies, no one even mentions his name. ||143||

column2: kabeer kauddee kauddee jor kai jore laakh karor ||
column3: Kabeer, the mortal gathers wealth, shell by shell, accumulating thousands and millions.

column2: chalatee baar na kachh milio liee la(n)goTee tor ||144||
column3: But when the time of his departure comes, he takes nothing at all with him. He is even stripped of his loin-cloth. ||144||

column2: kabeer baisano hooaa ta kiaa bhiaa maalaa melee(n) chaar ||
column3: Kabeer, what good is it to become a devotee of Vishnu, and wear four malas?

column2: baahar ka(n)chan baarahaa bheetar bharee bha(n)gaar ||145||
column3: On the outside, he may look like pure gold, but on the inside, he is stuffed with dust. ||145||

column2: kabeer roRaa hoi rahu baaT kaa taj man kaa abhimaan ||
column3: Kabeer, let yourself be a pebble on the path; abandon your egotistical pride.

column2: aaisaa koiee dhaas hoi taeh milai bhagavaan ||146||
column3: Such a humble slave shall meet the Lord God. ||146||

column2: kabeer roRaa hooaa ta kiaa bhiaa pa(n)thee kau dhukh dhei ||
column3: Kabeer, what good would it be, to be a pebble? It would only hurt the traveller on the path.

column2: aaisaa teraa dhaas hai jiau dharanee meh kheh ||147||
column3: Your slave, O Lord, is like the dust of the earth. ||147||

column2: kabeer kheh hooiee tau kiaa bhiaa jau udd laagai a(n)g ||
column3: Kabeer, what then, if one could become dust? It is blown up by the wind, and sticks to the body.

column2: har jan aaisaa chaaheeaai jiau paanee saraba(n)g ||148||
column3: The humble servant of the Lord should be like water, which cleans everything. ||148||

column2: kabeer paanee hooaa ta kiaa bhiaa seeraa taataa hoi ||
column3: Kabeer, what then, if one could become water? It becomes cold, then hot.

column2: har jan aaisaa chaaheeaai jaisaa har hee hoi ||149||
column3: The humble servant of the Lord should be just like the Lord. ||149||

column2: uooch bhavan kanakaamanee sikhar dhajaa faharai ||
column3: The banners wave above the lofty mansions, filled with gold and beautiful women.

column2: taa te bhalee madhookaree sa(n)tasa(n)g gun gai ||150||
column3: But better than these is dry bread, if one sings the Glorious Praises of the Lord in the Society of the Saints. ||150||

column2: kabeer paaTan te uoojar bhalaa raam bhagat jeh Thai ||
column3: Kabeer, the wilderness is better than a city, if the Lord's devotees live there.

column2: raam sanehee baaharaa jam pur mere bhaa(n)i ||151||
column3: Without my Beloved Lord, it is like the City of Death for me. ||151||

column2: kabeer ga(n)g jamun ke a(n)tare sahaj su(n)n ke ghaaT ||
column3: Kabeer, between the Ganges and Jamunaa Rivers, on the shore of Celestial Silence,

column2: tahaa kabeerai maT keeaa khojat mun jan baaT ||152||
column3: there, Kabeer has made his home. The silent sages and the humble servants of the Lord search for the way to get there. ||152||

column2: kabeer jaisee upajee pedd te jau taisee nibahai oR ||
column3: Kabeer, if the mortal continues to love the Lord in the end, as he pledged in the beginning,

column2: heeraa kis kaa baapuraa pujeh na ratan karoR ||153||
column3: no poor diamond, not even millions of jewels, can equal him. ||153||

column2: kabeeraa ek acha(n)bhau dhekhio heeraa haaT bikai ||
column3: Kabeer, I saw a strange and wonderful thing. A jewel was being sold in a store.

column2: banajanahaare baaharaa kauddee badhalai jai ||154||
column3: Because there was no buyer, it was going in exchange for a shell. ||154||

column2: kabeeraa jahaa giaan teh dharam hai jahaa jhooTh teh paap ||
column3: Kabeer, where there is spiritual wisdom, there is righteousness and Dharma. Where there is falsehood, there is sin.

column2: jahaa lobh teh kaal hai jahaa khimaa teh aap ||155||
column3: Where there is greed, there is death. Where there is forgiveness, there is God Himself. ||155||

column2: kabeer maiaa tajee ta kiaa bhiaa jau maan tajiaa nahee jai ||
column3: Kabeer, what good is it to give up Maya, if the mortal does not give up his pride?

column2: maan munee munivar gale maan sabhai kau khai ||156||
column3: Even the silent sages and seers are destroyed by pride; pride eats up everything. ||156||

column2: kabeer saachaa satigur mai miliaa sabadhu ju baahiaa ek ||
column3: Kabeer, the True Guru has met me; He aimed the Arrow of the Shabad at me.

column2: laagat hee bhui mil giaa pariaa kaleje chhek ||157||
column3: As soon as it struck me, I fell to the ground with a hole in my heart. ||157||

column2: kabeer saachaa satigur kiaa karai jau sikhaa meh chook ||
column3: Kabeer, what can the True Guru do, when His Sikhs are at fault?

column2: a(n)dhe ek na laagiee jiau baa(n)s bajaieeaai fook ||158||
column3: The blind do not take in any of His Teachings; it is as useless as blowing into bamboo. ||158||

column2: kabeer hai gai baahan saghan ghan chhatrapatee kee naar ||
column3: Kabeer, the wife of the king has all sorts of horses, elephants and carriages.

column2: taas paTa(n)tar na pujai har jan kee panihaar ||159||
column3: But she is not equal to the water-carrier of the Lord's humble servant. ||159||

column2: kabeer nirap naaree kiau ni(n)dheeaai kiau har cheree kau maan ||
column3: Kabeer, why do you slander the wife of the king? Why do you honor the slave of the Lord?

column2: oh maa(n)g savaarai bikhai kau oh simarai har naam ||160||
column3: Because one combs her hair for corruption, while the other remembers the Name of the Lord. ||160||

column2: kabeer thoonee paiee thit bhiee satigur ba(n)dhee dheer ||
column3: Kabeer, with the Support of the Lord's Pillar, I have become steady and stable.

column2: kabeer heeraa banajiaa maan sarovar teer ||161||
column3: The True Guru has given me courage. Kabeer, I have purchased the diamond, on the banks of the Mansarovar Lake. ||161||

column2: kabeer har heeraa jan jauharee le kai maa(n)ddai haaT ||
column3: Kabeer, the Lord is the Diamond, and the Lord's humble servant is the jeweller who has set up his shop.

column2: jab hee paie'eeh paarakhoo tab heeran kee saaT ||162||
column3: As soon as an appraiser is found, the price of the jewel is set. ||162||

column2: kabeer kaam pare har simareeaai aaisaa simarahu nit ||
column3: Kabeer, you remember the Lord in meditation, only when the need arises. You should remember Him all the time.

column2: amaraa pur baasaa karahu har giaa bahorai bit ||163||
column3: You shall dwell in the city of immortality, and the Lord shall restore the wealth you lost. ||163||

column2: kabeer sevaa kau dhui bhale ek sa(n)t ik raam ||
column3: Kabeer, it is good to perform selfless service for two - the Saints and the Lord.

column2: raamu ju dhaataa mukat ko sa(n)t japaavai naam ||164||
column3: The Lord is the Giver of liberation, and the Saint inspires us to chant the Naam. ||164||

column2: kabeer jeh maarag pa(n)ddit ge paachhai paree baheer ||
column3: Kabeer, the crowds follow the path which the Pandits, the religious scholars, have taken.

column2: eik avaghaT ghaaTee raam kee teh chaR rahio kabeer ||165||
column3: There is a difficult and treacherous cliff on that path to the Lord; Kabeer is climbing that cliff. ||165||

column2: kabeer dhuneeaa ke dhokhe mooaa chaalat kul kee kaan ||
column3: Kabeer, the mortal dies of his worldly troubles and pain, after worrying about his family.

column2: tab kul kis kaa laajasee jab le dhareh masaan ||166||
column3: Whose family is dishonored, when he is placed on the funeral pyre? ||166||

column2: kabeer ddoobahigo re baapure bahu logan kee kaan ||
column3: Kabeer, you shall drown, you wretched being, from worrying about what other people think.

column2: paarosee ke jo hooaa too apane bhee jaan ||167||
column3: You know that whatever happens to your neighbors, will also happen to you. ||167||

column2: kabeer bhalee madhookaree naanaa bidh ko naaj ||
column3: Kabeer, even dry bread, made of various grains, is good.

column2: dhaavaa kaahoo ko nahee baddaa dhes badd raaj ||168||
column3: No one brags about it, throughout the vast country and great empire. ||168||

column2: kabeer dhaavai dhaajhan hot hai niradhaavai rahai nisa(n)k ||
column3: Kabeer, those who brag, shall burn. Those who do not brag remain carefree.

column2: jo jan niradhaavai rahai so ganai i(n)dhr so ra(n)k ||169||
column3: That humble being who does not brag, looks upon the gods and the poor alike. ||169||

column3: Without meeting the Guru, the Lord of the Universe, they are all reduced to dust again. ||179||

column3: Kabeer speaks after careful consideration; hear this, O Saints, in your minds. ||180||

column3: Kabeer, those who do not know anything, pass their lives in peaceful sleep.

column3: But I have understood the riddle; I am faced with all sorts of troubles. ||181||

column3: Kabeer, those who are beaten cry a lot; but the cries of the pain of separation are different.

column3: Struck by the Mystery of God, Kabeer remains silent. ||182||

column3: Kabeer, the stroke of a lance is easy to bear; it takes away the breath.

column3: But one who endures the stroke of the Word of the Shabad is the Guru, and I am his slave. ||183||

column2: ek anekeh mil giaa ek samaanaa ek ||191||
column3: One 'Raam' is pervading everywhere, while the other is contained only in himself. ||191||

column3: Kabeer, those houses in which neither the Holy nor the Lord are served

column3: - those houses are like cremation grounds; demons dwell within them. ||192||

column2: aaTh jaam chausaTh gharee tua nirakhat rahai jeeau ||
column3: Twenty-four hours a day, every hour, my soul continues to look to You, O Lord.

column2: neeche loin kiau karau sabh ghaT dhekhau peeau ||235||

column3: O Lord, there is no end or limit to Your Glorious Virtues; all beings and creatures are Yours. You are the Giver of all, the One Invisible Lord.

column3: He Himself supports the Universe, revealing His All-powerful Creative Potency. He has no color, form, mouth or beard.
