column3: Sorath: My Supplication to Ad(i) Purakh (Primordial Lord), salutation the holy feet of the True Guru (who is the embodiment of the Lord)

column2: ghaT ghaT kaa paraves ek anek bibek sas ||
column3: Like the moon, who though one, resides everywhere and in everyone and yet remains one.

column2: dhoharaa: onam sree satigur charan aadh purakh aadhes ||
column3: Dohra: Salutation in the holy feet of Satguru, the embodiment of glorious Waheguru who is the Primeval Lord.

column2: ek anek bibek sas ghaT ghaT kaa paraves ||
column3: He is like the moon, Who though one is present everywhere and yet remains one.

column2: chha(n)dh: ghaT ghaT kaa paraves ses peh kahat na aavai ||
column3: Channt: Waheguru (Lord) who is all-pervading and whose extent cannot be defined even by Sheshnag (a mythological serpent with thousand heads),

column2: net net keh net bedh ba(n)dheejan gaavai ||
column3: Whose praises Ved, Bhats and aIl others have been singing since eons and yet say-not this, not even this.

column2: aadh madh ar a(n)t hute hut hai pun honam ||
column3: Who was there in the beginning, in between era and will remain in future,

column2: aadh purakh aadhes charan sree satigur onam ||1||
column3: My supplication to Him through the holy feet of the True Guru in which He is totally effulgent. (1)

column2: soraThaa: abigat alakh abhev agam apaar ana(n)t gur ||
column3: Sorath: Eternal, imperceptible, fearless, beyond reach, illimitable, infinite and destroyer of the darkness of ignorance

column2: satigur naanak dhev paarabraham pooran braham ||
column3: Waheguru (Lord) who is transcendental and immanent in the form of Guru Nanak Dev.

column2: dhoharaa: agam apaar ana(n)t gur abigat alakh abhev ||
column3: Dohra: The embodiment of formless God, who is imperishable, beyond description, inaccessible, illimitable, infinite and destroyer of darkness of ignorance.

column2: paarabraham pooran braham satigur naanak dhev ||
column3: Satgur (True Guru) Nanak Dev is the immanent form of God.

column2: chha(n)dh: satigur naanak dhev dhev dhevee sabh dhiaaveh ||
column3: Channt: All gods and goddesses contemplate on the True Guru, Guru Nanak Dev.

column2: naadh baadh bisamaadh raag raagan gun gaaveh ||
column3: They along with minstrels of heaven sing his praises to the accompaniment of musical instruments producing ecstatic music.

column2: su(n)n samaadh agaadh saadh sa(n)gat sapara(n)par ||
column3: Saints and holy men in his company (Guru Nanak) go in deep meditation and state of nothingness,

column2: abigat alakh abhev agam agamit apara(n)par ||2||
column3: And get absorbed in the eternal, imperceptible, infinite, fearless, and inaccessible Lord (Satguru). (2)

column2: soraThaa: jagamag jot saroop param jot mil jot meh ||
column3: Sorath: The light eternal of Guru Nanak Dev melded into the light of Guru Angad Dev who acquired effulgence like the former.

column2: adhabhut ateh anoop param tat tateh milio ||
column3: With the light of Guru Nanak merging with that of Guru Angad Dev Ji, the latter became wondrous in form and beyond words of praise.

column2: dhoharaa: param jot mil jot meh jagamag jot saroop ||
column3: Dohra: Light supreme (Guru Nanak Dev Ji) merged in Guru Angad Dev's light who himself became light divine.

column2: param tat tateh milio adhabhut ateh anoop ||
column3: Truth of Guru Nanak merged with the essence of Guru Angad transforming him into astonishing form.

column2: chha(n)dh: adhabhut ateh anoop roop paaras kai paaras ||
column3: Channt: Guru Angad coming in contact with Guru Nanak the philosopher-stone, became a philosopher-stone himself. His form too became wondrous.

column2: gur a(n)gadh mil a(n)g sa(n)g mil sa(n)g udhaaras ||
column3: Becoming inseparable from Guru Nanak, Lehna Ji became Guru Angad and then whosoever came in touch with him (Guru Angad) was liberated.

column2: akal kalaa bharapoor sootr gat ot pot meh ||
column3: Guru Angad Ji integrated himself like warp and weft with Guru Nanak, the possessor of Divine power of the Lord.

column2: jagamag jot saroop jot mil jot jot meh ||3||
column3: Light merged with light so much that whosoever came in contact with light embodiment (Guru Angad) , became resplendent too. (3)

column2: soraThaa: a(n)mirat dhirasaT nivaas a(n)mirat bachan anahadh sabadh ||
column3: Sorath: In the divine glimpse of Guru Amar Das dwells the elixir of life. (On whomsoever he casts his look, he makes him immortal). His elixir-like words are like unstruck music.

column2: satigur amar pragaas mil a(n)mirat a(n)mirat bhe ||
column3: Resplendent True Guru Amar Das Ji became elixir-like after meeting Guru Angad Dev Ji. He now makes others calm and mortal.

column2: dhoharaa: a(n)mirat bachan anahadh sabadh a(n)mirat dhirasaT nivaas ||
column3: Dohra: Meditating on unstruck melodious Divine Word, the sight and utterances of Guru Amar Das Ji, started showering elixir of life.

column2: mil a(n)mirat a(n)mirat bhe satigur amar pragaas ||
column3: Meeting Guru Angad Dev Ji, elixir-like cool, tranquil and granter of emancipation, Satgur Amar Das too became the same.

column2: chha(n)dh: satigur amar pragaas taas charanaamirat paavai ||
column3: Channt: Satgur Amar Das Ji who is light refulgent, whosoever partakes nectar-like wash of his feet,

column2: kaam naam nihakaam param padh sahaj samaavai ||
column3: Becomes free from all desires is absorbed in high state of spirituality and equipoise.

column2: gurmukh sa(n)dh suga(n)dh saadh sa(n)gat nij aasan ||
column3: By the fragrance of Naam Simran of Guru Amar Das Ji, the Guru's obedient seeker finds stability in the company of holy men and Lord's devotees

column2: a(n)mirat dhirasaT nivaas a(n)mirat mukh bachan pragaasan ||4||
column3: In the elixir-like vision of Guru Amar Das lies the nectar of life and his words provide elixir-like luminance of Naam of the Lord. (4)

column2: soraThaa: brahamaasan bisraam gur bhe gurmukh sa(n)dh mil ||
column3: Sorath: Satguru who resides in Waheguru (Brahm), meeting such Guru-conscious person (Guru Amar Das), and becoming one with him he too acquired all traits of Guru.

column2: gurmukh ramataa raam raam naam gurmukh bhe ||
column3: Through the blessings of Naam Simran of the principal Guru Satguru (Amar Das Ji), Guru Ram Das Ji too became prime Guru.

column2: dheharaa: gur bhe gurmukh sa(n)idh mil brahamaasan bisraam ||
column3: Dohra: In the association of prime Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji) he too became Guru and found refuge in the holy feet of the Lord.

column2: raam naam gurmukh bhe gurmukh ramataa raam ||
column3: The Guru-conscious person whose name is Ram Das, by perpetual meditation on Lord's name, became Guru-oriented and virtuous (Satguru)

column2: chha(n)dh: gurmukh ramataa raam naam gurmukh pragaTaio ||
column3: Channt: Through God-conscious Guru Amar Das Ji and by the blessing of meditation on His name, the virtuous Ram Das emerged as Guru Ram Das (slave of the Lord).

column2: sabadh surat gur giaan dhiaan gur guroo kahaio ||
column3: Because of knowledge of Guru Shabad and consciously uniting with Him, Guru Ram Das became known as principal Guru.

column2: dheep jot mil dheep jot jagamag a(n)tar ur ||
column3: The flame of a beacon lights up another lamp.

column2: gurmukh ramataa raam sa(n)dh gurmukh mil bhe gur ||5||
column3: Thus Guru Ram Das became principal Guru through the blessings of Simran of Lord's name and his association with Guru Amar Das Ji. (5)

column2: soraThaa: aadh a(n)t bisamaadh fal dhraum gur sikh sa(n)dh gat ||
column3: Sorath: Just as the puzzle of seed and tree as to who came first is strange and perplexing, similarly strange is understanding the meeting of Guru and Sikh.

column2: aadh param paramaadh a(n)t ana(n)t na jaaneeaai ||
column3: This mystery of the beginning and end is beyond comprehension. Lord is beyond, away and infinite.

column2: dhoharaa: fal dhraum gur sikh sa(n)dh gat aadh a(n)t bisamaadh ||
column3: Dohra: Guru Ram Das caused the meeting of Guru and Sikh in the same wondrous way of fruit and tree.

column2: a(n)t ana(n)t na jaaneeaai aadh param paramaadh ||
column3: That perspective is infinite and no one can understand it. It is beyond, away and still away out of the reach of mortals.

column2: chha(n)dh: aadh param paramaadh naadh mil naadh sabadh dhun ||
column3: Channt: Just as the sound of musical instruments melds with the words (of song/hymns), similarly Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan became indistinguishable.

column2: salileh salil samai naadh saritaa saagar sun ||
column3: Just as the river water becomes inseparable from the water of the ocean, Guru Arjan became one with Guru Amar Das by engrossing himself in his precepts and following them obediently.

column2: narapat sut nirap hot jot gurmukh gun garajan ||
column3: Just as son of a king becomes king, similarly Guru Arjan born as son to Guru Ram Das became an enlightened soul by singing the eulogies of Lord-a boon blessed to him by Satguru.

column2: raam naam parasaadh bhe gur te gur arajan ||6||
column3: By the grace of Guru Ram Das, Arjan Dev succeeded him as Guru Arjan Dev.

column2: soraThaa: pooran braham bibek aapaa aap pragaas hui ||
column3: Sorath: Being supreme conscious and knowledgeable; it seems God Himself has descended as light divine in the form of Guru Hargobind.

column2: naam dhoi prabh ek gur gobi(n)dh bakhaaneeaai ||
column3: One may hold them (Guru Hargobind) and Gobind different due to their names, but in reality, God Himself has appeared in the form of Hargobind.

column2: dhoharaa: aapaa aap pragaas hoi pooran braham bibek ||
column3: Dohra: Guru Hargobind the enlightened is manifest of Lord. He is granter of spiritual knowledge.

column2: gur gobi(n)dh bakhaaneeaai naam dhoi prabh ek ||
column3: Guru and Gobind are just two separate names, but in reality it is Lord Himself who is manifest.

column2: chha(n)dh: naam dhoi prabh ek Tek gurmukh Thaharaiee ||
column3: Channt: Guru and Gobind though are two different names, in reality He himself is refulgent

column2: aadh bhe gur naam dhuteea gobi(n)dh baddaiee ||
column3: Sikhs ever in attendance of Guru has this strong belief that, first He was called Guru Arjan and then he gave this honour of Guruship to Hargobind.

column2: har gur har gobi(n)dh rachan rach thaap uthaapan ||
column3: God Lord is Guru Arjan Himself and then He Himself became Hargobind.

column2: pooran braham bibek pragaT hui aapaa aapan ||7||
column3: The Omnipotent Lord who created the cosmos, established it and has singular authority of destroying it; it seems He Himself has taken the form of Hargobind to reveal all knowledge about Himself. (7)

column2: soraThaa: bisamaadheh bisamaadh asacharajeh asacharaj gat || aadh purakh paramaadh adhabhut paramadhabhut bhe ||
column3: Sorath: God-manifest Satguru's play is ecstatic and blissful, astonishing beyond astonishment, unimaginably wondrous, and amazing beyond perception.

column2: dhoharaa: asacharajeh asacharaj gat bisamaadheh bisamaadh || adhabhut paramadhabhut bhe aadh purakh paramaadh ||
column3: Dohra: (Describing the essence of the Guru), we have reached the high stage of magnificence and ecstaticisim. I have reached this stage of transcendence by seeing the magnificence of the Lord, who is the beginning of the cosmos and beyond.

column2: chha(n)dh: aadh purakh paramaadh savaiaadh ras ga(n)dh agochar ||
column3: Channt: Primordial Lord (God) has no beginning. He is beyond and still farther. He is free of such mundane worldly pleasures like taste, desires and fragrances.

column2: dhirasaT dharas asaparas surat mat sabadh manochar ||
column3: He is beyond vision, touch, reach of mind, intelligence and words.

column2: log bedh gat giaan lakhe nahee alakh abhevaa ||
column3: The imperceptible and unattached Lord cannot be known by study of Vedas and through other earthly knowledge.

column2: net net kar namo namo nam satigur dhevaa ||8||
column3: Satguru who is embodiment of Lord and inhabits His divine radiance is infinite. Thus, he is worthy of salutation and obeisance in all the three times-past, present and future. (8)

column2: dharasan dhekhat hee sudh kee na sudh rahee budh kee na budh rahee mat mai na mat hai ||
column3: A glimpse of (Satguru) left me bereft of all my consciousness, senses, intelligence, cleverness and all other considered wisdom of the world.

column2: surat mai na suratiaau dhayaan mai(n) na dhayaan rahayo gayaan mai na gayaan rahayo gat mai na gat hai ||
column3: I lost my awareness, attachment of mind with insignificant matters, desires to acquire base or futile ego inflating knowledge and other worldly predicaments.

column2: dheeraj ko dheeraj garab ko garab gayo rat mai na rat rahee pat rat pat hai ||
column3: My patience was lost and so was my vanity. There was no life in me and I was bereft of my existence even.

column2: adhabhut paramadhabhut bisamai bisam asacharajai asacharaj at at hai ||25||
column3: The glimpse of Satguru is capable of amazing one with wondrous feelings. These are astonishing and marvellous and there is no end to this amazement. (9)

column2: dhasam sathaan ke samaan kauan bhauan kaho gurmukh paavai su te anat na paaviee ||
column3: What other place of mystic abode can I say than the tenth concealed opening of a human being? Only the Guru conscious person can reach it by the grace of True Guru by meditating on His name.

column2: aunamanee jot paTa(n)tar dheejai kauan jot dhayaa kai dhikhaavai jaahee taahee ban aaviee ||
column3: What light can be equated with the radiance one receives at the time of spiritual enlightenment?

column2: anahadh naadh samasar naadh baadh kauan sree guroo sunaavai jaeh soiee liv laaviee ||
column3: What melodious musical sound can be equal to the melodious unstruck musical sound of divine word?

column2: nijhar apaar dhaar tul na a(n)mirat ras apiau peeaavai jaeh taahee mai samaaviee ||2||
column3: There is no other elixir capable of making one immortal than the one that flows perpetually in the concealed opening (Dasam Duar) of a human being. And one who is blessed by the True Guru (Satguru) to receive this elixir of immortality obtains it by His grace. (10)

column2: gur sikh sa(n)dh mile bees ik iees iees it te ula(n)gh ut jai Thaharaaviee ||
column3: Meeting with Guru, a Sikh receives the Lord's word to meditate upon and by his untiring and resolute efforts become one with Him. He frees himself from the worldly matters and lives in harmony in the realm of the Lord.

column2: charam dhirasaT moo(n)dh pekhai dhib dhirasaT kai jagamag jot ounamanee sudh paaviee ||
column3: He shuts his eyes from mundane worldly attractions and lives in the spiritual wisdom that helps him feel His presence in everything.

column2: surat sa(n)kochat hee bajar kapaaT khol naadh baadh parai anahat liv laaviee ||
column3: Weaning his thoughts away from the worldly attractions, his doors of ignorance are opened; he is distracted from all sources of worldly pleasures and he gets engrossed in listening to celestial songs and music.

column2: bachan bisarajit an ras rahit hui nijhar apaar dhaar apiau peeaaviee ||11||
column3: Renouncing the worldly matters and shedding all attachment with worldly pleasures, he drinks deep the elixir that flows continuously in his (Dasam Duar) the celestial door of the body. (11)

column2: jau lau an ras bas tau lau nahee prem ras jau lau aan dhiaan aap aap nahee dhekheeaai ||
column3: So long a human being remains absorbed in worldly attractions and pleasures, he cannot know love. So long his attention is focused on something else, he cannot realize self.

column3: God in His immanent form as Satguru who is beyond all castes, creed and race make the Sikhs realise the true form of God.

column3: The heart piercing melodious tune which Satguru sings to his Sikhs is in fact manifestation of True Lord.

column3: Satguru, manifestation of Almighty God, is like jasmine creeper of which He Himself is the root and all His devotees and pious persons are its leaves and branches.

column3: Pleased at the services of His devotees (like Bhai Lehna Ji, Baba Amar Das Ji, etc.) Satguru turns those devotees by His grace and makes them into fragrance-spreading flowers and by manifesting in them is liberating the world.

Those engrossed in material world are converted into God-loving and godly persons. They are detached from maya (mammon) and united with the Almighty. (37)

column2: pooran braham gur birakh bithaar dhaar mool kha(n)dh saakhaa patr anik prakaar hai ||
column3: Satguru, a total form of complete Lord is like a fragrant tree, whose spread has many branches, leaves, flowers in the form of Sikhs.

column3: By the strenuous toil of devoted Sikhs like Bhai Lehna Ji and Baba Amar Das Ji, the True Guru illuminated His own light in them. Engulfed in the desire of worship and fragrance of the Lord, these pious souls are keen to spread and distribute the elixir-like Naam.

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh ras rasik hui chaakhe charanaamirat sa(n)saar ko udhaar hai ||
column3: Such Gursikhs enjoying the fragrance of the dust of Lord's lotus-feet emancipate others from the world.

column2: gurmukh maarag mahaatam akath kathaa net net net namo namo namasakaar hai ||38||
column3: The glory of the path of Sikhism cannot be described. All that we can say is that He is infinite, infinite and beyond and is worthy of our salutes myriad times. (38)

column3: Similarly the Guru-conscious person (Gurmukh) renounces various worldly pleasures and adopts one colour of the formless God. And because of the blessings of his Guru who has taught him to unite with the divine word and his mind, he achieves higher spiritual state. (39)

column3: In the darkness of the night, many stars shine but during the day, the light of one Sun alone is considered authentic.

column2: logan mai logaachaar gurmukh eka(n)kaar sabadh surat unaman unamaaneeaai ||40||
column3: Similarly a Sikh who lives life according to the advice of his Guru becomes divine in all respects, even when he is living life as a worldly person. Due to the lodging of the divine word in his mind, he is known to be living in heavenly state. (40)

column3: Just as a daughter-in-law covers herself with veil in front of the elders of the house, but keeps no distance from her husband at the time of sharing his bed;

column3: Just as a son avoids talking to his wife in front of his parents, but when alone showers all his love upon her,

column2: logan mai logaachaar gurmukh eka(n)kaar sabadh surat unaman man heea sai ||41||
column3: Similarly a devoted Sikh appears worldly among others but having attached his mind with Guru's word, he rises spiritually and realises the Lord. Quintessence: One may maintain oneself as a worldly person outwardly but inwardly one keeps oneself attached with Naam and attains divine bliss. (41)

column3: Those following the path of Gyan (knowledge) keep their mind focused on contemplation while those in contemplation are wandering for Gyan. But the state of a person treading the path of his Guru is above those persons who are pursuing Gyan or Dhyan (contemplation).

column2: prem kai bhagat ar bhagat kai prem nem alakh bhagat prem gurmukh reet hai ||
column3: Followers of path of love yearn for devotion and those on path of devotion desire love, but the innate desire of Guru-conscious person is to remain engrossed in loving worship of God.

column3: By meditating on Gur Shabad (Guru's Word) and taking its refuge, Guru's precepts are revealed to him. When he reaches the state of listening to unstruck melody of the divine word, he enjoys the bliss of higher state of equipoise.

column3: Concentrating on the knowledge of the True Guru, listening to his counsel, practicing contemplation and living life according to His command, a feeling of love grows and blossoms. column3: As the bumble bee attains the divine bliss by drinking the elixir and getting shut in the box-like petals of a lotus flower, similarly in order to provide spiritual peace to his life, a true seeker enjoins the lotus-like feet of Guru and drinks deep by contemplating on Naam. (43)

column3: They remain engrossed in the words of the Guru and the tune of these words remain lodged in their consciousness. But the knowledge of word and consciousness is beyond reach.

column3: By following the teachings of the True Guru and moulding one's character in accordance with the contemplation of Lord's qualities, a sense of love develops. The well defined routine of Guru's philosophy, leads one to free oneself from the worldly shackles.

column3: A Guru-conscious person feels like a mighty king when he is able to concentrate his mind on words and acts as per the teachings of Gum. When he is able to rest in a state of equipoise, he feels like an emperor of infallible kingdom.

column3: By imbibing the five virtues of Truth, Contentment, Compassion, Righteousness and Purpose in accordance with the teachings of the Gum, he becomes acceptable and an honourable person.

column3: By practicing on Naam, a Guru-conscious person lives in a state of equipoise. Any description of that state is beyond our comprehension. It is indescribable. By dint of that state, he becomes aware of all that is happening in every nook and corner of the world.

column3: Because of the refuge of True Guru and moulding his mind, words and actions as per His teachings, a Guru-conscious person learns the happenings of the three worlds innately. He recognises the true Lord residing within.

column3: Thus union of a disciple with Guru imbibes the trait of service of the Master. He serves all without reward or desire as he has learnt that he is serving Him who resides in all.

column3: And when he establishes his relationship with Him, he realises through the medium of meditation on His name that Formless Lord has manifested Himself in various forms and shapes.

column3: The union of a devoted Sikh with True Guru renders him with an attitude of service and benevolence and he yearns to be available at His service. He then develops character of loving devotion and divine reflection.

column3: The state of union of a God-conscious person and his True Guru is glorious and full of astonishment. No other state can equal it. He is worthy of salutation infinite time, again and again. (51)

column3: By concentrating mind in his philosophy and attaching the mind in Naam Simran, one realises the omnipresent Lord in the entire expanse created by Him.

column2: niragun saragun kusamaavalee suga(n)dh sa(n)dh ek aau anek roop ga(n)mitaa agam hai ||
column3: One Transcendental Lord is appearing in countless immanent forms. Like the fragrance of a flower bed, He, the inaccessible can be realised and felt.

column2: paramadhabhut asacharajai asacharaj mai akath kathaa alakh bisamai bisam hai ||81||
column3: The precept and philosophy of the True Guru is utmost admirable. It is most astonishing and beyond description. He is beyond understanding and stranger than the strangest. (81)

column2: satigur dharas dhiaan giaan a(n)jam kai mitr satrataa nivaaree pooran braham hai ||
column3: By concentrating mind on the vision and by toiling on Naam Simran with rapt attention, one destroys all enmity and friendship and experiences presence of One Lord God.

column2: gur upadhes paraves aadh kau aadhes usatat ni(n)dhaa meT ga(n)mitaa agam hai ||
column3: By imbibing the words of the Guru in one's heart and by the counsel of the True Guru can one indulge in His praise humbly. All desires of praise and slander are destroyed and one reaches the inaccessible Lord.

column2: charan saran gahe dhaavat baraj raakhe aasaa manasaa thakat safal janam hai ||
column3: By taking the refuge of a True Guru, a mind chasing vices and other evil pleasures come to rest. All desires and expectations end. Thus a human birth becomes a success.

column2: saadh sa(n)g prem nem jeevan mukat gat kaam nihakaam nihakaram karam hai ||82||
column3: Through joining the congregation of the Guru (Sadh Sangat), one reaches the state of emancipation while alive (Jeevan Mukt). One feels unaffected by worldly desires and instead focusses on Simran and Seva without desire for any reward. (82)

column2: satigur dhev sev alakh abhev gat saavadhaan saadh sa(n)g simaran maatr kai ||
column3: Keeping company of holy persons wakefully, serving the effulgent True Guru and practicing continuous Naam Simran the indescribable and incomprehensible Lord is perceived.

column2: patit puneet reet paaras karai manoor baas mai(n) subaas dhai kupaatreh supaatr kai ||
column3: In the true tradition of converting sinners into pious individuals, by the sermon of Naam Simran, a True Guru changes the iron slag-like base persons into gold/philosopher-stone. And by instilling the fragrance of Naam Simran in the bamboo-like arrogant individuals, he makes them superior persons.

column2: patit puneet kar paavan pavitr keene paaras manoor baas baasai dhrum jaatr kai ||
column3: He who is made noble by Guru, strives to make others noble. Focusing on Naam, an iron-like person is made into gold or a philosopher's stone. A bamboo-like arrogant person becomes humble and acquires a fragrance that spreads to others.

column2: saritaa samu(n)dhr saadh sa(n)g tirakhaava(n)t jeea kirapaa jal dheejai moh ka(n)Th chhedh chaatrakai ||83||
column3: The company of holy and True Guru is like rivers and lakes from where his disciples drink the elixir of Naam and quench their thirst. I, an unfortunate person am still thirsty because I am full of ill traits and vices. Please be clement on me and grant me the boon of Naam Simran. (83)

column2: bees ke baratamaan bhe na subaas baa(n)s hem na bhe manoor log bedh giaan hai ||
column3: Practically, bamboo cannot acquire fragnance and iron cannot become gold. However, through the Guru, a bamboo-like arrogant person can acquire the fragnance of virtues and a vice ridden person (dirty like iron) can become pious and shine like gold.

column2: gurmukh pa(n)th ik iees ko baratamaan cha(n)dhan subaas baa(n)s baasai dhuram aan hai ||
column3: The path of Sikhism is a path of One God. The sandalwood like True Guru blesses a bamboo-like arrogant person with humility and Naam making him full of virtuous qualities. His dedication to Naam Simran instills fragrance into other similar persons.

column2: ka(n)chan manoor hoi paaras paras bheT paaras manoor karai aaur Thaur maan hai ||
column3: Vice laden iron waste-like person becomes philosopher-stone by touching Paaras (philosopher stone) like True Guru. The True Guru converts the wasted person into gold like virtuous. He earns respect everywhere.

column2: gursikh saadh sa(n)g patit puneet reet  gursikh sa(n)dh mile gursikh jaan hai ||84||
column3: The congregation of holy and true disciples of a True Guru is capable of making the sinners into pious persons. One who joins the congregation of true Sikhs of Satguru is also known as Guru's disciple. (84)

column2: charan saran gur bhiee nihachal mat man unaman liv sahaj samaae hai ||
column3: In the refuge of Satguru the intellect becomes stable. The mind attaches itself with state divine and rests in equipoise.

column2: dhirasaT dharas ar sabadh surat mil paramadhabhut prem nem upajaae hai ||
column3: With the mind engrossing into the teachings of Satguru and divine word residing for ever in the memory, astonishing loving devotion is generated.

column2: gur sikh saadh sa(n)g ra(n)g hui ta(n)bol ras paaras paras dhaat ka(n)chan dhikhaae hai ||
column3: In the company of devoted Sikhs, one gets dyed in the color of the Lord; they give their fragrance like a betel leaf and as metal can become gold when touched with the Philosophers-stone; so becomes the state of devoted Sikhs.

column2: cha(n)dhan suga(n)dh sa(n)dh baasanaa subaas taas akath kathaa binodh kahat na aae hai ||85||
column3: The touch of the Holy Feet, a glimpse of the True Guru, passes on fragrance like the sandalwood, which makes other trees equally fragrant. This state of ecstasy is beyond words. (85)

column2: prem ras a(n)mirat nidhaan paan pooran hui akath kathaa binodh kahat na aae hai ||
column3: The union between Guru and Sikh is full of pleasure and happiness. It cannot be described. By the strenuous practice of meditation on the Guru blessed Naam and by relishing the elixir of love, a Sikh feels totally satiated.

column2: giaan dhiaan siaan simaran bisimaran kai bisam bidheh bisamaadh bisamaae hai ||
column3: Forgetting the worldly boasts of knowledge, involvements, wisdoms and other achievements, practicing the Simran strenuously, a Sikh loses the awareness of his existence and he merges in the astonishing of astonishing state.

column2: aadh paramaadh ar a(n)t kai ana(n)t bhe thaeh kai athaeh na apaar paar paae hai ||
column3: By reaching the high divine state and becoming one with the Lord who is beyond the beginning, and even the eons, a Sikh goes beyond the beginning and end. He becomes unfathomable and because of his oneness with Him, his extent cannot be comprehended.

column2: gur sikh sa(n)dh mile bees ik iees iees soha(n) soiee dheepak sai dheepak jagai hai ||86||
column3: This union of Guru and Sikh surely makes a Sikh like God Himself. This union makes him dwell in His name. He perpetually utters-Thou! Thou! Lord! Lord! and he enlightens the beacon of Naam. (86)

column2: satigur charan saran chal jai sikh charan saran taa(n) kee jagat chal aaviee||
column3: A Sikh who devotedly goes to the refuge of a True Guru, has the whole world falling at his feet.

column2: satigur aagayaa satay satay kar maanai sikhay aagayaa taeh sagal sa(n)saar hitaaviee ||
column3: A Sikh of the Guru who abides by the command of his Guru, accepting it to be true; his command is loved by the whole world.

column2: satigur sevaa bhai praan poojaa karai sikh sarab nidhaan agrabhaag liv laaviee ||
column3: A Sikh of the Guru who serves his Guru with loving devotion at the cost of his life considering such service as worship, all the treasures are mute attendant before him.

column2: satigur seekhayaa dheekhayaa hiradhai praves jaah|| taa kee seekh sunat param padh paaviee ||87||
column3: A Sikh of the Guru who has the teachings and consecration of his Guru in his heart, listening to his teachings/sermons one can reach supreme spiritual state. (87)

column2: gursikh saadh sa(n)g ra(n)g ma(n)ai ra(n)geele bhe baaranee biga(n)dh ga(n)g sa(n)g mile ga(n)g hai ||
column3: As evil smelling wine when poured into river Ganges become like the water of Ganges, so can vice ridden, maya (mammon) immersed, worldly pleasure seeking individuals get dyed in the hue of Naam Simran when they join the true, Naam immersed holy company of devoted Sikhs.

column2: surasaree sa(n)gam haivai prabal pravaeh liv saagar athaeh satigur sa(n)g sa(n)g hai ||
column3: As the rapid flow of brooks and rivers like Ganges merges into the vast ocean losing all their destructive traits, so can one get absorbed into the ocean like Satguru by keeping the company of true, loving and devoted Sikhs.

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh nihachal chit dharasan sobhaa nidh lahar tara(n)g hai ||
column3: The mind stabilises in the fragrant dust of Satguru’s feet. The glimpse of infinite praise, myriad colourful waves of Naam appear in his consciousness.

column2: anahadh sabadh kai sarab nidhaan dhaanoo gayaan a(n)s ha(n)s gat sumat sraba(n)g hai ||88||
column3: By virtue of Naam Simran and appearance of unstruck music in the consciousness, a Sikh feels he has been blessed with all the treasures of the world. He acquires knowledge of the True Guru that reflects in every hair of his body. (88)

column2: gurmukh maarag hui dhubidhaa bharam khoe charan saran gahe nij ghar aae hai ||
column3: Entering the path of Sikhism destroys suspicions and separatism and by the support of Satguru, one realises self.

column2: dharas dharas dhib dhirasaT pragaas bhiee a(n)mirat kaTaachh kai amar padh paae hai ||
column3: By the glimpse of Satguru, one is blessed with a vision that enables one see the Lord all around oneself. By the clement look of Satguru, one achieves eternal position.

column2: sabadh surat anahadh nijhar jharan simaran ma(n)tr liv unaman chhaae hai ||
column3: By the union of word and consciousness and by virtue of the sweet tune of Naam, a perpetual flow of divine elixir starts flowing. By continuous repetition of Guru-given incantation, higher spiritual state is achieved.

column2: man bach kram hui ikatr gurmukh sukh prem nem bisam bisavaiaas upajaae hai ||89||
column3: A Guru-conscious person attains real spiritual comfort and peace by bringing in harmony between mind, words and deeds. That unique tradition of Lord's love breeds a wonderful confidence and faith in his mind. (89)

column2: gurmukh aapaa khoi jeevan mukat gat bisam bidheh geh samat subhaau hai ||
column3: The Sikh follower of Guru loses his self and achieves salvation in his life when still alive. Leading a house holder’s life, he feels no concern for distress or peace/comfort that comes his way.

column2: janam maran sam narak surag ar pa(n)un paap sa(n)pat bipat chi(n)taa chaau hai ||
column3: And then birth and death, sin and piety, heaven and hell, pleasures and tribulations, worry and happiness all means equal to him.

column2: ban greh jog bhog log bedh giaan dhiaan dhukh sukh sogaana(n)dh mitr satr taau hai ||
column3: For such a Guru-conscious person, jungle and home, enjoyment and renunciation, folk traditions and traditions of the scriptures, knowledge and contemplation, peace and distress, sorrow and pleasure, friendship and enmity are all the same.

column2: losaT kanik bikh a(n)mirat agan jal sahaj samaadh unaman anuraau hai ||90||
column3: A lump of earth or gold, poison and nectar, water and fire are all the same for a Guru-conscious person. Because, his love is to remain absorbed in the stable state of perpetual knowledge of the Guru. (90)

column2: safal janam gurmukh hui janam jeetio charan safal gur maarag ravan kai ||
column3: A human life is usefully spent when one leads it as an obedient Sikh of the True Guru and wins all its benefits. The feet are successful if they tread the path defined by the Guru.

column2: lochan safal gur dharasaa valokan kai masatak safal raj padh gavan kai ||
column3: The eyes are successful if they accept the omnipresence of the Lord and see Him everywhere. The forehead is successful if it touches the dust of the path tread by Satguru.

column2: hasat safal nam satagur baanee likhe surat safal gur sabadh sravan kai ||
column3: The hands are successful if they are raised in the salutation of Satguru and to write his utterances/compositions. The ears become successful by listening to the glory, adulations of the Lord and words of the Guru.

column2: sa(n)gat safal gursikh saadh sa(n)gam kai prem nem ga(n)mitaa tirakaal tirabhavan kai ||91||
column3: The congregation of holy and true souls attended by a Sikh is useful as it helps in uniting with the Lord. Thus abiding by the tradition of Naam Simran, he becomes aware of all the three worlds and the three periods. (91)

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh ras lubhit hui sahaj samaadh sukh sa(n)paT samaane hai ||
column3: By becoming a true servant of Satguru Ji, remaining fond of the fragrance of the dust of the holy feet of the True Guru, and in perpetual contemplation, a Sikh permeates himself in the spiritual peace.

column2: bhaijal bhiaanak lahar na biaap sakai dhubidhaa nivaar ek Tek Thaharaane hai ||
column3: Guru-conscious person is never affected by the frightening worldly waves of desires and hopes. He is deemed to have destroyed all duality and taken the refuge of the Lord.

column2: dhirasaT sabadh surat baraj bisarajit prem nem bisam bisavaiaas ur aane hai ||
column3: He keeps his eyes away from the evils and ears closed to the slander and praise. Ever engrossed in Naam Simran, he imbibes the celestial faith of the Lord in his mind.

column2: jeevan mukat jag jeevan jeevan mool aapaa khoi hoi apara(n)par paraane hai ||92||
column3: Liberated Guru-conscious Sikh sheds all his ego and becomes a devotee of the infinite Lord, the creator of the World and source of all life on it. (92)

column2: saritaa sarovar salil mil ek bhe ek sai anek hot kaise niravaaro jee ||
column3: When the water of river and lake meet, they become indistinguishable. Then how can they be disintegrated into their earlier form when they have become one?

column2: paan choonaa kaathaa supaaree khaae sura(n)g bhe bahur na chatur baran bisathaaro jee ||
column3: Chewing beetle leaf, catechu, lime and beetle nut produces deep red colour. But then none of these ingredients can be separated from that red colour.

column2: paaras paras hot kanik anik dhaat kanik mai anik na hot gotaachaaro jee ||
column3: Many metals turn into gold by a touch of the philosopher-stone. Thereafter they cannot revert back to their original form.

column2: cha(n)dhan subaas kai subaasanaa banaasapatee bhagat jagat pat bisam bichaaro jee ||93||
column3: The sandalwood tree imparts fragrance to all the other trees around it. That fragrance cannot then be taken away from them. Similarly the union of the Lord and his devotees is a very strange and astonishing tale. They become one and there is no duality left. (93)

column2: chatur baran mil sura(n)g ta(n)bol ras gursikh saadh sa(n)g ra(n)g mai ra(n)geele hai ||
column3: As the union of beetle leaf, beetle nut, lime and catechu produce deep red colour, so do the Sikhs living in the presence of Satguru get dyed in hue of his love and Naam in the company of True and noble Sikhs.

column2: khaa(n)dd ghirat choon jal mile bi(n)janaadh savaiaadh prem ras a(n)mirat mai rasik raseele hai ||
column3: As the mixing of sugar, clarified butter, flour and water results in various types of dainty dishes, similarly Guru-conscious persons become the relishers of elixir like Naam in the company of the holy and noble people who themselves are engrossed in the meditation of Lord's name.

column2: sakal suga(n)dh sanaba(n)dh aragajaa hoi sabadh surat liv baasanaa baseele hai ||
column3: As all fragrances when put together result in a perfume of high quality, similarly the servant Sikhs of the Guru become pleasant smelling by virtue of Naam Simran and instilling the words of Guru in their conscious mind.

column2: paaras paras jaise kanik anik dhaat dhib dheh man unaman unameele hai ||94||
column3: As many metals turn into gold by the touch of paaras (Philosopher-Stone), so do the devoted Sikhs become refulgent and blossoms in the company of True Guru. (94)

column2: pavan gavan jaise guddeeaa uddat rahai pavan rahit guddee udd na sakat hai ||
column3: As a kite keeps aloft in the sky only if there is breeze blowing, and in the absence of breeze it drops down on the ground;

column2: ddoree kee maror jaise laTooaa firat rahai taau haau miTai gir parai haivai thakat hai ||
column3: As a top keeps revolving on its axis/spindle as long as the torque provided to it by the thread lasts, where after it drops dead;

column2: ka(n)chan asudh jiau(n) kuThaaree Thaharaat naahee sudh bhe nihachal chhab kai chhakat hai ||
column3: As a base gold cannot remain stable in a crucible and on becoming pure, rests and acquire glitter;

column2: dhuramat dhubidhaa bhramat hai chatur ku(n)T gurmat ek Tek mon na bakat hai ||95||
column3: So does a person roams about in all the four directions due to duality and base intelligence. But once he takes the refuge of Guru's wisdom, he acquires peace and becomes engrossed within. (95)

column2: prem ras a(n)mirat nidhaan paan pooran havai paramadhabhut gat aatam tara(n)g hai ||
column3: A Guru-conscious Sikh feels fully satiated drinking the loving elixir of the nectar-like Naam. He experiences strange and astonishing waves of spiritual ecstasy within.

column2: eit te dhirasaT surat sabadh bisarajat ut te bisam asacharaj prasa(n)g hai ||
column3: Relishing the loving elixir, a Guru-conscious person turns his senses away from the worldly engrossments and attaches them with the faculties that help him enjoy the divine pleasures. As a result he experiences strange and astonishing sensations within.

column2: dhekhai so dhikhaavai kaise sune so sunaavai kaise chaakhai so bataavai kaise raag ras ra(n)g hai ||
column3: All that he experiences, he cannot make others experience. How can he make others hear the unstruck music that he himself hears? The taste of Naam nectar that he enjoys himself, how can he describe it to others? All these he alone can enjoy.

column2: akath kathaa binodh a(n)g a(n)g thakat havai herat hiraanee boo(n)dh saagar sraba(n)g hai ||96||
column3: That person feels astonished and reaches a state of spiritual delight where every part of his body becomes stable in happiness. Staying in the holy feet of Satguru, the person merges with God like a drop falling in the sea loses its identity. (96)

column2: saadh sa(n)g ga(n)g mil sree gur saagar mile giaan dhiaan param nidhaan livaleen hai ||
column3: A Sikh ever in attendance of Satguru merges in the ocean-like True Guru through the Ganges-like holy congregation. He remains engrossed in the fountain-head of Cyan (knowledge) and contemplation.

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh madhukar gat cha(n)dhramaa chakor gur dhiaan ras bheen hai ||
column3: A True Sikh remains absorbed and immersed in the holy dust of the True Guru like a bumble bee and longs for a glimpse of his Guru just as a moon bird experiences pangs of separation of his beloved moon.

column2: sabadh surat mukataahal ahaar ha(n)s prem paramaarath bimal jal meen hai ||
column3: Like a swan whose diet is pearls, a true Sikh relishes the pearl-like Naam as his life support. Like a fish, he swims in the cool, clean and comforting waters of spirituality.

column2: a(n)mit kaTaachh amaraapadh kirapaa kirapaal  kamalaa kalapatar kaamadhainaadheen hai ||97||
column3: By the element and nectar-like glimpse of grace of the True Guru, a true Sikh attains immortality. And then all mythical donors like Kamdhen cow or Kalap brichh and even Lakshmi (Goddess of wealth) serve him diligently. (97)

column2: ek brahamaa(n)dd ke bithaar kee apaar kathaa koT brahamaa(n)dd ko naik kaise jaaneeaai ||
column3: When description of one universe is beyond the ability of a human being then how can the master of millions of universes be known?

column2: ghaT ghaT a(n)tar aau sarab nira(n)tar hai sookham sathool mool kaise pahichaaneeaai ||
column3: God, the cause of all visible and invisible world who is prevailing equally in all and sundry; how can he be reckoned?

column2: niragun adhirasaT sirasaT mai naanaa prakaar alakh lakhio na jai kaise ur aaneeaai ||
column3: God who is not visible in His Transcendental form, and is visible in myriad forms in His immanent form; who cannot be perceived, how can he then be lodged in the mind?

column2: sat roop sat naam satigur giaan dhiaan pooran braham sarabaatam kai maaneeaai ||98||
column3: Imperishable of character, of ever stable name, the complete Lord God, becomes known to a devoted Sikh through the Gyan dispensed by True. Guru. He attaches his conscious mind in the word and its tune and realises His presence in every living being. (98)

column2: pooran braham gur pooran sarab miee pooran kirapaa kai paripooran kai jaaneeaai ||
column3: Guru-blessed Sikh realises the universal presence of God through the total benefaction and kindness of the complete Guru who is manifestation of Supreme God.

column2: dharas dhiaan liv ek aau anek mek sabadh bibek Tek ekai ur aaneeaai ||
column3: By absorbing the mind in the form of True Guru and contemplation of Guru's teachings, the Sikh lodges that God in his heart who is one and is present in all.

column2: dhirasaT dharas ar sabadh surat mil pekhataa bakataa sorataa ekai pahichaaneeaai ||
column3: By keeping the vision of the eyes in the glimpse of Satguru and tuning the ears to the sound of Guru's utterances, an obedient and devoted Sikh reckons Him as the speaker, listener and watcher.

column2: sookham sathool mool gupat pragaT ThaT naT vaT simaran ma(n)tr man maaneeaai ||99||
column3: God who is the cause of the visible and invisible expanse, who is playing the game of the world both as a performer and the apparatus, the mind of a devoted Sikh of Guru gets engrossed in words and teachings of the Guru. (99)

column2: nahee dhadhasaar pitaa pitaamaa par pitaamaa sajan kuTa(n)b sut baa(n)dhav na bhraataa hai ||
column3: In the paternal hierarchy, there is not one relation; whether grandfather, great grandfather or any other son of the family, ward or brother;

column2: nahee nanasaar maataa par maataa biradh par maataa maamoo maamee maasee aau mauasaa bibidh bikhayaataa hai ||
column3: Similarly there isn't any relation, whether it is mother, grandmother or great grandmother, maternal uncle, aunt or any other recognised relationships;

column2: nahee sasuraar saas sasuraa saaro aau saaree nahee birateesur mai jaachik na dhaataa hai ||
column3: And also there is no relationship in the in-laws family whether mother-in-law, brother-in-law or sister-in-law; nor is their any relationship of family priest, donor or beggar.

column2: asan basan dhan dhaam kaahoo mai na dhekhio jaisaa gursikh saadh sa(n)gat ko naataa hai ||100||
column3: Nor has any relationship been seen amongst the friends and close associates who share their eats and drinks as is the relationship of Sikh Sangat (congregation) and a Sikh. (100)

column2: jaise maat pitaa pratipaalat anek sut anik sutan pai na taise hoi na aaviee ||
column3: As parents bring up and care for many of their children yet £hose children do not reciprocate the same way;

column2: jaise maat pitaa chit chaahat hai sutan kauo taise na sutan chit chaeh upajaaviee ||
column3: As parents love their wards from the core of their hearts, the same intensity of love cannot be generated in the hearts of the children.

column2: jaise maat pitaa sut sukh dhukh sogaana(n)dh sukh dhukh mai na taise sut Thahiraaviee ||
column3: As parents feel delighted on the happy occasions of their children and are distressed when they face tribulations, but the children do not feel the reciprocal intensity for their parents;

column2: jaise man bach kram sikhan luddaavai gur taise gur sevaa gursikh na hitaaviee ||101||
column3: As Satguru Ji pamper and cuddle the Sikhs with mind, words and deeds, similarly a Sikh cannot express in reciprocation these boons of Satguru Ji with equal intensity. (101)

column2: jaise kachhap dhar dhiaan saavadhaan karai taise maat pitaa preet sut na lagaaviee ||
column3: Just as a she tortoise bears its young ones in sand and takes care of them till they are sufficiently capable of looking after themselves, such love and concern for parents cannot be the characteristic of a child.

column2: jaise simaran kar koo(n)j parapak karai taiso simaran sut pai na ban aaviee ||
column3: Just as a crane teaches its young ones to fly and make them adept by flying many miles, a child cannot do for his parents.

column2: jaise guoo bachharaa kau dhugadh peeaai pokhai taise bachharaa na guoo preet hit laaviee ||
column3: Just as a cow feeds her young one with her milk and brings him up, the young one cannot reciprocate with same feelings the love and affection for the cow.

column2: taise giaan dhiaan simaran gursikh prat taise kaise sikh gur sevaa Thahiraaviee ||102||
column3: As a True Guru blesses a Sikh and expresses his love by making him well versed in divine knowledge, contemplation and meditation on Lord's name, how can a devoted Sikh rise to the same level of dedication and devotion in the service of Guru? (102)

column2: jaise maat pitaa keree sevaa saravan keenee sikh biralo iee gur sevaa Thahiraaviee ||
column3: A rare disciple would stay and serve his Guru just as noble Sarvan served his blind parents so dedicatedly.

column2: jaise lachhaman raghupat bhai bhagat mai koT madhe kaahoo gur bhaiee ban aaviee ||
column3: Some rare devotee would serve his Guru with so much love and devotion with which Lachhman served his brother Ram.

column2: jaise jal baran baran saraba(n)g ra(n)g biralo bibekee saadh sa(n)gat samaaviee ||
column3: As water mixes with any colour to acquire the same hue; thus a rare Sikh contemplating and practising meditation merges into the holy gathering of Guru's devotees.

column2: gur sikh sa(n)dh mile bees ik iees iees pooran kirapaa kai kaahoo alakh lakhaaviee ||103||
column3: On meeting the Guru and receiving the blessings of initiation from him, a Sikh surely reaches and realises God to become one with Him. Thus a True Guru showers his beneficence on a rare Sikh and lifts him to the divine level of supreme consciousness. (103)

column2: lochan dhiaan sam losaT kanik taa kai sravan usatat ni(n)dhaa samasar jaaneeaai ||
column3: For a devoted Sikh of the Guru, a lump of earth and gold are equal in value. Thus, praise and slander for him are the same.

column2: naasakaa suga(n)dh biraga(n)dh sam tul taa kai ridhai mitr satr samasar unamaaneeaai ||
column3: For that devoted Sikh, both fragrance and foul smell means nothing. So he treats both friend and foe alike.

column2: rasan suaadh bikh a(n)mrit samaan taa kai kar saparas jal agan samaaneeaai ||
column3: For him the taste of poison is not different from that of nectar. He feels the touch of water and fire alike.

column2: dhukh sukh samasar biaapai na harakh sog jeevan mukat gat satigur giaaneeaai ||104||
column3: He treats comforts and distresses alike. These two emotions do not influence him. By the benign and magnificence of a True Guru, who has blessed him with Naam, he achieves emancipation while living a house-holder's life. (104)

column2: charan saran gahe nij ghar mai nivaas aasaa manasaa thakat anat na dhaaviee ||
column3: In the refuge of a True Guru, a devoted Sikh resides in higher spiritual plane. All his expectations and desires vanish and his mind does not waver any more.

column2: dharasan maatr aan dhiaan sai rahat hoi simaran aan simaran bisaraaviee ||
column3: By the glimpse of True Guru, a devoted Sikh seeks not audience with anyone else. He rids himself of all other remembrances.

column2: sabadh surat mon brat kau praapat hoi prem ras akath kathaa na keh aaviee ||
column3: By engrossing his mind in the divine word (of Guru), he becomes bereft of all other thoughts. (He gives up all other futile talks). Thus his love for his Lord is beyond description.

column2: ki(n)chat kaTaachh kirapaa param nidhaan dhaan paramadhabhut gat at bisamaaviee ||105||
column3: By a momentary glimpse of the True Guru, one attains invaluable treasure of His name. The state of such a person is amazing and a cause of surprise for the beholder. (105)

column2: sabadh surat aapaa khoi gur dhaas hoi baratai baratamaan gur upadhes kai ||
column3: Shedding away the mine and - thine differentiation by the union of mind and divine word, one becomes a humble slave of the Guru. He makes his present a success by perpetual contemplation on His name.

column2: honahaar hoiee joiee joiee soiee soiee bhalo pooran braham giaan dhiaan paraves kai ||
column3: With his mind focused on the name of the Lord; living life according to Guru's teachings, he accepts all happenings as divine Will and blessings.

column2: naam nihakaam dhaam sahaj subhai chai prem ras rasik hui a(n)mrat aves kai ||
column3: A devotee living life of a householder, engrossed, in meditation of Lord's name and seized in His love ever enjoys the elixir of His name.

column2: sat roop sat naam satigur giaan dhiaan pooran sarab miee aadh kau adhes kai ||106||
column3: Such a slave of the Guru who by focusing his mind in the Lord regards the indestructible and ever stable Lord permeated in every speck, salutes and pays his obeisance to the force who is the cause of all beginnings. (106)

column2: sabadh surat aapaa khoi gur dhaas hoi baal budh sudh na karat moh dhroh kee ||
column3: One becomes true disciple only by getting the divine word of Guru absorbed in the mind and becoming a humble slave of the Guru. For virtually a possessor of the child-like wisdom, he is free of deceit and infatuations.

column2: sravan usatat ni(n)dhaa sam tul surat liv lochan dhiaan liv ka(n)chan aau loh kee ||
column3: Since his consciousness is engrossed in the name of the Lord; he is least affected by praise or rejection.

column2: naasakaa suga(n)dh biraga(n)dh samasar taa kai jihabaa samaan bikh a(n)mrit na boh kee ||
column3: Fragrance and foul smell, poison or elixir are the same for him, because his (devotee's) conscious is absorbed in Him.

column2: kar char karam akaram apath path kirat birat sam ukat na dhroh kee ||107||
column3: He remains stable and uniform even if he uses his hands in good or indifferent deeds; or treads path not worthy of appreciation. Such a devotee never harbours any feeling of deceit, falsehood or ill deeds. (107)

column2: sabadh surat aapaa khoi gur dhaas hoi sarab mai pooran braham kar maaneeaai ||
column3: By contemplating and absorbing oneself in the name obtained by the blessings of a True Guru, and shedding the feelings of mine and his, one becomes a servant of the Guru. Such a servant acknowledges the presence of one Lord everywhere.

column2: kaasaT agan maalaa sootr goras goba(n)s ek aau anek ko bibek pahichaaneeaai ||
column3: As the same fire exists in all the woods, different beads are arranged in the same thread; as all shades and species of cows yield milk of the same colour; similarly the slave of True Guru achieves the wisdom and knowledge of the presence of one Lord in all the living beings.

column2: lochan sravan mukh naasakaa anek sotr dhekhai sunai bolai man mek ur aaneeaai ||
column3: As all that is seen by the eyes, heard by the ears and said by the tongue reaches the mind, similarly the slave of the Guru sees one Lord residing in all beings and lodges Him in his mind.

column2: gur sikh sa(n)dh mile soha(n) soiee oot pot jotee jot milat jotee saroop jaaneeaai ||108||
column3: The union of a Sikh with his Guru makes him utter Lord's name repeatedly and enjoins in Him like warp and weft. When his light merges with light eternal, he too acquires the form of light divine. (108)

column2: gaa(n)ddaa mai miThaas taas chhilakaa na leeo jai dhaaram aau dhaakh bikhai beej geh ddaareeaai ||
column3: As the sweet juice of the sugarcane is taken and the cane is discarded; as the seeds in pomegranate and grapes are discarded;

column2: aa(n)b khiranee chhuhaaraa maajh guThalee kaThor kharaboojaa aau kaleedhaa sajal bikaareeaai ||
column3: Mango, dates have their endocarps hard; melon and watermelons though sweet release water and become unworthy of consumption very soon;

column2: madh maakhee mai maleen samai pai safal hui ras bas bhe nahee tirasanaa nivaareeaai ||
column3: The honey when cleaned of the bees and the wax become hard to give up eating it;

column2: sree gur sabadh ras a(n)mirat nidhaan paan gursikh saadh sa(n)g janam savaareeaai ||109||
column3: Similarly a Sikh of the Guru, relishes the elixir-like Naam in the company of holy men and makes his life a success. (109)

column2: salil mai dharan dharan mai salil jaise koop anaroop kai bimal jal chhaae hai ||
column3: As there is land in water and water inside Earth, like a well that is dug up to obtain neat and cold water;

column2: taahee jal maaTee kai banaiee ghaTikaa anek ekai jal ghaT ghaT ghaTikaa samaae hai ||
column3: The same water and earth are used for making pots and pitchers and all of them contain the same type of water.

column2: jaahee jaahee ghaTikaa mai dhirasaT kai dhekheeat pekheeat aapaa aap aan na dhikhaae hai ||
column3: Whichever pot or pitcher one looks into, one would see the same image in it, and nothing else is seen,

column2: pooran braham gur eka(n)kaar kai akaar braham bibek ek Tek Thahiraae hai ||110||
column3: Similarly the complete God pervades in the form of a-Guru and appear in the hearts of Sikhs (as was the case of image in various water-filled pots and pitchers). (110)

column2: charan saran gur ek pai(n)ddaa jai chal satigur koT pai(n)ddaa aage hoi let hai ||
column3: A disciple who walks one step towards Guru to take his refuge and goes to him with devotion and humility, Guru advances to receive him (devotee) by taking million steps.

column2: ek baar satigur ma(n)tr simaran maatr simaran taa(n)h baara(n)baar gur het hai ||
column3: He who unites with the Lord by remembering the incantation of the Guru even once, the True Guru remembers him millions of time.

column2: bhaavanee bhagat bhai kaauddee agrabhaag raakhai taeh gur sarab nidhaan dhaan dhet hai ||
column3: He who makes an offering of even a shell before the True Guru with loving worship and faith, the True Guru blesses him with the countless treasures of invaluable wealth that is Naam.

column2: satigur dhayaa nidh mahimaa agaadh bodh namo namo namo namo net net net hai ||111||
column3: The True Guru is a repository of compassion that is beyond description and understanding. Therefore myriad salutations to Him because there is no one else like Him. (111)

column2: prem ras a(n)mirat nidhaan paan pooran havai unaman unamat bisam bisavaiaas hai ||
column3: When a devotee meditating on His name is satiated with the drinking of loving nectar of Lord's name, he (devotee) enjoys supernatural ecstatic feeling in higher spiritual planes.

column2: aatam tara(n)g bahu ra(n)g a(n)g a(n)g chhab anik anoop roop uoop ko pragaas hai ||
column3: With multi-coloured waves of spiritual thoughts growing in his (devotee) mind, every part of his body conveys the glory of the Lord by emittence of strange and unique radiance.

column2: savaiaadh bisamaadh bahu bibidh surat sarab raag naadh baadh bahu baasanaa subaas hai ||
column3: The relishment of loving elixir of the Lord's name is astonishing. Enchanting tunes of all the musical modes and their consorts are heard in the ears. The nostrils feel the smell of myriad fragrances.

column2: paramadhabhut brahamaasan si(n)ghaasan mai(n) sobhaa sabhaa ma(n)ddal akha(n)ddal bilaas hai ||112||
column3: With the residing of the consciousness in the highest spiritual seat (the tenth opening), one enjoys the magnificent glory of all the spiritual planes. This ultimate state of tranquility provides complete stability to the body, mind and soul. (112)

column2: bayathaava(n)tai ja(n)tai jaise baidh upachaar karai bayathaa birataa(n)t sun harai dhukh rog kau ||
column3: As a medicine practitioner listens to the ailment of a patient and treats him for the malady;

column2: jaise maataa pitaa hit chit kai milat sutai khaan paan pokh tokh harat hai sog kau ||
column3: As parents fondly and lovingly meet their son, bring him up by serving dainty dishes, feel happy to allay all his distresses;

column2: birahanee banitaa kau jaise bharataar milai prem ras kai harat bireh biog kau ||
column3: As a wife separated from her husband for long relieves her pangs of separation and distresses with loving emotions;

column2: taise hee bibekee jan paraupakaar het milat salil gat sahaj sa(n)jog kau||113||
column3: Similarly those wise and realised servers of Lord dyed in the hue of Lord's name become humble like water and meets the needy who yearn for the divine solace and clemency. (113)

column2: bayathaava(n)tai baidh roop jaachik dhaataar gat gaahakai biaapaaree hoi maat pitaa poot kau ||
column3: Gursikhs with contemplated knowledge extend all help to the needy as an act of welfare, just as a medicine practitioner does for a patient, a donor does for a beggar, a trader for a customer and parents for their son.

column2: naar bharataar bidh mitr mitraiee roop sujan kuTa(n)b sakhaa bhai chai soot kau ||
column3: As an act of benevolence, the relishers of Lord's name reach the distressed people to render them comfort They are husband to a distressed wife or vice versa, friends to friends and other loved ones; according to the defined moral code.

column2: logan mai logaachaar bedh kai bedh beechaar giaan gur eka(n)kaar avadhoot avadhoot kau ||
column3: Sikhs blessed with Guru's wisdom acquire the supreme knowledge of the Lord and meet the common mortals as one of them and as intelligent and wise in the gathering of learned men. They approach the hermits as renouncers.

column2: biralo bibekee jan paraupakaar het milat salil gat ra(n)g sraba(n)g bhoot kau ||114||
column3: Such a rational and knowledgeable Sikh is very rare who for the sake of benevolence becomes humble like water and unites with the people of all denominations. (114)

column2: dharasan dhiaan dhib dheh kai bidheh bhe dhirag dhib dhirasaT bikhai bhaau bhagat cheen hai ||
column3: By the contemplated vision of the True Guru, the Guru-conscious Sikhs become free of ego while still in their body form. By virtue of divine sight of the True Guru, they acquire the wisdom of loving worship.

column2: adhiaatam karam kar aatam praves paramaatam praves sarabaatam liau leen hai ||
column3: By virtue of his spiritual knowledge and righteous actions, a follower of Guru finds peace and tranquillity in his self. By becoming one with Lord, he realises the presence of the divine light in the beings.

column2: sabadh giaan paravaan hui nidhaan paae paramaarath sabadhaarath prabeen hai ||
column3: By the knowledge acquired through meditation on divine word, a devoted Sikh is accepted by the Guru who blesses him with the treasure of Lord's Naam. He then becomes wise to understand the principles of spirituality.

column2: tatai mile tat jotee jot kai param jot prem ras bas bhe jaise jal meen hai ||115||
column3: As the quintessence merges into its origin, the soul of a Guru-conscious person merges with the Supreme soul like the flame of a beacon becomes one with the other flame. He gets engrossed in the pleasure of Lord's love like a fish in water. (115)

column2: adhiaatam karam paramaatam param padh tat mil tateh param tat vaasee hai ||
column3: A rare Guru-conscious person attains the knowledge of spirituality through spiritual deeds and absorbs himself in Him as truth rejoins with Truth.

column2: sabadh bibek Tek ek hee anek mek ja(n)tr dhun raag naadh anabhai abhiaasee hai ||
column3: As musical instruments produce melodious notes which also represent words in a song, so does a meditation practitioner merges in the fearless Lord who pervades in all and sundry.

column2: dharas dhiaan unamaan praan praanapat abigat gat at alakh bilaasee hai ||
column3: As meditation renders all our breaths one with Lord- the granter of life, so would a Guru-conscious man be engrossed in Him by contemplating on Him and becomes capable of enjoying all His bliss by this union with Him.

column2: a(n)mirat kaTaachh dhib dheh kai bidheh bhe jeevan mukat kouoo biralo udhaasee hai ||116||
column3: By the elixir-like divine glance of the True Guru, he becomes unconscious of his body (needs). Such a person with renounced and detached inclination is rare to come by. (116)

column2: supan charitr chitr jaagat na dhekheeat taarakaa ma(n)ddal parabhaat na dhikhaieeaai||
column3: Just as dream events cannot be seen while awake, just as stars are not visible after sunrise;

column2: taravar chhaiaa lagh dheeragh chapal bal teerath purab jaatraa thir na rahaieeaai||
column3: Just as the shadow of a tree keeps changing in size with the falling rays of the sun; and the pilgrimage to the holy places does not last for ever.

column2: nadhee naav ko sa(n)jog log bahurio na milai ga(n)dhrab nagar mirag tirasanaa bilaieeaai ||
column3: As the fellow travellers of a boat do not get to travel together again, as the presence of water due to mirage or the imaginary abode of gods (in space) is an illusion.

column2: taise maiaai moh dhroh kuTa(n)b saneh dheh gurmukh sabadh surat liv laieeaai ||117||
column3: So does a Guru-conscious person regards mammon, attachment and love of the body an illusion and he keeps his consciousness focused on the divine word of the Guru. (117)

column2: naihar kuaar ka(n)niaa laaddilee kai maaneeat biaahe sasuraar jai gunan kai maaneeaai ||
column3: An unmarried daughter is loved by everyone in parental house and enjoys respect in the in-laws house because of her virtues.

column2: banaj biauhaar lag jaat hai bidhes praanee kahe'ee sapoot laabh labhat kai aaneeaai ||
column3: As one goes to other cities to trade and earn living, but one is known as an obedient son only when one makes profit;

column2: jaise tau sa(n)graam samai par dhal mai akelo jai jeet aavai soiee sooro subhaT bakhaaneeaai ||
column3: As a warrior ingresses into enemy ranks and comes out victorious is known as a brave man.

column2: maanas janam pai charan saran gur saadh sa(n)g milai gur dhavaar pahichaaneeaai ||118||
column3: Similarly he who enjoins the holy gatherings, acquire the refuge of the True Guru is accepted in the court of the Lord. (118)

column2: naihar kuTa(n)b taj biaahe sasuraar jai gunan kai kulaa badhoo biradh kahaaviee ||
column3: Just as a girl leaves her parent's house after getting married and earns a respectable name for herself and her husband's family by virtue of her good traits;

column2: pooran patibrat aau gur jan sevaa bhai gireh mai girahesur sujas pragaTaaviee ||
column3: Earns the honourable title of all in all and revered one, by devotedly serving her elders and remaining loyal and faithful to her partner;

column2: a(n)t kaal jai pria sa(n)g seh gaaminee hui lok paralok bikhai uooch padh paaviee ||
column3: Departs from this world as an honourable companion of her husband and earns name for herself here and in world hereafter;

column2: gurmukh maarag bhai bhai nirabaahu karai dha(n)n gursikh aadh a(n)t Thahiraaviee ||119||
column3: So is a Sikh of Guru worthy of praise and adulations from beginning to end who treads the path of the Guru, lives life in the reverential fear of the Lord. (119)

column2: jaise nirap dhaam bhaam ek sai adhik ek naik anek raajaa sabhan laddaaviee ||
column3: As a king has many queens in his palace, each of remarkable beauty, he cajoles and pampers each one of them;

column2: janamat jaa kai sut vaahee kai suhaag bhaag sakal raanee mai paTaraanee so kahaaviee ||
column3: One who bears him a son enjoys higher status in the palace and is declared as the chief among the queens;

column2: asan basan sihajaasan sa(n)jogee sabai raaj adhikaar tau sapootee gireh aaviee ||
column3: Each one of them has the right and opportunities to enjoy the pleasures of the palace and share the bed of the king;

column2: gursikh sabai gur charan saran liv gur sikh sa(n)dh mile nij padh paaviee ||120||
column3: So do the Guru's Sikhs assemble in the refuge of the True Guru. But he who meets with the Lord after losing his self reaches the realm of spiritual peace and comfort. (120)

column2: tus mai ta(n)dhul boi nipajai saha(n)sr guno dheh dhaar karat hai paraupakaar jee ||
column3: A grain of rice covered by its husk when sowed yields many time more such grains and as rice (a staple food item) do much good in the world.

column2: tus mai ta(n)dhul nirabighan laagai na ghun raakhe rahai chira(n)kaal hot na bikaar jee ||
column3: The rice remains protected against insects as long as it remains in the husk. It remains preserved for long.

column2: tus mai nikas hoi bhagan maleen roop savaiaadh karavai raadhe rahai na sa(n)saar jee ||
column3: Outside the husk, rice breaks. It acquires a darkish hue and slight bitterness. It loses its worldly importance.

column2: gur upadhes gursikh gireh mai bairaagee gireh taj banakha(n)dd hot na udhaar jee ||121||
column3: So does a Sikh of Guru following the advice of Guru lives a householder's life without being attached and engrossed in it. He does good to others while living with his family members. He does not renounce the family and lives in jungles to emancipate himself from this world. (121)

column2: haradhee aau choonaa mil arun baran jaise chatur baran kai ta(n)bol ras roop hai ||
column3: As turmeric and lime when mixed produce red colour, but when betel leaf, lime, betelnut and catechu are all brought together, a very deep red colour is produced;

column2: dhoodh mai jaaman milai dhadh kai bakhaaneeat khaa(n)dd ghirat choon mil bi(n)jan anoop hai ||
column3: As a small cogulent added to the milk set it as curd but sugar, flour and clarified butter produces a very tasty dish;

column2: kusam suga(n)dh mil til sai fulel hot sakal suga(n)dh mil aragajaa dhoop hai ||
column3: An extract of flowers when mixed with sesame oil become scented oil, but mixing of saffron musk, sandalwood and rose make a very fragrant product called argaja;

column2: dhoi sikh saadh sa(n)g pa(n)ch paramesar hai dhas bees tees mile abigat uoop hai ||122||
column3: So would two Sikhs together make a holy congregation while five of them would represent the Lord. But where ten, twenty or thirty like-minded Sikhs engrossed in the love of the Guru meet, their praise is beyond description. (122)

column2: ek hee goras mai anek ras ko pragaas dhahio mahio maakhan aau ghirat unamaaneeaai ||
column3: From milk alone several products like curd, butter milk, butter and ghee (clarified butter) are obtained;

column2: ek hee uookhaaree mai miThaas ko nivaas  guR khaa(n)dd misaree aau kaleeka(n)dh pahichaaneeaai ||
column3: Being sweet, sugarcane gives us jaggery cakes, sugar, crystal sugar etc;

column2: ek hee gehoo sai hot naanaa bi(n)janaadh savaiaadh bhoone bheeje peese aau useiee bibidhaaneeaai ||
column3: Wheat is turned into various forms of dainty dishes; some 'fried, boiled, roasted or minced;

column2: paavak salil ek ekeh gun anek pa(n)ch kai pa(n)chaamirat su saadh sa(n)g jaaneeaai ||123||
column3: Fire and water have specific traits but when three others (wheat flour, clarified butter and sugar) join with them, elixir like Karhah Parshad results. Similarly coming together of obedient and loyal Sikhs of the Guru in the form of a congregation is considered holy and supreme. (123)

column2: khaa(n)dd ghirat choon jal paavak ikatr bhe pa(n)ch mil pragaT pa(n)chaamirat pragaas hai ||
column3: As coming together of sugar, clarified butter, flour, water and fire produces elixir like Karhah Parshad;

column2: mirag madh gauraa choaa cha(n)dhan kusam dhal sakal suga(n)dh kai aragajaa subaas hai ||
column3: As all aromatic roots and materials like musk, saffron etc. when mixed produce scent.

column2: chatur baran paan choonaa aau supaaree kaathaa aapaa khoi milat anoop roop taas hai ||
column3: As betel nut, betel leaf, lime and catechu lose their self-existence and merge with each other to produce a deep red colour more attractive than each one of them;

column2: taise saadh sa(n)gat milaap ko prataap aaiso saavadhaan pooran braham ko nivaas hai ||124||
column3: So is the praise of the holy congregation of saints blessed by the True Guru. It drenches everyone with such hue of Naam Ras that it opens the path for mergence into the Lord. (124)

column2: sahaj samaadh saadhasa(n)gat mai saach kha(n)dd satigur pooran braham ko nivaas hai ||
column3: The congregation of holy men is like Realm of Truth where they get absorbed in the memory of the Lord, His abode.

column2: dharas dhiaan saragun akaal moorat poojaa ful fal charanaamirat bisavaiaas hai ||
column3: For the Sikhs of the Guru, focusing of mind on True Guru is like seeing the Transcendental Lord who is beyond time. There belief of enjoying the magnificence sight of the True Guru is like performing worship with flowers and fruits.

column2: nira(n)kaar chaar paramaarath param padh sabadh surat avagaahan abhiaas hai ||
column3: A true servant of Guru realises the supreme state of the Absolute Lord through perpetual meditation and engrossment of his mind in the divine word.

column2: sarab nidhaan dhaan dhik bhagat bhai kaam nihakaam dhaam pooran pragaas hai ||125||
column3: By the loving worship of the Lord, (the bestower of all treasures) in the true holy congregation, a Guru-conscious person is convinced of no alternate place for him and he rests in complete radiance of the light divine of the God Lord. (125)

column2: sahaj samaadh saadh sa(n)gat sukirat bhoomee chit chitavat fal praapat udhaar hai ||
column3: Engrossed in meditation on His name, holy congregation is the best place to sow the seeds of supreme deeds that satiates all desires and sails one across the worldly ocean.

column2: bajar kapaaT khule haaT saadh sa(n)gat mai sabadh surat laabh ratan biauhaar hai ||
column3: The company of holy men removes ignorance and opens up the tightly shut doors of knowledge. In the union of consciousness and divine word, one enjoys the benefit of trading in the jewel like Naam.

column2: saadh sa(n)g braham sathaan gurdhev sev alakh abhev paramaarath aachaar hai ||
column3: The service of True Guru in the divine like place of holy congregation leads one to the realisation of the Lord who is imperceptible and indistinguishable.

column2: safal su khet het banat amit laabh sevak sahaiee baradhaiee upakaar hai ||126||
column3: Loving the fruitful place like holy congregation, one obtains immeasurable gain. Such a congregation is benefactor, helpful and philanthropic for the servers and slaves (of the Lord). (126)

column2: gurmukh saadh charanaamirat nidhaan paan kaal mai akaal kaal biaal bikh maareeaai ||
column3: A Guru-conscious person enjoys the benefits of all the nine treasures in the company of holy men. Despite living in the wheel of time, he remains protected from its wrath. He destroys the poison of the time like snake.

column2: gurmukh saadh charanaamirat nidhaan paan kul akuleen bhe dhubidhaa nivaareeaai ||
column3: He drinks deep the elixir of the Lord's name sitting in the dust of the feet of holy men. He becomes bereft of caste pride and is able to remove all differences of high and low from his mind.

column2: gurmukh saadh charanaamirat nidhaan paan sahaj samaadh nij aasan kee taareeaai ||
column3: In the company of holy men and enjoying the treasure of elixir like Naam, he remains engrossed in his self and attached consciously in a state of equipoise.

column2: gurmukh saadh charanaamirat param padh gurmukh pa(n)th abigat gat niaareeaai ||127||
column3: Relishing the elixir like Naam of the Lord in the company of the holy men, he attains the supreme state. The path of Guru-conscious people is beyond description. It is imperishable and celestial. (127)

column2: sahaj samaadh saadh sa(n)gat sakhaa milaap gagan ghaTaa ghama(n)dd jugat kai jaaneeaai ||

column2: tiragun ateet hui bisraam nihakaam dhaam unaman magan anaahadh alaapahee ||266||
column3: Free from the influence of three traits of the maya (mammon), a Guru-conscious person is ever absorbed in singing the melody of the Naam in the mystical tenth door state of high spirituality. (266)

column3: Both lotus and Nymphea lotus crave for a sight of The Sun and The Moon respectively. Because of their meeting and separating frequently, their love is besmirched.

column2: tiragun ateet gur charan kamal ras madh makara(n)dh rog rahat arogee hai ||
column3: A Guru-conscious person is ever engrossed in the elixir-like relishment of True Guru's feet after freeing himself from the influence of three traits of maya (mammon). His love is blemishless.

column3: Such a God-oriented person stays free from the worldly affairs and remains engrossed in the mystical tenth door because of the unstruck music melody that keeps playing ere.

column2: gurmukh sukh fal mahimaa agaadh bodh jog bhog alakh nira(n)jan prajogee hai ||267||
column3: The wondrous state and glory of such a Guru-oriented person is beyond explanation and description. Guru-oriented person remains absorbed in the Lord who is imperceptible, beyond worldly pleasures, yet who is a yogi and a relisher (Bhogi) as well. (267)

column2: jaise dharapan bikhai badhan bilokeeat aaise saragun saakhee bhoot gur dhiaan hai ||
column3: As one sees one's face in the mirror, so is the True Guru, the image of Transcendental God that can be comprehended by concentrating the mind on True Guru.

column2: jaise ja(n)tr dhun bikhai baajat ja(n)tree ko man taise ghaT ghaT gur sabadh giaan hai ||
column3: Just as the player's mind is in harmony with the tune that he is playing on his musical instrument, so is the knowledge of absolute God merged in the words of the True Guru.

column2: man bach kram jatr katr sai(n) ikatr bhe pooran pragaas prem param nidhaan hai ||
column3: By virtue of contemplation on the lotus feet of the True Guru and practicing his teachings in life, concentrating the mind that wanders about due to spurious utterances and deeds, a Guru-conscious person becomes a lover of the great treasure of Lord's name. That enlightens him and his inner self.

column2: aunaman magan gagan anahadh dhun sahaj samaadh niraala(n)b nirabaan hai ||268||
column3: By contemplating the Guru's teachings, the disciple acquires higher spiritual state and is immersed in the melodious tune that plays in his mystical tenth door. In this state of equipoise,the eternal being destroys all his wants and desires. (268)

column2: koTin koTaan dhiaan dhirasaT dharas mil at asacharaj mai herat hiraae hai ||
column3: The wondrous and marvellous state that befalls upon a Sikh of the True Guru when he integrates his vision in that of the Lord, defeats millions of other contemplations.

column3: Even a little glory (equivalent to a sesame seed) in respect of a Sikh, who has achieved union with the Guru's words, is beyond assessment and evaluation. That grandeur is infinite and limitless, and can never be weighed or assessed.

column3: As a result of the light effulgence in the Sikh of the Guru who has perpetually practiced in his mind the contemplation on the words of the Guru millions of Moons and Suns go sacrifice unto him again and again. (269)

column3: The Lord who has millions of Universes existing in the tip of His each hair, to what extent is His complete radiance spread?

column2: jaa(n) ke ek til ko mahaatam agaadh bodh pooran braham jot kaise keh aaviee ||
column3: The Lord-significance of whose marvellous and wonderful radiance equal to a sesame seed is beyond description, how can His complete light be described?

column2: pooran braham gur mahamaa akath kathaa net net net namo namo kar aaviee ||270||
column3: Praise and panegyrics of the True Guru who is an image of the complete Lord is beyond mention and elucidation. The best way to express one's love and respect for Him is to salute Him again and again while addressing Him- "0 Lord, Master! You are infinite, infinite." (270)

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh ras lubhit hui man madhukar sukh sa(n)paT samaane hai ||
column3: The bumble bee-like mind of a Guru-oriented person acquires strange comfort and peace by meditating on the nectar-like dust of the feet of the True Guru.

column3: In a state of equipoise and by virtue of inaccessible and immeasurable concentration, he keeps repeating the sweet rune of Naam continuously.

column2: pooran param jot param nidhaan dhaan aan giaan dhiaan simaran bisaraane hai ||271||
column3: By acquiring the great treasure of the Lord's name who is light supreme and complete in all respects, he forgets all other forms of remembrances, contemplations and worldly awareness’s. (271)

column2: raj tam sat kaam krodh lobh moh ha(n)kaar haar gur giaan baan kraa(n)t nihakraa(n)t hai ||
column3: By virtue of initiation by the Guru and practicing of meditation on the Lord's name, all the traits of maya (Raja, Sato, Tamo) and vices like lust, anger, avarice, attachment and pride are defeated. Their influence also becomes negligible.

column2: kaam nihakaam nihakaram karam gat aasaa kai niraas bhe bhraa(n)t nihabhraa(n)t hai ||
column3: With the acquisition of Guru's knowledge, a Guru-oriented person loses attachment with all desires, and all his actions become benevolent. All his worldly desires end and his wandering stops.
