column3: When multiplicity of one sesame seed of the creator cannot be explained, how can the unknowable, formless Lord be known? (273)

column2: rachanaa charitr chit bisam bachitr pan ghaT ghaT ek hee anek hui dhikhaae hai ||

column3: The feet of a Guru-oriented person tread towards the path of the True Guru. They give up travelling or going in other directions. For him his lone desire of meeting the beloved Lord is unique and marvellous. (279)

column2: charan saran gur dhaavat baraj raakhai nihachal chit sukh sahaj nivaas hai ||

column3: Treading the path of Guru, he destroys all his duality and doubts. The refuge of the True Guru makes his mind stable.

column2: poojeeaai na sravan surat sanaba(n)dh kar poojeeaai na naasikaa subaas savaiaas kraa(n)t kai ||
column3: Ears are not worshipped for their power of hearing nor nostrils for their ability to smell and breathe.

column2: poojeeaai na mukh savaiaadh sabadh sa(n)jugat kai poojeeaai na hasat sakal a(n)g paa(n)t kai ||
column3: Mouth which enjoys all the tastes and make speech, is not worshipped nor the hands which nourish all other limbs.

column2: dhirasaT sabadh surat ga(n)dh ras rahit hui poojeeaai padhaarabi(n)dh navan mahaa(n)t kai ||289||
column3: Feet which are devoid of ability to see, talk, hear, smell or taste are worshipped for their traits of humility. (289)

column2: navan gavan jal niramal seetal hai navan basa(n)udhar sarab ras raas hai ||
column3: Water that flows downward is always cool and clear. The earth that remains under the feet of all is the treasure-house of all the goods that are pleasurable and worth relishing.

column2: auradh tapasiaa kai sreekha(n)dd baas bohai ban navan samu(n)dhr hot ratan pragaas hai ||
column3: Sandalwood tree wilted under the weight of its branches and leaves as if in supplication, spreads its fragrance and makes all the vegetation in the near vicinity fragrant.

column2: navan gavan pag poojeeat jagat mai chaahai charanaamirat charan raj taas hai ||
column3: Of all the limbs of body, feet which remain on earth and at the lowest end of the body are worshipped. The whole world desires nectar and dust of holy feet.

column2: taise har bhagat jagat mai ni(n)maree bhoot kaam nihakaam dhaam bisam bisavaiaas hai ||290||
column3: Similarly the worshippers of the Lord live as humble human beings in the world. Unsullied by the worldly sensualities, they remain stable and unmoved in unique love and devotion. (290)

column2: sabadh surat liv leen jal meen gat sukhamanaa sa(n)gam hui ulaT pavan kai ||
column3: Just as a fish swims through towards upstream swiftly, so does a disciple of Guru engrossed in the Guru's word crosses the confluence of all the three veins (Irha, Pingla and Sukhmana) with the methodology of reverse breathing/air.

column2: bisam bisavaiaas bikhai anabhai abhiaas ras prem madh apeeau peeaai guhaj gavan kai ||
column3: Becoming fearless in the strange devotion and love, engrossed in the practice of Naam Simran and reaching there through strangely mysterious ways, one drinks deep the loving eternal nectar.

column2: sabadh kai anahadh surat kai unamanee prem kai nijhar dhaar sahaj ravan kai ||
column3: By plentiful practicing of meditation on Guru's teachings, the mind starts listening to the unstruck melody. As a result, it changes its stance and becomes God-oriented. Then one relishes the continuous flow of the divine nectar that is produced as a result of celestial love.

column2: tirakuTee ula(n)gh sukh saagar sa(n)jog bhog dhasam sathal nihakeval bhavan kai ||291||
column3: By crossing the confluence of three nerves, one enjoys the bliss of meeting the Lord. The mystical door there is the unique place of enjoying peace, union, relishment and pleasure. (291)

column2: jaise jal jalaj aau jal dhudh seel meen chakiee kamal dhinakar prat preet hai ||
column3: Just as a lotus flower loves water, water has affinity for milk, fish loves water, ruddy Sheldrake and lotus love the sun;

column2: dheepak pata(n)g al kamal chakor sas mirag naadh baadh ghan chaatirak sucheet hai ||
column3: A winged insect (patanga) is attracted to the flame of the light, a black bee is crazy of the fragrance of the lotus flower, a red legged partridge is ever craving for a glimpse of the moon, a deer has affinity for music, while a rain-bird is ever alert for the swati drop.

column2: naar aau bhataar sut maat jal tirakhaava(n)t khudhiaarathee bhojan dhaaridhr dhan meet hai ||
column3: As a wife loves her husband, a son is deeply attached with his mother, a thirsty man craves for water, a hungry for food, and a pauper is always trying to befriend wealth.

column2: maiaa moh dhroh dhukhadhaiee na sahaiee hot gur sikh sa(n)dh mile tiragun ateet hai ||292||
column3: The love of maya is deceitful, its tricks cause suffering and it doesn't accompany us in the finals hours of our life. Love that a Sikh has for his Guru is beyond the influence of maya and supports the Sikh when he departs from this world. (292)

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh ras lubhit hui a(n)g a(n)g bisam sraba(n)g mai samaane hai ||
column3: The loving disciples of the True Guru whose every limb of the body is intoxicated in the elixir-like Naam of the Lord remain absorbed in the Lord whose form is awesome and enrapturing.

column2: dhirasaT dharas liv dheepak pata(n)g sa(n)g sabadh surat mirag naadh hui hiraane hai ||
column3: Devotee's mind is akin to a moth who is always absorbed in love of light. Like a deer, enchanted by certain sounds, the devotee remains engrossed in the unstruck music by practicing Naam Simran.

column2: kaam nihakaam krodhaakrodh niralobh lobh moh niramoh aha(n)mev ha(n)oo lajaane hai ||
column3: A Guru-oriented Sikh is free from the effects of lust, anger, avarice, attachment and shy of pride and other vices.

column2: bisamai bisam asacharajai asacharaj mai adhabhut paramadhabhut asathaane hai ||293||
column3: The mind of Guru-conscious and practitioners of Naam resides in the mystical tenth door. This is a place that is full of ecstasy, astonishing beyond astonishments and most amazing. (293)

column2: dharasan jot ko udhot sukh saagar mai koTik usatat chhab til ko pragaas hai ||
column3: The radiance of the light of the True Guru, the ocean of happiness and comfort is repository of all the happiness of the world. A glimmer of light no more than a sesame seed has generated radiance of millions of beauties and adulations in the world.

column2: ki(n)chat kirapaa koTik kamalaa kalapatar madhur bachan madh koTik bilaas hai ||
column3: A little kind look of the True Guru has millions of goddesses of wealth and celestial trees capable of fulfilling all desires, hidden in it. Elixir immersed sweet words of the True Guru has millions of relishments of the world.

column2: ma(n)dh musakaan baan khaan hai koTaan sas sobhaa koT loT poT kumadhanee taas hai ||
column3: The habit of soft and slow smile of the True Guru is the source of praise of millions of moons. The glory of millions of nymphea flowers is sacrifice unto it.

column2: man madhukar makara(n)dh ras lubhit hui sahaj samaadh liv bisam bisavais hai ||294||
column3: A devoted and loving Sikh of the Guru enamoured by the elixir-like relishment of Naam Simran practiced through the teachings of the True Guru remains absorbed in a state of equipoise and astonishing devotion of the Lord. (294)

column2: charan saran raj majan maleen man dharapan gat gurmat nihachal hai ||
column3: By taking True Guru's shelter and meditating on the Lord's name, the mind polluted by vices become clear like a mirror.

column2: giaan gur a(n)jan dhai chapal kha(n)jan dhirag akul nira(n)jan dhiaan jal thal hai ||
column3: Under the, influence of mind and intelligence, putting colorium. of Guru's teachings in the bird-like playful eyes, the consciousness gets engrossed in the Lord Almighty who is caste and creedless, beyond the blemish of maya and residing in oceans and deserts alike.

column2: bha(n)jan bhai bharam ar ga(n)jan karam kaal paa(n)ch parapa(n)ch balaba(n)ch niradhal hai ||
column3: Such celestial cogitation, (Reflection) of Lord is capable of ridding myriads suspicions, destroyer of vices and virtues that a person in the dragnet of births and deaths. It shatters the five enemies and their tricks as well.

column2: sevaa kara(n)jan sarabaatam nira(n)jan bhe maiaa mai udhaas kalimal niramal hai ||295||
column3: A Guru-conscious person, seeing the light of mammon-less Lord effulging in all the living beings and serving the mankind devotedly becomes like unsullied Lord. Renouncing attachment of maya, he saves himself from grave vices and become pure and clean (of heart and soul). (295)

column2: cha(n)dhramaa achhat rav raahu na sakat gras dhirasaT agochar hui sooraj grahan hai ||
column3: With the presence of the moon, Rahu cannot devour the Sun, But when the Sun hides from the moon, the solar eclipse takes place. (Here the moon is symbol of noble person in whose company the maya does not devour the hot natured Sun).

column2: pachham udhot hot cha(n)dhramai namasakaar poorab sa(n)jog sas ket khet han hai ||
column3: East and West are the directions of Sun and Moon respectively. When two days after the new moon day, the moon becomes visible in the West, all salutes him (according to Indian traditions). But on full moon day, the moon rises in the East and it is not eclipsed. (Company of a noble person is like Cool moon that is the means of protection of the hot-tempered Sun. On the contrary, company of hot Sun-like person becomes a source of distress for the cool-tempered moon).

column2: kaasaT mai agan magan chira(n)kaal rahai agan mai kaasaT parat hee dhahan hai ||
column3: The fire remains hidden in wood for long but as soon as wood touches fire, it burns (Here fire is symbolic of low sinful man whereas cool-minded wood is shown as a God-fearing person).

column2: taise siv sakat asaadh saadh sa(n)gam kai dhuramat gurmat dhuseh sahan hai ||296||
column3: Similarly, keeping company of wicked-minded self-willed persons, one has to suffer pain and distress but keeping company of Guru-oriented persons, one achieves salvation. (296)

column2: saadh kee sujanataiee paahan kee rekh preet bair jal rekh hui bisekh saadh sa(n)g mai ||
column3: The loving relationship of Guru-oriented persons is like a line drawn on stone slab and is indelible. That is, the significance of company of Guru oriented persons is, that there is no ill feeling or animosity.

column2: dhurajanataa asaadh preet jal rekh ar bair tau pakhaan rekh sekh a(n)g a(n)g mai ||
column3: Love of self oriented persons is momentary like a line drawn on water while their enmity remains like a line on a stone slab. It becomes part of their limb.

column2: kaasaT agan gat preet bipreet surasaree jal baaroonee saroop jal ga(n)g mai ||
column3: A Gurmukhs love is like that of wood; it keeps it’s fuel of fire hidden within. Company of evil-minded people leaves bad effects and company of good people leaves good effect.  Similarly, pure water from the river Ganges can be polluted with wine.

column2: dhuramat gurmat ajayaa sarap gat upakaaree aau bikaaree dda(n)g hee kudda(n)g mai ||297||
column3: A person with base and impure mind is like a snake who commits evil due to its bad trait. It is always ready to harm. But a Guru-oriented person is like a goat which is always ready to do a good deed. (297)

column2: dhuramat gurmat sa(n)gat asaadh saadh kaasaT agan gat Tev na Tarat hai ||
column3: Like wood and fire, the companies of Manmukh and Gurmukh dispense base wisdom and Guru's intelligence respectively. Wood hordes the fire within but fire destroys the wood. Both good and bad do not refrain from their nature.

column2: ajayaa sarap jal ga(n)g baarunee bidhaan san aau majeeTh khal pa(n)ddit larat hai ||
column3: A goat is good doer while a snake causes distress by its bite. River Ganges purifies the wine poured in it, while a drop of wine in Ganges water pollutes it. A rope of jute binds while Rubia munjista plant colours fast. Similarly fools and intelligent men are of opposite nature.

column2: ka(n)Tak puhap sail ghaTikaa sanaeh sasatr ha(n)s kaag bag biaadh mirag hoi nibarat hai ||
column3: A thorn pains, flowers emit fragrance. A pitcher gives cold water, a stone breaks the pitcher. An armour coat saves, weapons cause injury. A swan is of good intellect, crows and herons eat flesh. Hunters hunt dears, dears give musk and hide. All settle on who and what is good or bad.

column2: losaT kanik seep sa(n)kh madh kaalakooT sukh dhukh dhaik sa(n)saar bicharat hai ||298||
column3: Iron made into weapons gives distress, while gold is comfort giving. A shell makes a swati drop into a pearl whereas a conch only wails. Nectar makes a person immortal while poison kills. Similarly Gurmukhs do good to all whereas Manmukhs dispense distress. (298)

column2: dhaadhar saroj baa(n)s baavan maraal bag paaras pakhaan bikh a(n)mirat sa(n)jog hai ||
column3: A frog and lotus flower, a bamboo and sandalwood tree, a crane and a swan, an ordinary stone and a philosopher-stone, nectar and poison may come together, yet do not adopt each other's characteristics.

column2: mirag miragamadh eh man madh umaakhee saakhee baa(n)jh badhoo naeh neh nihafal bhog hai ||
column3: Deer has musk in its naval, a cobra has a pearl in its hood, a bee lives with honey, a sterile woman gets to meet with her husband with love but all in vain.

column2: dhinakar jot uloo barakhai samai javaaso asan basan jaise birathaava(n)t rog hai ||
column3: Just as Sun's light for an owl, rain for a wild herb (javran-alhogi maunosum) and clothes and food for a patient are like disease.

column2: taise gurmat beej jamat na kaalar mai a(n)kur udhot hot naahin biog hai ||299||
column3: Similarly sullied and vice-ridden hearts cannot be fertile to the seeds of Guru's sermons and teachings. It just does not sprout. Such a person remains separated from his God. (299)

column2: sa(n)gam sa(n)jog prem nem kau pata(n)g jaanai bireh biog sog meen bhal jaaniee ||
column3: The loving atmosphere that gets generated when a lover is about to meet his beloved can best be known by a moth. The pang of separation is best described by a fish that has been separated from its beloved water.

column2: eik Tak dheepak dhiaan praan paraharai salil biog meen jeevan na maaniee ||
column3: A moth burns itself for the love of the flame that he keeps watching and playing with. Similarly a fish separated from water has no meaning of life. She dies when out of it.

column2: charan kamal mil bichhurai madhup man kapaT saneh dhirag janam agiaaniee ||
column3: These beings lay down their lives in love of their beloveds. Contrarily, an evil person's mind, like a black bee, hops from one flower to another, knowingly seperating from the holy feet of True Guru. Human life is a waste and a curse for such a person.

column2: nihafal jeevan maran gur bimukh hui prem ar bireh na dhouoo ur aaniee ||300||
column3: A follower of his own heart turned away from the refuge of the Guru, who does not feel the pangs of separation and love of the holy feet of the. True Guru, has wasted away his birth and death thus living a worthless life. (300)

column2: dhirasaT dharas liv dhekhai aau dhikhaavai soiee sarab dharas ek dharas kai jaaneeaai ||
column3: An obedient disciple of the Guru who has focused his vision in the glimpse of the True Guru, he observes the impermeable Lord everywhere and every place. He makes others see Him too. He regards and understands that all philosophies are present in His sight.

column2: sabadh surat liv kahat sunat soiee sarab sabadh ek sabadh kai maaneeaai ||
column3: When a Guru-oriented person acquires the teachings of the True Guru, his mind gets absorbed in the practicing of Lord's Naam Simran. He then speaks and hears the words of the True Guru deep in his soul. He regards all singing modes engrossed in the melody of the divine words.

column2: kaaran karan karatag sarabag soiee karam karatoot karataar pahichaaneeaai ||
column3: In this state of immersion in the elixir of Naam, a Guru oriented slave recognises the cause of all causes, the knower of all deeds and capable of knowing all; who is the doer of all the deeds-the Doer and Creator,

column2: satigur giaan dhiaan ek hee anek mek|| braham bibek Tek ekai ur aaneeaai ||301||
column3: And thus a Guru-conscious person becomes aware of One God through the knowledge blessed by the True Guru and perpetual contemplation of Him, Such a person leans on none else for support except One All-pervading Lord, (301)

column2: ki(n)chat kaTaachh maiaa mohe brahama(n)dd kha(n)dd saadh sa(n)g ra(n)g mai bimohit magan hai ||
column3: The Lord whose one transverse glance can infatuate millions of people of the regions and realms in maya, that God, enamoured by the love of the assembly of true God-loving meditating people remains absorbed in them.

column2: jaa(n) ke oa(n)kaar kai akaar hai naanaa prakaar keeratan samai saadh sa(n)g sau lagan hai ||
column3: The Lord whose expanse and forms are indescribable, He remains involved in the pious people through the singing of His hymns of praise.

column2: siv sanakaadh brahamaadh aagiaakaaree jaa ke agrabhaag saadh sa(n)g gunan agan hai ||
column3: The Lord who has the services of all the three deities and the four sons of Brahma at His beck and call and obedience, that Lord of countless traits remains obedient in the company of the holy and saintly persons who are ever engrossed in Him.

column2: agam apaar saadh mahimaa apaar bikhai at livaleen jal meen abhagan hai ||302||
column3: Praise of congregation immersed in His loving remembrance is beyond comprehension. A Guru-conscious devotee remains in love with Him like a fish in water. (302)

column2: nij ghar mero saadh sa(n)gat naaradh mun dharasan saadh sa(n)g mero nij roop hai ||
column3: Lord (Bhagwan) tells sage Narad, 0 dear devotee! Congregation of Guru-conscious and true people is my abode if company is my glimpse.

column2: saadh sa(n)g mero maataa pitaa aau kuTa(n)b sakhaa saadh sa(n)g mero sut sresaT anoop hai||
column3: Company of godlike people of the True Guru is like my friends and whole family. The company of true is my beautiful and supreme son.

column2: saadh sa(n)g sarab nidhaan praan jeevan mai saadh sa(n)g nij padh sevaa dheep dhoop hai ||
column3: Congregation is a treasure-house of all comforts and happiness. It is my life-support. Congregation of true people is means of gaining higher spiritual state. It is also a place of performing service which is true worship.

column2: saadh sa(n)g ra(n)g ras bhog sukh sahaj mai saadh sa(n)g sobhaa at upamaa aau uoop hai ||303||
column3: Company of Guru beloveds is a place of relishing the elixir of Naam Simran and enjoying spiritual peace. The glory and grandeur of the holy congregation is beyond praise unique and wondrous. (303)

column2: agam apaar dhev alakh abhev at anik jatan kar nigreh na paieeaai ||
column3: The Lord who is highly inaccessible, infinite, light effulgent and beyond comprehension, cannot be reached by controlling the senses with all available means.

column2: paieeaai na jag bhog paieeaai na raaj jog naadh baadh bedh kai agahu na gahaieeaai ||
column3: He cannot even be realised through holding/performing of Yag, hom (offerings to fire god), holding of feast for holy men, nor through Raj Yog. He cannot be reached through playing of musical instruments nor recitation of Vedas.

column2: teerath purab dhev dhev sevakai na paieeaai karam dharam brat nem liv laieeaai ||
column3: Such God of gods can also not be reached by visiting places of pilgrimage, celebrating days considered auspicious or by the service of gods. Even fasts of myriad kind cannot even bring Him closer. Contemplations are futile as well.

column2: nihafal anik prakaar kai achaar sabai saavadhaan saadh sa(n)g hui sabadh gaieeaai ||304||
column3: All the methods of God-realisation are of no use. He can only be realised by singing His paeans in the company of holy men and meditating on Him with concentrated and singular mind. (304)

column2: sufan charitr chitr joiee dhekhai soiee jaanai dhoosaro na dhekhai paavai kahu kaise jaaneeaai ||
column3: The miracle of a dream is known to the one who has seen it. No one else can see it. Then how can anyone else know about it?

column2: naal bikhai baat ke'ee suneeat kaan dhe'ee bakataa aau srotaa bin kaa pai unamaaneeaai ||
column3: If something is spoken in one end of a tube and the other end is put in one's own ears, then only he alone would know who has said or heard what. No one else can know.

column2: paghoolaa ke mool bikhai jaise jal paan keejai leejeeaai jatan kar pe'ee man maaneeaai ||
column3: Just as a lotus flower or any other plant draws water through its roots from the soil, the flower or plant alone knows about the state of its bloom, who drinks according to his desire.

column2: gur sikh sa(n)dh mile guhaj kathaa binodh giaan dhiaan prem ras bisam bidhaaneeaai ||305||
column3: The event of a Sikh meeting with his Guru and obtaining initiation from him is very wondrous, blissful and mysterious. The description of the knowledge obtained from the True Guru, contemplation on Him, His love and ecstasy is very strange to describe. No one else can know about it. (305)

column2: navan gavan jal seetal a mal jaise agan uradh mukh tapat maleen hai ||
column3: Just as water flowing downward remains cool and clear of contamination but fire that goes upward causes heat and pollution;

column2: safal hui aa(n)b jhuke rahat hai chira(n)kaal nivai na ari(n)dd taa(n) te aarabalaa chheen hai ||
column3: Just as a mango tree bends down when it yields fruit, and lives a long life, but a castor oil seed plant does not bend. It would break if we bend it, it breaks. Thus it has a short span of life.

column2: cha(n)dhan subaas jaise baaseeaai banaasapatee baa(n)s tau baddaiee booddio sa(n)g livaleen hai ||
column3: Just as the sweet smell of a small sized sandalwood tree gets infused in the vegetation around it, but a tall and high bamboo plant arrogant of its size absorbs no fragrance of the sandalwood tree.

column2: taise hee asaadh saadh aha(n)budh nimrataa kai san aau majeeTh gat paap pu(n)n keen hai ||306||
column3: Similarly evil and apostate people bound by their pride and ego commit sins. On the contrary those good people who live in the way of the Guru and are humble, do good work like Rubia munjista (Majith). (306)

column2: sakal banaasapatee bikhai dhrum dheeragh dhui nihafal bhe boodde bahut baddaiee kai ||
column3: Amongst all the vegetation, both Silk cotton (Simhal) and Bamboo are the tallest but feeling proud of their size and greatness, they remain failures.

column2: cha(n)dhan subaasanaa kai se(n)bal subaas hot baa(n)s niraga(n)dh bahu gaa(n)Than ddiThaiee kai||
column3: At least a Silk cotton tree do acquire some fragrance from a Sandalwood tree but due to the obstinacy of the knots, a Bamboo tree remains bereft of Sandalwood smell.

column2: se(n)bal ke fal tool khag mirag chhaiaa taa kai baa(n)s tau baran dhokhee jaarat buraiee kai ||
column3: The cotton of the Silk cotton tree is put to use. The vast expanse of the tree provides shade for birds and other animals, but a Bamboo is family destroyer and due to its evil nature, it burns the other Bamboos that it rubs with.

column2: taise hee asaadh saadh hot saadh sa(n)gat kai tirasaTai na gur gop dhroh gur bhaiee kai ||307||
column3: Similarly an apostate Sikh becomes an obedient of the Guru by obtaining his sermons and enjoying the company of godly persons. But one who turns his face despite belonging to Guru, who is guilty of doing wrong to his Guru-brothers pushed around from door to door.(307)

column2: birakh balee milaap safal saghan chhaiaa baa(n)s tau baran dhokhee milai jarai jaar hai ||
column3: Many fruit-bearing trees along with creepers climbing upon them become dense of shade. They provide comfort to all wayfarers. But Bamboo that rubs with each other becomes cause of its own destruction through fire and for others as well who are near it.

column2: safal hui tarahar jhukat sakal tar baa(n)s tau baddaiee booddio aapan sa(n)maar hai ||
column3: All other fruit-bearing trees bow down but a Bamboo tree sublimed in his own praise keep accumulating pride.

column2: sakal banaasapatee sudh ridhai mon gahe baa(n)s tau reeto gaTheelo baaje dhaar maar hai ||
column3: All fruit trees remain at peace at heart and are silent of disposition. They produce no sounds. But the tall Bamboo is hollow from inside and is knotted. It wails and produces noise.

column2: cha(n)dhan sameep hee achhat niraga(n)dh rahe gursikh dhokhee bajar praanee na udhaar hai ||308||
column3: He who remains proud and hypocrite despite living in the close proximity of Sandalwood like True Guru, (remains fragrance-less) and does not acquire Guru's wisdom, such a person whoever wishes ill of Guru's disciples can never sail across the worldly ocean. (308)

column2: gur sikh sa(n)gat milaap ko prataap aeso prem kai parasapar pag lapaTaavahee ||
column3: The glory of the meeting of obedient and truthful persons of the True Guru is such that they bend down to touch each others feet regardless of their high or low status or age.

column2: dhirasaT dharas ar sabadh surat mil pooran braham giaan dhiaan liv laavahee ||
column3: Having seen the True Guru and by the divine effect of words residing in their mind, such Sikhs of the Guru remain engrossed in perfect Lord by virtue of Guru's knowledge and contemplation. The effect is always visible on them.

column2: ek misaTaan paan laavat mahaa prasaadh ek gurapurab kai sikhan bulaavahee ||
column3: Many of these devotees of the Guru bring dainty dishes for the consumption of the saintly persons of the congregation. Others send invitations to the Sikhs of Guru and hold Religious functions on the days associated with their Gurus.

column2: siv sanakaadh baachhai tin ke uchisaT kau saadhan kee dhookhanaa kavan fal paavahee ||309||
column3: Even gods like Shiv, Sanak crave for the leftovers of such Sikhs of the Guru who are blessed with divine traits of Naam Simran. What good will one reap who thinks ill of such godly ones? It is evident that such a person will be severely 'shed in the court of Almighty. (309)

column2: jaise bojh bharee naav aa(n)guree dhaivai baahar haivai paar parai poor sabai kusal bihaat hai ||
column3: A fully loaded boat remains above water-level by no more than two fingers. Everyone rejoices when all the travellers are able to disembark on the other bank/shore;

column2: jaise ekaahaaree ek gharee paakasaalaa baiTh bhojan kai bi(n)janaadh savaiaadh ke aghaat hai ||
column3: Just as a person who eats food once in 24 hours (though hungry) feels his hunger satiated when he spends sometime in the kitchen where the food is being prepared;

column2: jaise raaj dhavaiaar jai karat juhaar jan ek gharee paachhai dhes bhogataa haivai khaat hai ||
column3: Just as a servant shows much respect at the door of the king or his master, and later on, he reaps the fruit of his service when he himself becomes landlord.

column3: Obedient disciple of the True Guru considers the support of Guru teachings and wisdom as authentic and true. He has no one else in his heart other than One God. He does not recognise god-Shiv or goddess-Shakti as a means of emancipation. He remains a meditator of One Fearless God.

column2: tiragun ateet jeet haar na harakh sog sa(n)jog biog meT sahaj nivaasee hai ||
column3: He remains unsullied of the influence of maya. Defeat or victory, happiness or sorrow does not disturb or please him. He remains absorbed in supreme spiritual state discarding all thoughts of achievements and failures.

column2: chatur baran ik baran hui saadh sa(n)g pa(n)ch parapa(n)ch tiaag bisam bisavaiaasee hai ||
column3: By joining true congregation he destroys the differences of high low caste and belongs to One God. Detaching from the love of five elements, he takes to Naam Simran of the wondrous God Lord and holds his faith in Him.

column2: khaT dharasan parai paar hui sapat sar nav dhuaar ula(n)gh dhasamiee udhaasee hai ||333||
column3: A Gursikh stays in the company of true seekers beyond the garbs of the six philosophical schools. He frees himself from the bonds of nine doors of the body and lives blissfully in of the tenth door (Dasam Duar). (333)

column2: nadhee naav ko sa(n)jog sujan kuTa(n)b log hoigo jo dheeo sooiee milai aagai jai kai ||
column3: The union with friends, family members and other acquaintances in this world is like voyagers in a boat that lasts for a short period of time. Therefore whatever is donated for good deeds in. this world will be received in the world beyond.

column2: asan basan dhan sa(n)g na chalat chale arape dheejai dharamasaalaa pahuchai kai ||
column3: Food, clothing and wealth does not go with one in the next world. Whatever has been assigned to the Guru in the true company is what one's wealth or earnings are for life beyond.

column2: aaTho jaam saaTho gharee nihafal maayaa moh safal palak saadh sa(n)gat samai kai ||
column3: Spending all the time in the love of maya and its actions are futile but enjoying the company of saintly persons even for a few seconds is a big achievement and useful.

column2: mal mootr dhaaree aau bikaaree nira(n)kaaree hot sabadh surat saadh sa(n)g liv lai kai ||334||
column3: By uniting the words/teachings of the Guru with mind, and by the grace of holy company, this filth-filled and vice-ridden human being becomes an obedient disciple of the Guru. (334)

column2: haumai abhimaan asathaan taj ba(n)jh ban charan kamal gur sa(n)paT samaae hai ||
column3: The black bee like mind of a Guru-oriented person who is attached with the congregation of saintly persons, forsakes pride and ego which is like a jungle of bamboos. He leaves attachment and infatuations. Enamoured by the lotus-like feet of the True Guru, he remains engrossed in it.

column2: at hee anoop roop herat hiraane dhirag anahadh gu(n)jat sravan hoo siraae hai ||
column3: Seeing the most beautiful form of the True Guru, his eyes are amazed. Listening to the pleasing and enchanting notes of the words of Guru, his ears feel calm and tranquil.

column2: rasanaa bisam at madh makara(n)dh ras naasikaa chakit hee subaas mahikaae hai ||
column3: Relishing the sweet elixir-like dust of the feet of the True Guru, the tongue enjoys strange bliss and pleasure. The nostrils are amazed by the sweet smell of that dust of the True Guru.

column2: komalataa seetalataa pa(n)g saraba(n)g bhe man madhukar pun anat naa dhaae hai ||335||
column3: Experiencing the calmness and tenderness of the sweet smell of the holy feet of the True Guru, all limbs of the body become stable. The black bee like mind then does not wander anywhere else and remains attached with lotus-like feet. (335)

column2: baasanaa ko baas dhoot sa(n)gat binaas kaal charan kamal gur ek Tek paiee hai ||
column3: He who has taken the refuge of the lotus-like feet of the True Guru, is freed from attraction of all other smells and involvement in the five vices.

column2: bhaijal bhiaanak lahar na biaap sakai nij ghar sa(n)paT kai dhubidhaa miTaiee hai ||
column3: The worldly waves of wants and desires cannot influence him anymore. Having engrossed himself in the Self, he has destroyed all type of duality.

column2: aan giaan dhiaan simaran bisimaran kai prem ras bas aasaa manasaa na paiee hai ||
column3: The black bee like lover of the lotus-feet of the True Guru, forgets all other type of knowledge, contemplations and incantations of meditations. He has destroyed all his wants and desires by virtue of his love for the lotus feet of the True Guru.

column2: dhuteeaa naasat ek Tek nihachal mat sahaj samaadh unaman liv laiee hai ||336||
column3: A Sikh of the Guru who is lover of the lotus feet (of the Guru) sheds his duality. He remains absorbed in the refuge of the lotus feet. In the higher spiritual state, he is absorbed in the stable contemplation of the Lord. (336)

column2: charan kamal raj masatak lepan kai bharam karam lekh sayaamataa miTaiee hai ||
column3: The application of the holy dust of the lotus-like feet of the true Guru obliterates the dross of all deeds performed in the previous births under the influence of doubts, suspicions and lack of faith.

column2: charan kamal charanaamirat maleen man kar niramal dhoot dhubidhaa miTaiee hai ||
column3: By quaffing the nectar-like elixir of the holy feet of the True Guru, the dross of the mind is dispensed and one becomes clean (of heart). He is also freed from the influence of the five evils and other dualities.

column2: charan kamal sukh sa(n)paT sahaj ghar nihachal mat ek Tek Thahiraiee hai ||
column3: Engrossed in the meditation of the holy name, one lives in abode of God. The consciousness becomes stable and in the refuge of the Lord.

column2: charan kamal gur mahimaa agaadh bodh sarab nidhaan aau sakal fal dhaiee hai ||337||
column3: The knowledge of the glory of True Guru's holy feet is limitless and vast. He is the store-house of all material goods and a perfect and complete donor. (337)

column2: charan kamal raj majan kai dhib dheh mahaa mal mootr dhaaree nira(n)kaaree keene hai(n) ||
column3: Bathing in the holy dust of the True Guru's feet, the body of an individual acquires golden hue. One who is evil of thoughts, becomes Guru-oriented and divine of temperaments.

column2: charan kamal charanaamirat nidhaan paan tiragun ateet cheet aapaa aap cheene hai(n) ||
column3: By relishing the elixir of the True Guru's feet, the mind is freed from the triple traits of maya (mammon). He then recognises his self.

column2: charan kamal nij aasan si(n)ghaasan kai tirabhavan aau tirakaal ga(n)mitaa prabeene hai(n) ||
column3: By instilling the lotus-like holy feet of the True Guru in self, I.e. mind, one becomes aware of all the three times and the three worlds.

column2: charan kamal ras ga(n)dh roop seetalataa dhuteeaa naasat ek Tek liv leene hai(n) ||338||
column3: By relishing the coolness, sweetness, fragrance and beauty of the lotus-like feet of the True Guru, the duality disappears from the mind. One remains absorbed in the refuge and support of the holy feet (of the True Guru). (338)

column2: charan kamal raj majan prataap at purab teerath koT charan saran hai ||
column3: Bathing in the holy dust of the lotus feet of the True Guru has great significance. Millions of places of pilgrimage reside in the refuge of the True Guru. One is deemed to have visited all the holy places by the touch of the dust of His holy feet.

column2: charan kamal raj majan prataap at dhevee dhev sevak hui poojat charan hai ||
column3: The glory and grandeur of the dust of True Guru's holy feet supreme. All gods and goddesses worship Him as His humble servants. (worship of all gods and goddesses lie in feet of the True Guru).

column2: charan kamal raj majan prataap at kaaran adheen keen kaaran karan hai ||
column3: The significance of bathing in the dust of the holy feet of True Guru is so great· that he who is ever under the causes, himself becomes the creator of those causes, by becoming a devoted slave of the True Guru.

column2: charan kamal raj majan prataap at patit puneet bhe taaran taran hai ||339||
column3: Importance of touching of True Guru's holy feet is so supreme that a human being badly soiled in sins of maya becomes pious in his refuge. He even becomes a ship for others to sail across the worldly ocean. (339)

column2: maanasar ha(n)s saadh sa(n)gat param ha(n)s dharam dhujaa dharamasaalaa chal aavahee ||
column3: Just as swans visit lake Mansarover, so do the righteous people with divine wisdom visit the holy congregation of Lord's loving servants/devotees.

column2: aut mukataahal agar dhuteeaa naasat it gur sabadh surat liv laavahee ||
column3: There, at Mansarover, the swans relish pearls as their food and nothing else; so do these devotees engross their minds in the holy Naam of the Lord and remains attached with His divine words.

column2: aut kheer neer niravaaro kai bakhaaneeat it gurmat dhuramat samajhaavahee ||
column3: The swans are believed to disintegrate milk in its constituents of water and milk; while here in the holy congregation, one learns about those who are Guru-oriented and self-oriented.

column2: aut bag ha(n)s ba(n)s dhubidhaa na meT sakai it kaag paag sam roop kai milaavahee ||340||
column3: The temperament of herons cannot be changed into those of swans but here in the holy congregation, those who are like filth-eating crows are transformed into holy and devoted persons through the hue of Naam blessed by the True Guru. (340)

column2: gursikh sa(n)gat milaap ko prataap chhin siv sanakaadh brahamaadhik na paavahee ||
column3: Even gods like Shiv, Brahma, Sanak etc. are unable to acquire the importance of the congregation that one achieves by keeping the company of the obedient and devoted disciples of the True Guru even for a second.

column2: simirat puraan bedh saasatr aau naadh baadh raag raaganee hoo net net kar gaavahee ||
column3: A very short while spent in the holy congregation is sung as infinite, infinite by various religious scriptures like Simritis, Purans, Vedas beside the musical instruments, and various modes of singing.

column2: dhevee dhev sarab nidhaan aau sakal fal savairag samooh sukh dhiaan dhar dhiaavahee ||
column3: All goddesses, gods, treasures, fruits and comforts of heaven sing and remember the peace that they enjoyed even with a fractional association with congregation of the saints.

column2: pooran braham satigur saavadhaan jaan gursikh sabadh surat liv laavahee ||341||
column3: The obedient disciples attach their mind and engross themselves in the words of the True Guru with singular mind considering the True Guru to be complete and perfect form of Lord. (341)

column2: rachanaa charitr chitr bisam bachitr pan kaahoo so na kouoo keeno ek hee anek hai ||
column3: Miracle of His creation is wondrous and astonishing. No human being has been created like another. Yet His light prevails in all.

column2: nipaT kapaT ghaT ghaT naT vaT naT gupat pragaT aT paT jaavadhek hai ||
column3: This world is an illusion. But every creation that is part of this entangled illusion, He, Himself is causing these wondrous acts both conspicuously and latently like a juggler.

column2: dhirasaT see dhirasaT na dharasan so dharas bachan so bachan na surat samek hai ||
column3: In this creation, no one looks alike, talks alike, thinks alike or sees alike. No one's wisdom is the same.

column2: roop rekh lekh bhekh naadh baadh naanaa bidh agam agaadh bodh braham bibek hai ||342||
column3: Living beings are of myriad forms, fortune, posture, sound and rhythm. All this is beyond comprehension and knowledge. In fact it is beyond human capability to understand the strange and wondrous creation of the Lord. (342)

column2: sat roop satigur pooran braham dhiaan sat naam satigur te paarabraham hai ||
column3: True of form, the True Guru is the embodiment of the perfect Lord. Focusing on True Guru is truly focusing on the Lord. True Guru helps us realise the Lord of Eternal Name.

column2: sat gur sabadh anaahadh braham giaan gurmukh pa(n)th sat ga(n)mitaa aga(n)m hai ||
column3: The Guru-blessed unstruck word is eternal of form and this is the means of divine knowledge and His realisation. The Guru-wise path defined by the True Guru is eternal of form, but this path is beyond reach.

column2: gur sikh saadh sa(n)g braham sathaan sat keeratan samai hui saavadhaan sam hai ||
column3: The assembly of Guru's obedient and saintly disciples is the abode of the eternal Lord. Singing His praises through Gurbani with singular mind, a devoted disciple becomes one with God, the Lord.

column2: gurmukh bhaavanee bhagat bhaau chaau sat sahaj subhaau gurmukh namo nam hai ||343||
column3: The heart of a Guru-conscious disciple of the Guru is ever filled with loving devotion and enthusiasm of His worship. Salute such a cool-natured Guru-conscious disciple again and again. (343)

column2: nira(n)kaar niraadhaar niraahaar nir bikaar ajonee akaal apara(n)par abhev hai ||
column3: The eternal form of the Lord whose embodiment is True Guru, is formless, who is bereft of all support, who has no desire of any food, who is free of all vices, free of entering wombs to take birth, who is imperishable, limitless and who cannot be fathomed.

column2: niramoh nirabair niralep niradhokh nirabhai nira(n)jan ateh par at ev hai ||
column3: He is sans attachment, animosity, free of all allurements and stigmas, fearless, uninfluenced by maya and is beyond the beyond.

column2: abigat agam agochar agaadh bodh achut alakh at achhal achhev hai ||
column3: Whose extent cannot be known, is imperceptible, beyond the senses, whose expanse is unknowable, who is ever stable, beyond perceptions, is beyond deception nor can be hurt by anyone.

column2: bisamai bisam asacharajai asacharaj mai adhabhut paramadhabhut gurdhev hai ||344||
column3: Knowing Him is most baffling, amazing and astonishing that can make anyone blissfully ecstatic. The effulgent of form the True Guru is the form of such an eternal and radiant God Lord. (344)

column2: kaaratak maas rut saradh pooranamaasee aaTh jaam saaTh gharee aaj teree baaree hai ||
column3: It is the month of Karlik, and winter season with full moon night. In these eight watches, here is your chance to meet your beloved at any time. (Guru Nanak Dev Ji was born on this day).

column2: aausar abheech bahu naik kee naikaa hui roop gun joban si(n)gaar adhikaaree hai ||
column3: Therefore, you too be the rightful person to meet the beloved Lord of myriad other female-like seekers, with your loving devotion, love, worship like beauty and adornment of youthful virtues on this auspicious moment of star configuration.

column2: chaatir chatur paaTh sevak sahelee saaTh sa(n)padhaa samagree sukh sahaj suchaaree hai ||
column3: You are alert and adept in Naam Simran, the sixty main veins of your body are your friends and in your obedience, and you are the possessor of equipoise, beauteous treasure and other items of great value.

column2: su(n)dhar ma(n)dhar subh lagan sa(n)jog bhog jeevan janam dha(n)n preetam piaaree hai ||345||
column3: In this auspicious occasion, acquiring the union of the temple-like body with the beloved Lord on the nuptial bed of the heart will make your human birth and life a blessed one. And thus you become the beloved of your dear and loving husband (God). (345)

column2: dhinakar kiran suhaat sukhadhaiee a(n)g rachat si(n)gaar abharan sakhee aai kai ||
column3: (Before the girl is married off, the bride is adorned with ornaments and jewellery) and the rays of Sun falling on her, make her look more good. Her friends come to embellish her more.

column2: piratham ubaTanaa kai sees mai malaunee mel majan usan jal niramal bhai kai ||
column3: Paste of herbs, oil and salts is rubbed on her body, the hair are massaged with scents and oil and then shampooed with lukewarm water. Her body then starts radiating like gold.

column2: kusam aves kes baasat fulel mel a(n)g aragajaa lep het upajai kai ||
column3: Adoring the hair with flowers, applying the mixture of fragranced and scented mixture on the body, the feeling of romance and love is incited.

column2: cheer chaar dharapan madh aapaa aap cheen baiThee paraja(n)k par dhaavaree na dhai kai ||346||
column3: Wearing beautiful dresses, seeing her beautiful form in the mirror, she occupies the bed of her dear husband. Then her wandering mind does not wander any more and becomes stable and restful. (346)

column2: kakahee dhai maa(n)g urajhaae surajhaae kes ku(n)kam cha(n)dhan ko tilak dhe lilaar mai ||
column3: She should comb her entangled hair and create a neat parting in her hair, apply a dot of saffron and sandalwood on her forehead.

column2: a(n)jan kha(n)jan dhirag besar karan ful baaree sees fool dhai tamol mukh dhuaar mai ||
column3: Put collyrium in her frolicsome eyes, a ring in the nose, earrings, wear dome-shaped ornament on the head and wait at the main entrance chewing betel leaf.

column2: ka(n)Th saree kapot marakat aau mukataahal baran baran fool sobhaa ur haar mai ||
column3: Wear diamond and pearl-studded necklace and adorn her heart with colourful flowers of virtuous qualities,

column2: chachar charee ka(n)kan mu(n)dhirakaa mahadhee banee  a(n)geeaa anoop chhudhrapeeTh kaT dhaar mai ||347||
column3: Wear colourful rings in her fingers, bracelets, bangles on her wrists, apply henna on her hands, wear a beautiful bodice and a black thread with trinkets around her waist. Note: All the above adornments are related to the virtues and Naam Simran of the Sikh philosophy as preached by Gurus. (347)

column2: sobhit saradh nis jagamag jot sas pratham sahelee kahai prem ras chaakheeaai ||
column3: Note: Abandon bashfulness and enjoy the love of the beloved husband at the time of meeting Him. It is a wintry night and the Moon is spreading its light all around. A friend of the holy congregation urges to obtain Guru's sermons in order to enjoy the elixir of Lord husband's love.

column2: pooran kirapaa kai terai aae hai kirapaa nidhaan  mileeaai nira(n)tar hui a(n)tar na raakheeaai ||
column3: And when the clement Lord in His complete blessings comes and rests on your bed-like heart, then meet Him without any reservations and inhibitions.

column2: charan kamal makara(n)dh ras lubhit hui man madhukar sukh sa(n)paT bhilaakheeaai ||
column3: May the frolicsome mind remain longing for the fragrant dust of the lotus feet of the Lord.

column2: joiee lajai paieeaai na pun padham dhai palak amol pria sa(n)g mukh saakheeaai ||348||
column3: Guru-conscious persons testify that any seeker bride who remains shy and bashful at the time of meeting with husband Lord, loses that rare opportunity. She is then unable to obtain the invaluable moment even after spending countless money. (348)

column2: ka(n)chan asudh jaise bhramat kuThaalee bikhai sudh bhe bhramat na paavak pragaas hai ||
column3: As impure gold when heated in a crucible, keep on moving here and there but when purified becomes stable and glitters like fire.

column2: jaise kar ka(n)kan anek mai pragaT dhun ekai ek Tek pun dhun ko binaas hai ||
column3: If many bangles are worn in one arm, they keep making noise by striking with each other but when melted and made into one become quiet and noiseless.

column2: khudhiaa kai baalak bilalaat akulaat at asathan paan kar sahaj nivaas hai ||
column3: Just as a child cries when hungry but becomes quiet and peaceful after suckling milk from his mother's breasts.

column2: taise maiaa bhramat bhramat chatur ka(n)uT dhaavai gur upadhes nihachal gireh padh baas hai ||349||
column3: Similarly a human mind engulfed in worldly attachments and love keeps on wandering all over. But by the sermons of the True Guru, he becomes stable and calm. (349)

column2: jaise dheep dhipat bhavan ujiaaro hot sagal samagree gireh pragaT dhikhaat hai ||
column3: Just as a house is lit up when a lamp is lighted in it, it makes everything visible clearly;

column2: ot pot jot hot kaaraj baachhat sidh aana(n)dh binodh sukh sahaj bihaat hai ||
column3: With light spreading all around, all the tasks can be accomplished with ease and the time passes in peace and happiness;

column2: laalach lubhai ras lubit naanaa pata(n)g bujhat hee a(n)dhakaar bhe akulaat hai ||
column3: Just as many moths are enamoured by the light of the lamp but are distressed when the light goes off and darkness descends;

column2: taise bidhamaan jaaneeaai na mahimaa mahaa(n)t a(n)tireechh bhe paachhe log pachhutaat hai ||350||
column3: Just as those alive do not value a lamp until it turns off, similarly people repent and feel sad for not taking advantage of the presence of the True Guru after they have gone. They do not bother to know the greatness of the True Guru. (350)

column2: jaise dheep dhipat mahaatamai na jaanai kouoo bujhat hee a(n)dhakaar bhaTakat raat hai ||
column3: Just as the significance of a lit lamp is not appreciated by anyone, but when it is extinguished, one has to wander in the darkness.

column2: jaise dhaooram aa(n)gan achhit mahimaa na jaanai kaTat hee chhaa(n)h baiThabe kau bilalaat hai ||
column3: Just as a tree in the courtyard is not appreciated, but when felled or uprooted one longs for its shade.

column2: jaise raajaneet bikhai chain hui chatur ka(n)uT chhatr ddaalaa chaal bhe jatr katr jaat hai ||
column3: Just as enforcement of law and order of the kingdom ensures peace and prosperity everywhere, but chaos prevails when enforcement is compromised.

column2: taise gursikh saadh sa(n)gam jugat jag a(n)tireechh bhe paachhe log pachhutaat hai ||351||
column3: So is the unique opportunity for the Sikhs of the Guru to meet with the saintly True Guru. Once missed, everyone repents. (351)

column2: jaupai jaanai anoop roop dhiragan kai dhekheeat lochan achhat a(n)dh kaahe na pekhahee ||
column3: If we believe that we see the beauty of the nature because of our eyes, then why can't a blind person who has no eyes, enjoy the same spectacle?

column2: jau jaanai sabadh ras rasanaa bakhaaneeat jihabaa achhat kat ga(n)ug na sarekh hee ||
column3: If we believe that we speak sweet words because of our tongue, then why can't a dumb person with his tongue intact speak these words?

column2: jaupai jaane raag naadh suneeat sravan kai sravan sahat kiau baharo bisekh hee ||
column3: If we accept that we hear sweet music because of ears, then why can't a deaf person hear it with his ears intact?

column2: nain jihavaa sravan ko na kachhooaai basai sabadh surat so alakh lekh lekhahee ||352||
column3: Eyes, tongue and ears have no power of their own; only with words, can they enable us to enjoy what we see, speak or hear. Similarly, engaging with the words of the Guru and meditating on Naam, is it possible to realize and enjoy the Gurus love.

column2: jananee jatan kar jugavai jaThar raakhai taa te pi(n)dd pooran hui sut janamat hai ||
column3: Just as a pregnant woman takes all possible care of herself during her pregnancy and on completion of the period gives birth to a baby boy;

column2: bahurio akhaadh khaadh sa(n)jam sahit rahai taahee te pai peeat arog pan pat hai ||
column3: Then she observes and controls her eating habits meticulously and rigidly that helps the young child to grow healthy by consuming his mother's milk.

column2: mal mootr dhaar ko bichaar na bichaarai chit karai pratipaal baal tuoo tan gat hai ||
column3: The mother cares not about all the filth of the child and brings him up to give him a healthy body.

column2: taise arabhak roop sikh hai sa(n)saar madh sree gur dhiaal kee dhiaa kai san gat hai ||353||
column3: So is a disciple (Sikh), like a child in this world who like the mother is blessed by the Guru with Naam Simran that ultimately emancipates him. (353)

column2: jaise tau jananee khaan paan kau sa(n)jam karai taate sut rahai nirabighan arog jee ||
column3: Just as a would-be mother takes care of what she eats so that the child in her womb remains healthy.

column2: jaise raajaneet reet chakravai chaita(n)n roop taa te nihachi(n)t nirabhai basat log jee ||
column3: Just as a good ruler remains alert in the enforcement of law and order so as to keep his subjects safe, fearless of any harm and happy.

column2: jaise kareeaa samu(n)dhr bohith mai saavadhaan taa te paar paha(n)uchat pathik asog jee ||
column3: Just as a sailor is ever alert while sailing his boat in the ocean so that he takes all his passengers safely to other shore.

column2: taise gur pooran braham giaan dhiaan liv taa(n) te niradhokh sikh nij padh jog jee ||354||
column3: Similarly, the God-like True Guru is ever alert to bless his loving and devoted servant with knowledge and ability to focus his mind in Lord's name. And thus a Sikh of the Guru keeps himself free of all vices and becomes eligible for higher spiritual state. (354)

column2: jananee suteh jau dhikaar maar piaar karai piaar jhirakaar dhekh sakat na aan ko ||
column3: The mother scolds and spanks the child but cannot tolerate anyone else scolding, spanking and loving him.

column2: jananee ko piaar aau dhikaar upakaar het aan ko dhikaar piaar hai bikaar praan ko ||
column3: Mothers scolding and spanking of the child is for his benefit but when someone else does it, it is indeed painful.

column2: jaise jal agan mai parai boodd marai jarai taise kirapaa krop aan banitaa agiaan ko ||
column3: (Although water is cold and fire is hot) falling in water drowns while jumping into fire burns a person to death. Similarly it is foolish to believe on the kindness or anger of another woman. (It is utter foolishness to lay faith on any other god/goddess or so-called saint; leaving the True Guru).

column2: taise gur sikhan ko jugavat jatan kai dhubidhaa na biaapai prem param nidhaan ko ||355||
column3: Just like mother, the True Guru makes every effort and attaches the Sikhs in the love of the Supreme Lord, the source of everything. And thus they are never infatuated or attracted by the love or anger of any god/goddess or spurious saint. (355)

column2: jaise kar gahat sarap sut pekh maataa kahai na pukaar fusalai ur ma(n)dd hai ||

column2: az khhudhaa dhoor asat har koo khhudha-numaasat || 83 ||
column3: A person who is stuck in his self ego is driven farther and farther away from Waaheguru. (83)

column2: keesat goyaa mushat khhaak besh neesat
column3: O Goyaa! What is your existence in life?  It is no more than a handful of dust;

column2: aan ham a(n)dhar akhhatiaar khhesh neesat || 84 ||
column3: And, even that is not under your control; The body that we claim to own is not under our control either. (84)

column2: hak k haphataadho dho milat aafareedh
column3: Akaalpurakh created seventy two communities,

column2: phirakai naajee azeehaan bar guzeedh || 85 ||
column3: Out of which, He designated the Naajee community as the most elite. (85)

column2: phirakai naajee bidhaan be-ishatabaah
column3: We should consider the Naajee (who is considered above and beyond the cycles of transmigration) community, without any doubt,

column2: hasat haphataadho dho milat raa panaeh || 86 ||
column3: As the shelter for the seventy two clans. (86)

column2: maradhamaanash har yake paakeezaa tar
column3: Every member of this Najee community is sacred;

column2: khhooba-roo o khhooba-khhoo o khhusha-seear || 87 ||
column3: Beautiful and handsome, well mannered with a noble disposition. (87)

column2: pesh shaan juz yaadh hak manazoor neesat
column3: To these folks, nothing else but the remembrance of Akaalpurakh is acceptable;

column2: g(h)air haraph ba(n)dhagee dhasatoor neesat || 88 ||
column3: And, they do not have any tradition or mannerism other than the recitation of the words of prayer. (88)

column2: meechakadh az haraph shaan ka(n)dho nabaat
column3: Utter sweetness oozes out of their words and conversation,

column2: baaradh az har mooi shaan aab hayaat || 89 ||
column3: And, divine elixir is showered from every hair of theirs. (89)

column2: phaarig(h) a(n)dh az bug(h)zo keenaa o z hasadh
column3: They are above and beyond any form of jealousy, hostility or enmity;

column2: bar namee-aaidh az eshaan phial badh || 90 ||
column3: They never commit any sinful acts. (90)

column2: har kase raa izato huramat kuna(n)dh
column3: They extend respect and honor to every one;

column2: muphalase raa saahib dhaualat kuna(n)dh || 91 ||
column3: And, they help poor and needy to become rich and opulent. (91)

column2: muradhaa raa aabi-haivaan meedhiha(n)dh
column3: They bless the dead souls with divine nectar;

column2: har dhile pazamuradhaa raa jaan meedhiha(n)dh || 92 ||
column3: They bestow new and rejuvenated life to withered and demoralized minds. (92)

column2: sabaz meesaaza(n)dh chob khhushak raa
column3: They can transform dry wood into green twigs;

column2: booe meebakhasha(n)dh ra(n)g mushak raa || 93 ||
column3: They also can convert a stinking odor into scented musk. (93)

column2: jumalaa asharaaph a(n)dh dhar zaato siphaat
column3: All these well-intentioned persons possess noble personal qualities;

column2: taalib zaat a(n)dh khhudh ham aan zaat || 94 ||
column3: They are all seekers of Waaheguru's Entity; in fact, they are just like Him (are His image). (94)

column2: khhooi shaan ilamo adhab raa muzahar asat
column3: Learning and literature emerges (spontaneously) from their behavior;

column2: rooi shaan rauashan z mihar anavar asat || 95 ||
column3: And, their faces radiate like the glowing divinely sun. (95)

column2: milat shaan kauam masakeenaan bavadh
column3: Their clan consists of a group of humble, meek and gentle persons;

column2: har dho aalam shaik ieenaan bavadh || 96 ||
column3: And they have devotees in both the worlds; People in both the worlds believe in them. (96)

column2: kauam misakeen kauam maradhaan khhudhaa-sat
column3: This group of people is the community of gentle and humble souls, a community of God's men.

column2: e'een hamaa phaanee v uoo dhaim bakaasat || 97 ||
column3: Every thing that we see is destructible, but Akaalpurakh is the only One that prevails perpetually and is Imperishable. (97)

column2: suhabat shaan khhaak raa akaseer karadh
column3: Their company and association transformed even the dust to an effective cure.

column2: lutaph shaan bar har dhile taaseer karadh || 98 ||
column3: Their blessings effectively impressed every heart. (98)

column2: har k ba-eshaan nasheenadh yak dhame
column3: Anyone who enjoys their company just once even for a moment,

column2: rooz pharadhaa raa kujaa dhaaradh g(h)men || 99 ||
column3: He, then, does not have to be apprehensive about the day of reckoning. (99)

column2: aan ch dhar sadha-saalaa umarash nabhayaaphat
column3: A person who could not attain much in spite of hundreds of years of life,

column2: suhabat shaan hamachoo khhurasheedhash bitaakhhat || 100 ||
column3: Shone like a sun when he joined the company of  these people. (100)

column2: maa k az ihasaan shaan sharami(n)dhaa-em
column3: We are obligated and owe them a debt of gratitude,

column2: ba(n)dhai ihasaan shaan raa ba(n)dhaa em || 101 ||
column3: We are, in fact, persons/products of their favors and kindness. (101)

column2: sadh hazaaraan hamachoo man kurabaan shaan
column3: Millions like me are willing to sacrifice themselves for these nobilities;

column2: hab ch goim kam bavadh dhar shaan shaan || 102 ||
column3: No matter how much I say in their honor and praise, it will be inadequate. (102)

column2: shaan shaan beeroo(n) bavadh az guphatagoo
column3: Their honor and appreciation is beyond any words or expression;

column2: jaamai shaan paak az shusato shoo || 103 ||
column3: The style (attire) of their life is cleaner and chaste than any amount of washing or rinsing. (103)

column2: dhaan yakeen taa cha(n)dh ieen dhuniaa bavadh
column3: Believe me ! How long is this world going to last? Only for a short time;

column2: aakhharish kaar too baa maualaa bavadh || 104 ||
column3: Ultimately, we have to develop and maintain a relationship with the Almighty. (104)

column2: pas z aval kun hadhees shaeh raa
column3: Now you indulge yourself in the stories and discourses of (that) King, the Waaheguru.

column2: pairavee kun haadhe'ee ieen raeh raa || 105 ||
column3: And, follow the Guide who shows you the direction (of life). (105)

column2: taa too ham yaabee muraadh umar raa
column3: So that your life's hopes and ambitions are fulfilled;

column2: lazate yaabee z shauak kibareeaa || 106 ||
column3: And, you can have the pleasure of the savor of the devotion for Akaalpurakh.(106)

column2: jaahil aana-jaa saahibi-dhil meeshavadh
column3: (With His grace) even s stupid person can become an intellectual and enlightened;

column2: g(h)rak dhariaao basaahil meeshavadh || 107 ||
column3: And, a person drowning in deep waters of a river can reach the banks. (107)

column2: naa kis aan jaa aariph kaamil shavadh
column3: An insignificant person can become fully enlightened,

column2: yaadh maualaa har k raa haasil shavadh || 108 ||
column3: When he engages himself in the remembrance of Waaheguru. (108)

column2: e'een asab taajasat bar apharaak kas
column3: A person is being adorned, as if, with a crown of learning and honor on his head,

column2: aan k g(h)aaphil neesat az hak yak naphas || 109 ||
column3: Who does not become negligent even for one moment in remembering Akaalpurakh. (109)

column2: har kase raa neesat ieen dhaualat naseeb
column3: This treasure is not in the lot of everyone;

column2: dharadh shaan raa neesat g(h)air az hak tabeeb || 110 ||
column3: The cure for their pain is no one else other than the Waaheguru, the doctor. (110)

column2: dhaarooi har dharadh raa yaadh khhudhaasat
column3: Remembrance of Akaalpurakh is the cure-all for every malady and pain;

column2: zaan k dhar har haal hak dhaaradh ravaa-sat || 111 ||
column3: In whatever condition or state He keeps us, should be acceptable. (111)

column2: murashadh kaamil hamaa raa aarazoo
column3: It is the wish and desire of everyone to seek a perfect Guru;

column2: g(h)air murashadh kas na yaabadh reh badhoo || 112 ||
column3: Without such a mentor, no one can reach the Almighty. (112)

column2: raaha-ravaan raa raeh biseeaar aamadhaa
column3: There are several paths for the travelers to traverse;

column2: kaaravaan raa raeh dharakaar aamadhaa || 113 ||
column3: But what they need is the path of the caravan. (113)

column2: dham badham dhar zikar maualaa haazar a(n)dh
column3: They are always alert and prepared for the remembrance of Akaalpurakh;

column2: khhesh manazooro khhudhaa raa naazir a(n)dh || 114 ||
column3: They are acceptable to Him and they are His observers, on-lookers and spectators. (114)

column2: murashadh kaamil hamaan baanashadh hamaan
column3: A perfect Satguru is the one and the only one,

column2: kaz kalaamash booi hak aadh ayaan || 115 ||
column3: Whose conversation and Gurbaanee emits the Divine fragrance. (115)

column2: har k aaidh pesh eshaan zaraa vaar
column3: Anyone who comes in front of such persons (Perfect Gurus) in humility like a dust particle,

column2: zoodh garadhadh hamachoo mihar noor baar || 116 ||
column3: He, soon, becomes capable to shower radiance like that of sun. (116)

column2: zi(n)dhagee ieenasat be chuno chiraa
column3: That life is worth living that, without any delay or excuses,

column2: biguzaradh ieen umar dhar yaadh khhudhaa || 117 ||
column3: Is spent in the memory of the Providence in this lifetime. (117)

column2: khhudha-prasatee kaar naadhaan aamadhaa
column3: To indulge in self-propaganda is the work of stupid people;

column2: hak prasatee zaat ieemaan aamadhaa || 118 ||
column3: While to get engaged in meditation is the characteristic of the faithful. (118)

column2: har dhame g(h)falat bavadh marag azeem
column3: Negligence of every moment of not remembering Him is like a huge death;

column2: hak nigaeh dhaaradh z shaitaan razeem || 119 ||
column3: May God, with His eye, save us from the Satan of Hell. (119)

column2: aan k roozo shab ba-yaadhash mubatalaa-sat
column3: Anyone who is (constantly) imbued in remembering Him day and night,

column2: e'een mataa a(n)dhar dhukaan aaualeeaa-sat || 120 ||
column3: (Knows very well that) This wealth, the memory of Akaalpurakh, is available only at the store (congregation) of saintly persons. (120)

column2: kihatareen ba(n)dhai dharagaeh shaan
column3: Even the lowest person in their court

column2: bihatar asat az mihataraan ieen jahaan || 121 ||
column3: Is superior than the so called most respectable stalwarts of this world. (121)

column2: bas bazurag(h)aan koo phidhai raeh shaan
column3: Many wise and experienced persons are enamored and are prepared to make sacrifices on their paths,

column2: suramai chashamam z khhaak raeh shaan || 122 ||
column3: And, the dust of their paths is like a collyrium for my eyes. (122)

column2: hamachuneen pi(n)dhaar khhudh raa aai azeez
column3: You, too, my dear youngster! Consider yourself just like this,

column2: taa shavee aai jaan man maradh tameez || 123 ||
column3: So that, my dear! You, too, can transform yourself into a pious and saintly person. (123)

column2: saahibaan raa ba(n)dhaa bisaar aamadhaa
column3: These masters, the noble souls, have numerous followers and devotees;

column2: ba(n)dhaa raa baa-ba(n)dhagee kaar aamadhaa || 124 ||
column3: The main task assigned to each and every one of us is only to meditate. (124)

column2: mas turaa baidh k khhidhamatagaar shaan
column3: Therefore, you should become their follower and a devotee;

column2: baashee o haragiz nabhabaashee baar shaan || 125 ||
column3: But you should never be liability for them. (125)

column2: garacheh yaaree-dheh na g(h)air az saalake-sat
column3: Even though, there is no one else without them to connect us to the Almighty,

column2: lek kar g(h)uphatan chuneen aaibe base-sat || 126 ||
column3: Still, for them to make such a claim would be a transgression. (126)

column2: zaraa raa dheedham k khhurasheedh jahaan
column3: I realized that even a small particle became the sun for the whole world,

column2: shudh z phaiz suhabat saahiba-dhilaan || 127 ||
column3: With the blessings of the association with the saintly persons. (127)

column2: keesat saahibi-dhil k hak bisanaasadhash
column3: Who is that person with a great heart who can recognize the Akaalpurakh,

column2: kaz lakaish shauak hak mee-baaradhash || 128 ||
column3: And whose face (constantly) radiates His splendor ? (128)

column2: suhabat shaan shauak hak bakhhashadh turaa
column3: The company of such noble souls blesses you with the Devotion for the Lord,

column2: az kitaab hak sabak bakhhashadh turaa || 129 ||
column3: And it is their company too that gives you spiritual lessons from the holy book. (129)

column2: zaraa raa khhurasheedh anavar mee-kuna(n)dh
column3: They, the noble souls, can transform even a small particles into a sprightly sun;

column2: khhaak raa az hak munavar mee-kuna(n)dh || 130 ||
column3: And, it is them who can sparkle even the common dust into the Light of Truth. (130)

column2: chasham too khhaakee v dhar vai noor hak
column3: Even though your eye is made of dust, still it has the Divine radiance,

column2: a(n)dharoonash chaar soo v nahu tabak || 131 ||
column3: It also contains all the four directions, east, west, south and north, and the nine heavens. (131)

column2: khhidhamat shaan ba(n)dhageei hak bavadh
column3: Any service performed for them, the saintly persons, is the worship of Waaheguru;

column2: kaan kabool kaadhar mutalik bavadh || 132 ||
column3: Because they are the ones who are acceptable to the Omnipotent. (132)

column2: ba(n)dhagee kun jaan k uoo baashadh kabool
column3: You, too, should meditate so that you be acceptable before the Akaalpurakh.

column2: kadhar uoo raa kai bidhaanadh har jahool || 133 ||
column3: How can any stupid person appreciate His invaluable worth. (133)

column2: hasat kaar roozo shab dhar yaadh uoo
column3: The only task we should be engaged day and night is to remember Him;

column2: yak naphas khhaalee namee baashadh azoo || 134 ||
column3: Not even one moment should be spared without His meditation and prayers. (134)

column2: chasham shaan rauashan z dheedhaar alaah
column3: Their eyes are glistened because of His Divine glimpse,

column2: dhar libaas a(n)dhara-gadhaa o baadhashaeh || 135 ||
column3: They may be in the guise of a mendicant, but they are the kings. (135)

column2: baadhashaahee aan k uoo dhaim bavadh
column3: Only that kingdom is considered a real kingdom that lasts for ever,

column2: hamachoo jaat paak hak kaim bavadh || 136 ||
column3: And, like the pure and chaste Nature of God, should be eternal. (136)

column2: rasam shaan aaieen dharaveshee bavadh
column3: Their custom and tradition is mostly that of mendicants;

column2: as khhudhaa o baahamaa khhesee bavadh || 137 ||
column3: They are the lineage and the scions of Waaheguru, and they have intimacy and familiarity with all. (137)

column2: har gadhaa raa ize jaahe meedhiha(n)dh
column3: The Akaalpurakh blesses every ascetic with honor and status;

column2: dhaualat be-ishatabaahee meedhiha(n)dh || 138 ||
column3: Without any doubt, He also bestows (everyone) with wealth and treasures. (138)

column2: naakasaan raa aariph kaamil kuna(n)dh
column3: They can transform trivial and paltry persons into perfectly knowledgeable ones;

column2: be-dhilaan raa saahibi-dhil meekuna(n)dh || 139 ||
column3: And, the demoralized ones into courageous persons and masters of their destiny. (139)

column2: khhudha-prasatee az miaan baradhaashata(n)dh
column3: They eject their vanities from their inner self;

column2: tukhham hak dhar kishat dhilahaa kaashata(n)dh || 140 ||
column3: And, they sow seeds of Truth, the Lord, in the field-like hearts of the people. (140)

column2: khheshatan raa heech mee dhaana(n)dh shaan
column3: They always consider themselves insignificant and lowlier than others;

column2: haraph hak raa roozo shab khhaana(n)dh shaan || 141 ||
column3: And, they are absorbed in the meditation of Naam of Waaheguru day and night. (141)

column2: taa kujaa aauasaaph maradhaan khhudhaa-sat
column3: How much can I praise the God's men, the saints and the Mahaatamaas?

column2: az hazaaraan gar yake goim ravaa-sat || 142 ||
column3: It would be just wonderful if I could describe even one of their thousands of  virtues. (142)

column2: hamachuneen maradhum bajoo kaan keesata(n)dh
column3: You, too, should try to find such noble persons (What kind of persons?) who are alive for ever;

column2: dheegaraan muradha(n)dh ieehaan zeesata(n)dh || 143 ||
column3: The rest of them are apparently alive but are just like dead  bodies. (143)

column2: zeesatan raa maanee dhaanee keh cheesat
column3: Do you understand the meaning of 'being alive' ?

column2: aai khhushaa umare k dhar yaadhash bazeesat || 144 ||
column3: Only that life is worth living that is spent in remembering the Akaalpurakh. (144)

column2: maradh aariph zi(n)dhaa az iraphaan uoo-sat
column3: The enlightened persons are alive only because of the knowledge of the mysteries of God's attributes;

column2: niamat har dho jahaan dhar khhaanai uoo-sat || 145 ||
column3: (They know) that He has and can shower blessings of both of the worlds in His house. (145)

column2: maane'ee ieen zi(n)dhagee yaadh khhudhaa-sat
column3: The main purpose of this life is to (constantly) remember Akaalpurakh;

column2: kaz tuphailash zi(n)dhaa jaan aaualeeaa-sat || 146 ||
column3: The saints and prophets live only with this motive. (146)

column2: zikar uoo bar har zabaan goyaa shudh
column3: A mention of them is on every living tongue;

column2: har dho aalam raeh hak jooyaa shudhaa || 147 ||
column3: And, both the worlds are seekers of His path. (147)

column2: jumalaa mee-khhaana(n)dh zikar zulajalaal
column3: Everyone meditates the awe-inspiring splendid Waaheguru,

column2: aai zahe keelo zahe pharakhha(n)dhaa kaal || 148 ||
column3: Only then such a meditation is auspicious and such a discourse propitious. (148)

column2: keelo kaale gar barai hak bavadh
column3: If you want to converse and describe the Truth,

column2: az barai kaadhar mutalik bavadh || 149 ||
column3: That is possible only to discourse the Omnipotent. (149)

column2: yaaphat ieen saramaayai umar najeeb
column3: Such an asset and the treasure of meditation for a spiritual life

column2: hasat a(n)dhar suhabat eshaan naseeb || 150 ||
column3: Was blessed through association and the company they kept with the saintly persons. (150)

column2: aan ravaa baashadh dhigar manazoor neesat
column3: Any such treasure is not acceptable to them, and they do not like any thing other than the truth;

column2: g(h)r haraph raasatee dhasatoor neesat || 151 ||
column3: It is not their tradition to speak any words but the words of truth. (151)

column2: saadh sa(n)gat naam shaan dhar hi(n)dhaveesat
column3: In Hindi language, they are called the 'Saadh Sangat',

column2: e'een hamaa taareeph shaan aai maualaveesat || 152 ||
column3: O Maulvee ! All this is in their praise; and all this defines them. (152)

column2: suhabat eshaan bavadh lutaph khhudhaa
column3: The attainment of their company happens only with His blessings;

column2: taa naseeb kas shavadh ieen roo-namaa || 153 ||
column3: And, only with His grace, such persons are revealed. (153)

column2: har kase ieen dhaualat jaaveedh yaaphat
column3: Anyone who is fortunate enough to have obtained this eternal wealth,

column2: zi(n)dhage'ee umar raa umeedh yaaphat || 154 ||
column3: One may assume then that he has become full of hope for the duration of his whole life. (154)

column2: e'een hamaa phaanee v aan baakee bidhaan
column3: All these, the wealth and the life, are perishable, but they are eternal;

column2: jaam ishak paak raa saakee bidhaan || 155 ||
column3: Consider them as bartenders who are serving glasses full of divine devotion.  (155)

column2: har ch hasat az suhabat eshaan bavadh
column3: Whatever is seemingly apparent in this world is all because of their company;

column2: kaz taphailash jumalaa aabaadhaa bavadh || 156 ||
column3: It is their grace that we see all the habitation and prosperity here. (156)

column2: e'een hamaa aabaadhee az lutaph khhudhaa-sat
column3: All these habitations (of living beings) are the result of the blessings of Waaheguru;

column2: g(h)falat az vai yak naphas marago japhaa sat || 157 ||
column3: To neglect Him even for one moment is equivalent to pain and death. (157)

column2: suhabat shaan haasal ieen zi(n)dhageesat
column3: To achieve an association with them, the noble persons, is the cornerstone of this life;

column2: zi(n)dhagee ieen zi(n)dhagee ieen ba(n)dhagee-sat || 158 ||
column3: That is life, that is indeed life which is spent in meditating His Naam. (158)

column2: gar too meekhhaahee k maradh hak shavee
column3: If you wish to become Waaheguru's true devotee,

column2: aariph uoo kaamil mutalik shavee || 159 ||
column3: Then, you should become knowledgeable and enlightened about the perfect Entity. (159)

column2: suhabat shaan keemeeaa baashadh turaa
column3: Their company is like a cure-all for you;

column2: taa cheh meekhhaahee ravaa baashadh turaa || 160 ||
column3: Then, whatever you wish shall be appropriate. (160)

column2: e'een hamaa koo saahib jaan aamadha(n)dh
column3: All this breathing and living world that we see

column2: az barai suhabat shaan aamadha(n)dh || 161 ||
column3: Is only because of the company of the noble souls. (161)

column2: zi(n)dhage'ee shaan ziphaiz sahubat asat
column3: The existing lives of those living beings is the result of the company of saintly persons;

column2: suhabat shaan aait pur rahimat asat || 162 ||
column3: And, the company of such noble persons is the proof of the kindness and compassion of Akaalpurakh. (162)

column2: har kase raa suhabat shaan baidhash
column3: Everyone, in fact, needs their company;

column2: taa z dhil akadh guhar bikushaidhash || 163 ||
column3: So that they could unravel the chain of pearls (noble aspects) from their hearts. (163)

column2: saahib ga(n)jeenaiee a be-khhabar
column3: O naive! You are the master of priceless treasure;

column2: lek zaan ga(n)je turaa nabhabavadh khhabar || 164 ||
column3: But alas! You have no realization of that hidden treasure. (164)

column2: kai azaan ga(n)je ba-yaabee italaa
column3: How can you find out that invaluable treasure

column2: a(n)dharoon kuphal choo(n) baashadh mataa || 165 ||
column3: As to what kind of wealth is hidden inside the vault. (165)

column2: pas turaa laazim bavadh jooiee kuleedh
column3: Therefore, it is essential for you to strive to find the key to the treasure,

column2: taa ba-beenee ga(n)j khhupheeaa raa padheedh || 166 ||
column3: So that you can have a clear realization of this covert, mysterious and valuable repository. (166)

column2: kuphal bikushaa az kuleedh naam hak
column3: You should use the Naam of Waaheguru as the key to open this hidden wealth;

column2: az kitaab ga(n)j makhhaphee khhaan sabak || 167 ||
column3: And, learn the lessons from the Book of this hidden treasure, the Granth. (167)

column2: e'een kuleedh naam pesh shaan bavadh
column3: This key is found (only) with the saintly persons,

column2: maraham dhilahai reshe jaan bavadh || 168 ||
column3: And, this key serves as the ointment of lacerated hearts and lives. (168)

column2: choo(n) kase raa ieen kuleedh aaidh ba-dhasat
column3: Anyone who can get hold of this key

column2: saahib ga(n)jeenaa baashadh har k hasat || 169 ||
column3: He may be anyone, he can become the master of this treasure. (169)

column2: ga(n)j raa choo(n) yaaphataa joyai ga(n)j
column3: When the seeker of the treasure does find his goal,

column2: gashat phaarig az hamaa tashaveesho ra(n)j || 170 ||
column3: Then consider that he has been salvaged from all worries and anxieties. (170)

column2: aan ham az maradhaan hak shudh aai shapheek
column3: O my friend ! That person has joined the group of (true) devotees of God,

column2: aan k raahe yaaphat dhar kooi rapheek || 171 ||
column3: Who has discovered the direction to the streets of the Beloved Friend. (171)

column2: suhabat shaan zaraa raa choo(n) maeh karadh
column3: Their association transformed an insignificant dust particle to a shining moon.

column2: har gadhaa raa suhabat shaan shaeh karadh || 172 ||
column3: Again, it was their company that transformed every beggar into a king. (172)

column2: rahimat hak baadh bar aauazai shaan
column3: May Akaalpurakh bless their disposition with His grace;

column2: bar pidhar bar maadhare ibanai shaan || 173 ||
column3: And, also on their parents and children. (173)

column2: har k shaan raa dheedh hak raa dheedhaa asat
column3: Whosoever gets a chance to see them, consider that they have seen the Almighty God;

column2: khhush gul az baag(h) muhabat cheedhaa asat || 174 ||
column3: And that he has been able to get a glimpse of a beautiful flower out of the garden of love. (174)

column2: gul z baag(h) maaraphat bara-cheedhan asat
column3: The association with such noble persons is like taking a beautiful flower out of the garden of divine knowledge;

column2: dheedhan eshaan khhudhaa raa dheedhan asat || 175 ||
column3: And, a sight of such saints is like getting a glimpse of Akaalpurakh. (175)

column2: mushakil aamadh dheedhan hak raa biaan
column3: It is difficult to describe the 'glimpse' of Waaheguru;

column2: meedhihadh ieen jumalaa raa kudharat nishaan || 176 ||
column3: His powers are reflected in the entire Nature that He has created. (176)

column2: az tuphail shaan khhudhaa raa dheedhaa-am
column3: With their kindness, I have seen a glimpse of Akaalpurakh;

column2: gul z baag(h) maaraphat bar cheedhaa-am || 177 ||
column3: And, with their grace, I have selected a lively flower from the Divine Garden. (177)

column2: dheedhan hak maane'ee dhaaradh shareeph
column3: Even to think of getting a glimpse of Akaalpurakh is indeed a sacred intention;

column2: man ni-am ieen jumalaa aan zaat lateef || 178 ||
column3: Goya says, "I am nothing! "ll this, including the above thought, is due to His abstract and mysterious Entity." (178)

column2: har k uoo dhaanisat ieen haraph tamaam
column3: Whosoever has understood this complete message (word),

column2: yaaphat uoo aan ga(n)j makhhaphee raa makaam || 179 ||
column3: As if he has discovered the location of the hidden treasure. (179)

column2: maane'ee hak soorate dhaaradh nikoo-sat
column3: The reality of Waaheguru has an extremely attractive reflection;

column2: surat hak surat maradhaan uoo-sat || 180 ||
column3: The picture of Akaalpurakh is (can be seen) in His own men and women, the saintly persons. (180)

column2: khhalavat eshaan bavadh dhar a(n)juman
