column3: They feel they are in seclusion even when they are in the company of groups of people, the congregations;

column2: vasaph eshaan bar zubaan maradho zan || 181 ||
column3: Praises of their glory are on the tongues of everyone. (181)

column2: zeen khhabar vaakiph kase baashadh k uoo
column3: Only that person can be cognizant of this mystery,

column2: dhaaradh az shauak muhabat g(h)uphatag(h)oo || 182 ||
column3: Who talks and discusses about the devotion for Akaalpurakh with enthusiasm. (182)

column2: shauak maualaa-ash girebaan geer shudh
column3: Anyone whose enthusiastic devotion for Waaheguru becomes a necklace (garland) for his neck,

column2: naakase ham saahib tadhabeer shudh || 183 ||
column3: Even though he, being a lowly person, becomes wise and sagacious. (183)

column2: shauak maualaayat choo(n) baashadh dhasatageer
column3: When the enthusiasm of devotion for God becomes your supporter,

column2: zaraa garadhadh rashak khhurasheedh muneer || 184 ||
column3: Then even a particle of dust desires to emulate (and becomes) a bright sun. (184)

column2: basak hak meebaaradh az g(h)uphataar shaan
column3: When they talk, they shower (words of) the nectar of Truth,

column2: dheedhaahaa rauashan shudh az dheedhaar shaan || 185 ||
column3: With their glimpse, the eyes become more bright and soothed. (185)

column2: roozo shab baasha(n)dh dhar zikarash mudhaam
column3: They keep meditating on the Naam of Waaheguru day and night;

column2: dhar libaas dhunayavee maradh tamaam || 186 ||
column3: Even in the worldly guise, living in this world, they become perfect human beings. (186)

column2: baa hamaa az jumalaa aazaadha(n)dh shaan
column3: With everything around them, they are independent and are immune to the effects of these material distractions;

column2: dhar hamaa haal az khhudhaa shaadha(n)dh shaan || 187 ||
column3: They are always satisfied and pleased under the Will of Akaalpurakh. (187)

column2: dhar libaas dhunayaveen v rasam dheen
column3: Even they are dressed in worldly clothes, their tradition and practice is religious.

column2: hamachoo esaan saane'ee dheegar mabeen || 188 ||
column3: There is no one like them in this world. (188)

column2: ham chunaan dhar yaadh hak dhaara(n)dh dhasat
column3: They are starkly steady, firm and adept in the memory of Waaheguru,

column2: hak shanaaso hak pasa(n)dho hak prasat || 189 ||
column3: They appreciate and recognize Him, are dedicated to the Truth and also worship the Truth. (189)

column2: dhar libaas dhunayavee sar taa kadham
column3: Even though they are seen clad in worldly guise from head to toe,

column2: beenee vaa g(h)aaphil nabhabeenee neem dham || 190 ||
column3: You will never find them to be negligent of remembering Waaheguru even for half a moment. (190)

column2: aan khhudhai paak shaan raa paak karadh
column3: The chaste Akaalpurakh transforms them into pure and holy beings,

column2: gar cheh jisam shaan zi-mushat khhaak karadh || 191 ||
column3: Even though their body is made up of just a fistful of dust. (191)

column2: e'een vajoodh khhaak paak az yaadh uoo-sat
column3: This human body made of dust becomes sacred with His remembrance;

column2: zaan k eshaan mazahar buniaadh uoo-sat || 192 ||
column3: Because it is the manifestation of the foundation (personality) bestowed by Akaalpurakh. (192)

column2: rasam shaan aaieen dhiladhaaree bavadh
column3: It is their custom to remember the Almighty;

column2: dhar hamaa haal az khhudhaa yaaree bavadh || 193 ||
column3: And, it is their tradition to always generate love and devotion for Him. (193)

column2: har kase raa kai naseeb ieen dhaualat asat
column3: How can every one be blessed with such a treasure?'

column2: dhaualat jaaveedh a(n)dhar suhabat asat || 194 ||
column3: This non-perishable wealth is available only through their company. (194)

column2: e'een hamaa az suhabat maradhaan uoosat
column3: All these (material goods) are the result of the blessings of their company;

column2: dhaualat har dho jahaan dhar shaan uoosat || 195 ||
column3: And, the wealth of both the worlds is in their praise and honor. (195)

column2: suhabat shaan napheeaa biseeaar aavuradh
column3: An association with them is extremely profitable;

column2: nakhhal jisam khhaak hak baar aavuradh || 196 ||
column3: The date-palm of the body of dust brings in the fruit of Truth. (196)

column2: hamachuneen suhabat kujaa baaz aaidhat
column3: When would you be able to run into such (an exalted) company?

column2: kaz baraae maradhamee mee-shaidhat || 197 ||
column3: Such a blessed company will bestow upon you the humaneness. (197)

column2: maradhamee yaanee ba-hak paivasatan asat
column3: The purpose of human life is (ultimately) to merge with the Creator;

column2: g(h)air zikarash az hamaa vaa risatan asat || 198 ||
column3: Absence of His description and discourse is tantamount to breaking away from every one else. (198)

column2: choo(n) dhil ba(n)dhaa bazikarash raeh yaaphat
column3: When a human being gets into the tradition of remembering Waaheguru,

column2: haasil umaro dhil aagaeh yaaphat || 199 ||
column3: He becomes conversant with the attainment of both life and soul. (199)

column2: kaarash az garadhoon garadhaa(n) dhar goozarat
column3: He will be redeemed and set free from the attachments of this revolving world when someone breaks away his connections from it;

column2: bar sar dhuniaa choo maradhaa(n) dhar guzarat || 200 ||
column3: Then, he would become detached from the material distractions like a seeker of spiritual knowledge. (200)

column2: e'ee(n) jahaano aa(n) jahaa(n) tahisee(n) kuna(n)dh
column3: He was applauded in both the worlds,

column2: aa(n) k dhil az zikar hak ra(n)gee(n) kuna(n)dh || 201 ||
column3: When anyone imbued his heart and soul with the remembrance of Akaalpurakh. (201)

column2: dhar vajoodhash aafataabe taaphataa
column3: The body of such a person begins to radiate like the sun,

column2: naam hak dhar suhabat shaa(n) yaaphataa || 202 ||
column3: When he, in the company of saintly persons, has attained the real Truth. (202)

column2: naam hak az basak roozo shab giraphat
column3: He remembered the Naam of Akaalpurakh day and night,

column2: dhasat uoo raa zikar maualaa bara-giraphat || 203 ||
column3: Then only the discourses and praises of the Lord became his support. (203)

column2: zikar maualaa aa(n) k yaaree dhaadhaa shudh
column3: Anyone who has received the support of Akaalpurakh due to his meditation,

column2: khhaanai veeraa(n) z hak aabaadhaa shudh || 204 ||
column3: Will have his deserted house, with the achievement of the Truth, rehabilitated and revived again. (204)

column2: zikar maualaa dhaualate baashadh azeem
column3: Meditation of God is one great treasure;

column2: kai badhasat aaidh z ga(n)jo maalo seem || 205 ||
column3: How can one obtain such a magnificent treasure from the worldly riches like wealth and silver? (205)

column2: har k hak raa khaasat hak uoo raa bakhhaasat
column3: Whosoever developed a desire for (meeting with) the Lord, the Lord liked him;

column2: shauok maualaa bihatareen keemeeaa-sat || 206 ||
column3: The love and devotion for Akaalpurakh is the best cure-all panacea. (206)

column2: gohar makasoodh tan yaadh khhudhaa-sat
column3: The deed of the main purpose of this body is only to remember Waaheguru;

column2: lekan uoo a(n)dhar zubaan aaualeeaa sat || 207 ||
column3: However, He always abides and manifests on the tongues of the noble souls. (207)

column2: paarasaiee beh k bahir hak bavadh
column3: That saintliness is really worthwhile if it is to seek the Truth;

column2: baadhashaahee (n)cheesat kaa(n) naahak bavadh || 208 ||
column3: What is the worth of that kingdom that is useless if it is not aiming towards God. (208)

column2: har dho mushataak a(n)dh ri(n)dho paarasaa
column3: Both the drunk and the holy person are desirous of Him;

column2: taa kiraa khhaahadh khhudhai kibareeaa || 209 ||
column3: Let us see! Whom does He, the transcendent Akaalpurakh likes?  (209)

column2: ba(n)dhaa taa(n) baashadh barai ba(n)dhageesat
column3: A human being deserves to be called a human being only if he directs himself towards meditation;

column2: gair haraph hak hamaa sharami(n)dhageesat || 210||
column3: Without a description/word of Waaheguru, it is all humiliation. (210)

column2: lek dhar zaahir kase baashadh dharusat
column3: However, it is apparent that only that person is on the right path,

column2: aa(n) k aaradh murashadh kaamil badhasat || 211 ||
column3: Who has been able to attain (or attach himself to) a perfect Guru. (211)

column2: dheeno dhuniaa har dho pharamaa(n)-dhaar uoo
column3: Both the Faith and the world are in complete obedience to the Almighty;

column2: har dho aalam shaik dheedhaar uoo || 212 ||
column3: Both the worlds are equally desirous to get just one glimpse of Him. (212)

column2: har k raa ulaphat z naam hak bavadh
column3: Anyone who has developed deep love for the Naam of  Akaalpurakh,

column2: dhar hakeekat aaraph mutalik bavadh || 213 ||
column3: He becomes a perfect seeker of the divine knowledge in real terms. (213)

column2: yaadh hak raa taalib uoo mee kuna(n)dh
column3: Seekers of Waaheguru are (actively) involved in His meditation;

column2: aariph hak jumalaa neko mee kuna(n)dh || 214 ||
column3: Seekers of Waaheguru transform everyone into something very attractive. (214)

column2: hak hamaa(n) baashadh k baashee ba(n)dhai
column3: The truth is that you should (always strive to) become a person of God,

column2: be-adhab dhaim z hak sharama(n)idhai || 215 ||
column3: A disrespectful (apostate/atheist) person is always chagrined and ashamed before Him. (215)

column2: aumar aa(n) baashadh k uoo dhar yaadh raphat
column3: Only that life is worth living that is spent in remembering Waaheguru,

column2: aumar naa boodh aa(n) k barabaadh raphat || 216 ||
column3: What use is that life that is spent needlessly and in vain. (216)

column2: ba(n)dhaa paidhaa shudh baraae ba(n)dhagee
column3: A person is born (only) to be engaged in meditation;

column2: khhush ilaaje hasat bahir ba(n)dhagee || 217 ||
column3: In fact, religious devotion (and prayers) is a good cure to put this life in the proper perspective. (217)

column2: aai khhushaa chashame k dheedhaa rooi dhoosat
column3: How fortunate is that eye that has got a glimpse of the face of the Beloved!

column2: maradhum chasham dho aalam sooi uoo sat || 218 ||
column3: Eyes of the people of both the worlds are fixed towards it. (218)

column2: e'ee(n) jahaano aa(n) jahaa(n) az hak pur asat
column3: This and the other world are satiated with the Truth;

column2: lek maradh hak ba-aalam kamatar asat || 219 ||
column3: But devoted men of God are rare in this world. (219)

column2: har kase koo ba-khhudhaa hamara(n)g shudh
column3: If some one became indistinguishable with Akaalpurakh,

column2: vasaph uoo dhar mulak roomo za(n)g shudh || 220 ||
column3: Then his glory spreads in countries like Rome and Africa. (220)

column2: maane'ee yakara(n)gee aamadh shauak hak
column3: To get assimilated in the Entity of God is, in fact, real love for Him;

column2: ba(n)dhaa raa aaraam a(n)dhar zauak hak || 221 ||
column3: And, it is only with a real devotion for Him that one gets eternal bliss. (221)

column2: uoo bara(n)g saahibee baa izo jaah
column3: Under the influence of Akaalpurakh, (Accepting the Will of Waaheguru)  he enjoys eclat and honors;

column2: maa baara(n)g ba(n)dhagee a(n)dhar panaeh || 222 ||
column3: We, under the influence of meditation, have sought his (His) shelter and refuge. (222)

column2: uoo bara(n)g saahib pharamaa(n) ravaa
column3: Accepting Waaheguru's Will, he is the king of the world and his command prevails all over;

column2: maa bara(n)g ba(n)dhagee nizadhash gadhaa || 223 ||
column3: We, under the influence of meditation, are just beggars before him. (223)

column2: uoo bara(n)g saahibee dhaaradh nazar
column3: He, while imbued in accepting Master's Will, keeps a close watch on us;

column2: ba(n)dhaa raa az ba(n)dhagee baashadh khhabar || 224 ||
column3: And, one can get to know him only through meditation. (224)

column2: aumar haa joyai iee(n) dhaualat shudha(n)dh
column3: They kept looking for such a treasure for ages;

column2: saalahaa mushataak iee(n) suhabat shudha(n)dh || 225 ||
column3: They were anxiously desirous of such a company for years. (225)

column2: har kase raa zaraa zaa(n) baashadh naseeb
column3: Anyone who was fortunate enough to attain even an atomic particle of such a wealth,

column2: aa(n) bakhhoobee gashat khhurasheedh najeeb || 226 ||
column3: He became an extraordinary sun easily and spontaneously. (226)

column2: gair uoo yaanee z hak gaphalat bavadh
column3: The underlying meaning of living without the memory of Waaheguru is complete ignorance and naivety.

column2: yaadh uoo saramaayai dhaualat bavadh || 227 ||
column3: The valuable asset of the remembrance of Akaalpurakh becomes the treasure of some fortunate beings. (227)

column2: dheedhan hak taa muyasar mee-shavadh
column3: One can get a glimpse of the Omnipotent only

column2: suhabat maradhaa(n) tasur mee-shavadh || 228 ||
column3: When one's association with noble saints become fruitful. (228)

column2: haraph hak dhar dhil agar maavaa kunadh
column3: If someone can abide even one word of Truth in his heart,

column2: dhar bun har mooi uoo hak jaa kunadh || 229 ||
column3: Then, Truth but nothing but the Truth gets assimilated to the roots of each of his hair. (229)

column2: har k khhudh raa sooi hak mee-aadharash
column3: Anyone who can direct himself towards the divine path of Waaheguru,

column2: az rukhh uoo noori-hak mee-baaradhash || 230 ||
column3: God's glory and splendor radiates from his face. (230)

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa phaij az tuphail suhabat asat
column3: All this benevolence and benignity is because of them and their blessings,

column2: suhabat maradhaan hak khhush dhaualat asat || 231 ||
column3: The company of saintly persons (of God) is one priceless asset. (231)

column2: heech kas az haal shaa(n) aagaeh neesat
column3: No one really understands or appreciates the state of mind of these noble royalties;

column2: har k o meh raa dharaa(n)jaa raeh neesat || 232 ||
column3: Every Tom, Dick or Harry does not have the wherewithal to reach there (them). (232)

column2: dhar nazar aai(n)dh choo(n) zaat alaah
column3: In appearance, they look just like an embodiment of the specie of Akaalpurakh,

column2: dhar hakeekat har dho aalam apanaeh || 233 ||
column3: In reality, they are the refuge for everyone in both the worlds. (233)

column2: dhar kasab baasha(n)dh aazaadh az kasab
column3: While engaged in their professions or trades, they are still unattached and unduly engrossed in them;

column2: aumar guzaraana(n)dh a(n)dhar yaadh rab || 234 ||
column3: They spend their lives in remembering the Provident (day and night). (234)

column2: khhesh raa choo(n) moor bishanaasa(n)dh shaa(n)
column3: They, the noble souls, consider themselves (out of humility) just like an ant,

column2: dhar hakeekat bihatar az peel dhamaa(n) || 235 ||
column3: Even though they, in fact, might be more powerful than a ferocious and dangerous elephant. (235)

column2: har ch mee-beenee hamaa hairaan shaa(n)
column3: Whatever you are seeing in this world is simply astonished and confounded about them;

column2: shaan shaa(n) bihatar bavadh az imatihaa(n) || 236 ||
column3: Their splendor and aura is far superior than even that of the examinations. (236)

column2: suhabat maradhaan hak baashadh karam
column3: The company of the true devotees of Waaheguru is a great boon;

column2: dhaualate kaa(n) raa nabhabaashadh heech g(h)m || 237 ||
column3: Such a wealth and virtuosity does not suffer from any anxiety or grief. (237)

column2: khhudh bazurago har kase shaa(n) nishasat
column3: They, themselves, are elevated, mature and blessed; anyone who happens to  be bestowed with their company;

column2: uoo bazuragee yaaphat taa(n) har jaa k hasat || 238 ||
column3: He, too, becomes elevated, mature and blessed, and receives laurels everywhere. (238)

column2: har kase koo khhesh raa bishanaakhhataa
column3: Anyone who has recognized his own reality;

column2: dhar tareek ba(n)dhagee paradhaakhhataa || 239 ||
column3: Consider that he has adopted the mode or the method of meditation. (239)

column2: e'ee(n) zameeno aasamaa(n) pur az khhudhaa-sat
column3: This earth and the skies are saturated with (the creations of ) God,

column2: aalame har soo dhavaa(n) kaa(n) sheh kujaa-sat || 240 ||
column3: But this world keeps wandering and straying in all directions to find out as to where He is. (240)

column2: dheedhaa bar dheedhaar hak gar mubatalaa-sat
column3: If you can aim your eyes fixedly on a glimpse of Akaalpurakh,

column2: har cheh mee beenee bachashamat haka-numaa-sat || 241 ||
column3: Then, whatever you see will be a vision of the Almighty Waaheguru. (241)

column2: har k shaa(n) raa dheedh hak raa dheedhaa asat
column3: Anyone who has seen that noble soul, consider that he has got a glimpse of the Omnipotent;

column2: uoo tareek ba(n)dhagee phahimeedhaa asat || 242 ||
column3: And, that person has perceived and realized the path of meditation. (242)

column2: taraz yaka-ra(n)gee ajab ra(n)g aaradhash
column3: The focus on devotion for God brings in with it an unusual complexion of disposition,

column2: kaz badhan noor khhudhaa mee-baaradhash || 243 ||
column3: The splendor and radiance of Akaalpurakh then oozes out from each and every aspect of such a dedicated devotion. (243)

column2: uoo bara(n)g saahibee iee(n) hasato boodh
column3: He is the Master of all this illusion (of materialism), this is His own form;

column2: ba(n)dhagee dhaim ba-aadhaab sajoodh || 244 ||
column3: And, His meditation, with respect and prostrations, always seems apt. (244)

column2: uoo bara(n)g saahibee arashaadh uoo
column3: He is the shape and form of the Master and only His command prevails;

column2: ba(n)dhagee taa sar kadham bubayaadh uoo || 245 ||
column3: The meditation from head to toe also emerges out of (because of) Him. (245)

column2: saahibe baa saahibaa(n) zebadh mudhaam
column3: A Master looks graceful and befitting only among the Masters,

column2: ba(n)dhaa raa dhar ba(n)dhagee baashadh kiaam || 246 ||
column3: A person should, therefore, continue to stay in meditation all the times. (246)

column2: saahibaa(n) raa saahibee baashadh shuaar
column3: The character of Masters is to be master-like,

column2: ba(n)dhaa raa dhar ba(n)dhagee phasal bahaar || 247 ||
column3: And, a man has the spring season around him only when he meditates. (247)

column2: saahibaa(n) raa saahibee dhaim bavadh
column3: The master-ship character, His praises, of the Master is eternal,

column2: ba(n)dhaa ham dhar ba(n)dhagee kaim bavadh || 248 ||
column3: And, the meditation of a human being is permanent. (248)

column2: az barai aa(n) k too sara-gashataiee
column3: For this, you have turned your head away from Him, you have strayed;

column2: az pe dhuniaa z hak bara-gashataiee || 249 ||
column3: That you have turned your face away from Him just for the sake of this material  world. (249)

column2: dhaualat geetee na baashadh paidhaar
column3: The worldly riches are not going to last for ever,

column2: yak naphas khhudh raa basooi hak biaar || 250 ||
column3: (Therefore) You should turn yourself towards Waaheguru even for just one moment. (250)

column2: choo(n) dhil too mail yaadh khhudhaa-sat
column3: When your heart and soul becomes inclined towards remembering Waaheguru,

column2: aa(n) khhudhai paak kai az too judhaa-sat || 251 ||
column3: Then, how and when would that pious and chaste Waaheguru be separated from you? (251)

column2: gar too g(h)aaphila-baashee az phikar bula(n)dh
column3: If you remain negligent about paying close attention to the remembrance of lofty Akaalpurakh,

column2: too kujaa o uoo kujaa aai hoshama(n)dh || 252 ||
column3: Then, you mentally alert person! How can there be a meeting between you and Him (You are here and He is somewhere else)? (252)

column2: yaadh uoo dharadh dho aalam raa dhavaa-sat
column3: Memory of Waaheguru is the cure-all for all pains and agonies of both the worlds;

column2: yaadh uoo har guma-shudhaa raa raahanumaa sat || 253 ||
column3: His memory also directs all lost and strayed ones to the correct path. (253)

column2: yaadh uoo iee(n) jumalaa raa laazam bavadh
column3: His remembrance is absolutely imperative for everyone,

column2: har k g(h)aaphil shudh azo mulazam shavadh || 254 ||
column3: And, anyone who becomes negligent and forgets Him is indeed guilty. (254)

column2: yaa ilaahee ba(n)dhaa raa tauapheek dhih
column3: O Akaalpurakh ! Kindly bless me with such a courage and strength,

column2: taa ba-yaadhat biguzaradh iee(n) umar beh || 255 ||
column3: So that this life of mine is spent in a worthwhile manner in remembering You. (255)

column2: aumar aa(n) baashadh k dhar yaadh khhudhaa
column3: That life is worth living that is spent in remembering Akaalpurakh,

column2: biguzaradh dheegar nabhabaashadh mudhaa || 256 ||
column3: Any part of it spent without His memory, is simply a waste and useless. (256)

column2: mudhaa bihatar juz yaadh neesat
column3: There is no purpose (of life) better than the remembrance of Akaalpurakh,

column2: g(h)air yaadhash iee(n) dhil maa shaadh neesat || 257 ||
column3: And, our hearts and minds can never be pleased without remembering Him. (257)

column2: shaadheei dhaim bavadh yaadh khhudhaa
column3: The nostalgia about Waaheguru bestows upon us an eternal elation;

column2: aai zahe dhaualat k baashadh raahanumaa || 258 ||
column3: How fortunate we are that it shows us the direction (in our lives)!(258)

column2: gar ch hak dhar jumalai dhilahaa bavadh
column3: Even though Akaalpurakh abides in the hearts of everyone,

column2: lek aariph saahib ieemaa(n) bavadh || 259 ||
column3: Still, only an enlightened persons can be called 'a man of faith and religion'. (259)

column2: chasham aariph kaabal dheedhaar hasat
column3: Only the eye of an enlightened person deserves a glimpse of the Almighty;

column2: maradh aarif vaakiph asaraar hasat || 260 ||
column3: And, it is only the heart of a knowledgeable person who is familiar with His mysteries. (260)

column2: suhabat maradhaan hak raa dhoosat dhaar
column3: You should develop friendship with the noble souls and should keep their company;

column2: taa too ham garadhee z yamanash rusatagaar || 261 ||
column3: So that, with the Providential blessings, you may be redeemed from the cycles of transmigration. (261)

column2: har cheh hasat az suhabat ieeshaa(n) bavadh
column3: Whatever is visible in this world is all due to company of saintly persons;

column2: zaa(n) k jisamo jaa saraapaa jaa(n) bavadh || 262 ||
column3: Because our bodies and souls are, in fact, the soul of the Provident. (262)

column2: muradhumaan dheedhaa roshan shudh azo
column3: The pupils of my eyes are fully lighted only because of their company;

column2: khhaak jisamam jumalaa gulashan shudh azo || 263 ||
column3: And, the dirt of my body, for the same reason, is transformed into a lush garden. (263)

column2: aai zahe sahubat k khhaak akaseer karadh
column3: Blessed is that association that has transformed a dirt into a cure-all;

column2: naakase raa saahib tadhabeer karadh || 264 ||
column3: And, converted every lowly uniformed person into knowledgeable and intelligent. (264)

column2: goharo laalo javaahar pesh shaa(n)
column3: I present myself in the form of pearls, rubies and gems to my Beloved,

column2: har dhame koo biguzaradh dhar yaadh aa(n) || 265 ||
column3: When I spend every moment of my life in His memory. (265)

column2: e'ee(n) javaahara-haa hamaa phaanee bavadh
column3: All these worldly diamonds and pearls are perishable;

column2: yaadh hak bar ba(n)dhaa arazaanee bavadh || 266 ||
column3: The remembrance of Waaheguru, however, is extremely valuable for a human being. (266)

column2: rasam maradhaan khhudhaa dhaanee k cheesat
column3: Do you know what is the custom and tradition of the devotees of Omnipotent?

column2: phaarig(h) a(n)dh az kaidhahai marajo zeesat || 267 ||
column3: They are redeemed and are free from the imprisonment of the cycles of births and deaths for ever. (267)

column2: yak naphas be yaadh hak nabhaguzaashata(n)dh
column3: They do not spend even one moment without remembering Akaalpurakh,

column2: khhush aalam bar nahu tabak afaraashata(n)dh || 268 ||
column3: They unfurl their beautiful flag (of meditation) over all the nine skies. (268)

column2: khhairakhhaeh julagee paidhaish a(n)dh
column3: They wish and pray for the well-being of the entire created world,

column2: zeb bakhhash iee(n) hamaa aaraish a(n)dh || 269 ||
column3: It is them who bless all these creations and natural beauties with grace and elegance. (269)

column2: naam hak maradhaan hak raa zevar asat
column3: The Naam of Waaheguru is an ornament for His noble and saintly devotees,

column2: chasham shaa(n) az noor hak pur gauahar asat || 270 ||
column3: And, the eye of these nobilities is always full of pearls and gems because of the refulgent glow of the Almighty. (270)

column2: haraph shaa(n) taaleem umar jaavidhaa(n)
column3: Their words are a lessons for a permanent life,

column2: yaadh hak dhaara(n)dh dhaim bar zubaa(n) || 271 ||
column3: And, the memory of Akaalpurakh abides on their lips/tongue for ever. (271)

column2: har cheh meegoi(n)dh arashaadhasato bas
column3: Their utterances have the status of the words of Divine,

column2: bar namee aara(n)dh g(h)air az hak naphas || 272 ||
column3: And, not even one breath of theirs is spent without remembering Him. (272)

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa mushataak dheedhaar khhudhaa-sat
column3: All these saintly persons are really seekers of a Divine glimpse,

column2: bosataan dhahir gulazaar khhudhaa-sat || 273 ||
column3: And, this delightful worldly spread is, in fact, a heavenly flower bed. (273)

column2: har k baa-maradhaan hak shudh aashanaa
column3: Whosoever developed a friendship with the devotees of Waaheguru,

column2: saiaai uoo bihatar az baal humaa || 274 ||
column3: Take it that his shadow (on them) will be many times more blessed than the shadow of the feathers of  the Humaa bird (It is said that a shadow of Humaa bird can bestow the kingdom of the world). (274)

column2: yaadh hak yaanee z khhudh big(h)uzashatan asat
column3: We should take it that getting absorbed in Waaheguru's meditation is to give up self-ego,

column2: az khhiaal g(h)air hak vaarusatan asat || 275 ||
column3: And, not thinking about Him would get us stuck in every other worldly attraction. (275)

column2: rasatagee az khheshatan vaarasatagee-sat
column3: To redeem ourselves from our egos is the real emancipation,

column2: baa khhudhai khheshatan dhila-basatagee-sat || 276 ||
column3: And, to tie up our minds with Waaheguru's devotion is also real deliverance. (276)

column2: har kas koo baa khhudhaa dhil basataa asat
column3: Whosoever has linked and attached his mind to the Almighty,

column2: uoo z charakhh nahu tabak bara-jasataa asat || 277 ||
column3: Take it that he has easily leaped over a sky equipped even with nine locks. (277)

column2: suhabat dhila-basatagaan baa khhudhaa
column3: The company of such God-attached devotees,

column2: kai muyasar aaidhat iee(n) keemeeaa || 278 ||
column3: Take it that it is the cure-all; however, how can we be fortunate enough to obtain it? (278)

column2: dheeno dhuniaa har dho hairaa(n) maa(n)dhaa a(n)dh
column3: Both the faith and the religion are amazed,

column2: bas z hairaanee preeshaa(n) maa(n)dhaa a(n)dh || 279 ||
column3: And in this amazement beyond limits they are perplexed. (279)

column2: har keh raa iee(n) aarazooe paak hasat
column3: Whosoever imbibes such a chaste and divine desire,

column2: murashadh uoo saahib adharaak hasat || 280 ||
column3: His Guru (teacher) is the master of innate and intrinsic knowledge. (280)

column2: vaasilaani-hak turaa vaasil kuna(n)dh
column3: God connected noble saints can make your connection with Him,

column2: dhaualat jaaveedh raa haasil kuna(n)dh || 281 ||
column3: They can also help you to obtain the eternal treasure, the Naam. (281)

column2: dhaualat jaaveedh pesh aariph asat
column3: This is an immortal achievement for an enlightened person,

column2: e'ee(n) sakhhun mashahoor bas mutaariph asat || 282 ||
column3: This adage is commonly well known, and everyone is well acquainted with it. (282)

column2: aariphaano kaamilaano vaasilaa(n)
column3: The enlightened, perfect and submerged into the love of God devotees;

column2: naam uoo dhaaradh dhaim bar zubaa(n) || 283 ||
column3: They always have His Naam on their tongues and lips in meditation. (283)

column2: ba(n)dhageei shaa(n) bavadh zikar khhudhaa
column3: To continually meditate on His Naam is their worship;

column2: dhaualat jaaveedh baashadh haka-numaa || 284 ||
column3: And, the eternal treasure blessed by Akaalpurakh directs one towards His path. (284)

column2: choo(n) numaidh dhaualat jaaveedh roo
column3: When the divine eternal treasure shows Its face,

column2: too z hak baashee vaa hak baashadh z too || 285 ||
column3: You would then belong to Waaheguru and He would belong to you. (285)

column2: bar dhilat gar paratave hak baraphaga(n)dh
column3: If the shadow of Akaalpurakh falls on someone's heart and soul,

column2: khhaar hijarat raa z pai dhil kuna(n)dh || 286 ||
column3: Then take it that the painful thorn of separation has been extracted out of the foot (depth) of our mind. (286)

column2: khhaar hijar az pai dhil choo(n) dhoor shudh
column3: When the thorn of separation has been removed from the feet of the heart,

column2: khhaanai dhil az khhudhaa maamoor shudh || 287 ||
column3: Take it then that the Akaalpurakh has made the temple of our heart as His abode. (287)

column2: hamachoo kataraa koo badhariaa dhar phataadh
column3: Like that drop of water that fell into a river or ocean, giving up its own identity (showing humility),

column2: aain dhariaa gashato vasalash dhasatadhaadh || 288 ||
column3: It itself became the river and the ocean; (thus falling on the feet of Aakaalpurakh), and convergence with Him took place. (288)

column2: kataraa choo(n) shudh badhariaa aashanaa
column3: Once the drop merges into the ocean,

column2: baadh azaa(n) taphareek natavaa(n) shudh z jaa || 289 ||
column3: After that, it cannot be separated from the ocean. (289)

column2: kataraa choo(n) jaanib dhariaa shataaphat
column3: When the drop started to rush in the direction of the ocean,

column2: az reh taphareek khhudh raa kataraa yaaphat || 290 ||
column3: It, then, realized the significance of being just a drop of water. (290)

column2: kataraa raa iee(n) dhaualat choo(n) dhasatadhaadh
column3: When the drop was bestowed with this eternal meeting,

column2: kataraa shudh a(n)dhar hakeekat baa-muraadh || 291 ||
column3: The reality dawned on it, and its long-cherished desire was fulfilled. (291)

column2: guphat man yak kataraa aabee boodhaa am
column3: The droplet said, "Even though I am a small drop of water,

column2: paihan dhariaa raa chunaa(n) paimoodhaa am || 292 ||
column3: I have been able to measure the expanse of this huge ocean." (292)

column2: gar maraa dhar baaz raeh lutaph khhesh
column3: If the ocean, out of its extreme kindness, would agree to take me in,

column2: vaasil khhudh karadh az a(n)dhaazaa besh || 293 ||
column3: And, it agreed to merge me into itself even beyond its capacity; (293)

column2: hamachoo mauaj az paihan dhariaa roo namoodh
column3: And, it rose like a tidal wave out of the span of the ocean,

column2: mauaj gashat vaa karadh dhariaa raa sajoodh || 294 ||
column3: It became another wave, and then bowed in reverence to the ocean. (294)

column2: ham chunaa(n) har ba(n)dhaa k vaasil asat
column3: In the same manner, every such person who had a confluence with the Almighty,

column2: dhar tareek ba(n)dhagee bas kaamil asat || 295 ||
column3: Became complete and perfect on the path of meditation. (295)

column2: mauajau dhariaa gar ch dhar maanee yakesat
column3: In reality, a wave and the ocean are one and the same,

column2: lek a(n)dhar ieeno aa(n) pharake basesat || 296 ||
column3: But still there is a vast difference between them. (296)

column2: man yake mauajam too bahir bekaraa(n)
column3: I am just a simple wave, while you are an enormously large ocean,

column2: pharak baashadh az zameeno aasamaa(n) || 297 ||
column3: Thus, there is a big difference between you and me like that between the earth and the sky. (297)

column2: man neeam iee(n) jumalaa az alataaph too
column3: I am nothing; all this (that I am) is only because of your blessings,

column2: man yak mauajam z tabaai saaph too || 298 ||
column3: I am, too, one wave in Your vast manifest world. (298)

column2: baa bazuragaa(n) suhabate mee baidhat
column3: You would need the association with the noble persons,

column2: az humaa aval hamee(n) mee baidhat || 299 ||
column3: This will be the first and the foremost thing that you will need. (299)

column2: kaadhar mutalik bakudharat zaahir asat
column3: That perfect and complete Creator is visible through His own creations,

column2: dharamiaan kudharat khhudh kaadhar asat || 300 ||
column3: The Creator, in fact, abides amidst His own Nature and manifestations. (300)

column2: kaadharo kudharat baham aamekhhata(n)dh
column3: The Creator and His creations are one and the same,

column2: aa(n) matai g(h)air hak raa rekhhata(n)dh || 301 ||
column3: They, the noble persons, renounce all material distractions except the Provident. (301)

column2: pas turaa ham baidh aai yaar azeez
column3: O my dear friend! Then you should also make a judgement and conclude,

column2: hak kudhaam vaa too kudhaamee kun tameez || 302 ||
column3: As to who is God, and who you are, and how to distinguish between the two. (302)

column2: gar too vaasil gashataiee dhar zaat uoo
column3: If, in your pursuits, you happen to have a meeting with the Akaalpurakh.

column2: g(h)air haraph ba(n)dhagee dheegar magoo || 303 ||
column3: Then you should not utter any other word except the word of worship and meditation. (303)

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa az dhaualat iee(n) ba(n)dhageesat
column3: All this tangible and non-tangible boons are because of the meditation,

column2: zi(n)dhagee be-ba(n)dhagee sharami(n)dhagasit || 304 ||
column3: Without meditation, this life of ours is only mortification and humiliation. (304)

column2: hak taalaa ba(n)dhagee pharamoodhaa asat
column3: The Almighty God has also said,

column2: har kase koo ba(n)dhaa shudh aasoodhaa asat || 305 ||
column3: Anyone who transformed himself into a man of God is redeemed. (305)

column2: choo(n) analahak bar zubaa(n) izahaar karadh
column3: Anyone who proclaimed through his own mouth that he was God,

column2: sharaa aa(n) manasoor raa bara-dhaar karadh || 306 ||
column3: The Islamic religious law crucified him just like Mansoor. (306)

column2: masate'ee hak maaneei hushiaaree asat
column3: Inebriated with God is, in fact, to be always in a state of alertness,

column2: aariphaa(n) raa khhaab ham bedhaaree asat || 307 ||
column3: Even dreaming while asleep for the knowledgeable is indeed like staying awake. (307)

column2: dhar hakeekat be-adhab yaabadh sazaa
column3: In reality, a disrespectful faces the consequences (reaps the fruits) of his own actions,

column2: choo(n) aadhab amadh hamaa raa rahaanumaa || 308 ||
column3: Because, it is the 'respect' and 'civility' that is capable of showing all the direction of the right path. (308)

column2: gar too sar taa paa hamaa hak gashataiee
column3: If you have transformed yourself from head to toe into Akaalpurakh's form,

column2: vaasil be-choon mutalik gashataiee || 309 ||
column3: And, If you have merged into that unparalleled and matchless Waaheguru, (309)

column2: baaz raeh ba(n)dhagee dhar pesh geer
column3: Then you should adopt the path of meditation,

column2: ba(n)dhai uoo baash vaa raeh khesh geer || 310 ||
column3: And, become His (favorite) person by holding on to the divine spiritual  passage  of meditation. (310)

column2: dhar hamaa haalat khhudhaa haazar babee(n)
column3: One should assume His presence under all circumstances,

column2: haaziro naazir hamaa(n) naazir babee(n) || 311 ||
column3: Considering Him Omnipresent and Immanent, and also take it that He is capable of seeing everything everywhere. (311)

column2: dhar raeh hak juz adhab taaleem neesat
column3: There is no education except that of respect and civility in the path of God,

column2: taalib uoo raa bajuz tasaleem neesat || 312 ||
column3: It is not prudent for His seeker-devotee to accept anything but His Order. (312)

column2: taalibaan hak hameshaa baa adhab
column3: The seekers of the Divine Spirit are always respectful,

column2: baa adhab baasha(n)dh a(n)dhar yaadh rab || 313 ||
column3: They are also satiated with reverence while remembering Him. (313)

column2: beadhab raa kai z raeh shaa(n) khhabar
column3: What does an apostate know about the tradition of those noble persons?

column2: beadhab az hak hameshaa(n) be-asar || 314 ||
column3: The efforts of an atheist to get a glimpse of Akaalpurakh will always be ineffective. (314)

column2: beadhab haragiz ba-hak raeh nayaaphat
column3: A disrespectful can never find the path leading towards the Divine Spirit;

column2: raeh hak raa reech gumaraahe nayaaphat || 315 ||
column3: No strayed person has ever been able to find the path of God and much less to reach Him. (315)

column2: haadhe'ee raeh khhudhaa aamadh adhab
column3: It is reverence that is the guide to the path of Waaheguru;

column2: be-adhab khhaalee-sat az alataaph rab || 316 ||
column3: And, an atheist remains blank from receiving His blessings. (316)

column2: be-adhab raeh khhudhaa kai dhaanadhash
column3: How can an atheist find the way to the Almighty,

column2: har kiraa kahir khhudhaa meeraanadhash || 317 ||
column3: Who has been condemned due to the anger of Waaheguru?(317)

column2: dhar panaeh saiaai maradhaan hak
column3: If you care to seek the shelter (and agree to function in their shadow) of the noble souls of God,

column2: gar ravee aa(n) jaa adhab yaabee sabak || 318 ||
column3: You will receive teachings and instructions about respectability there. (318)

column2: be adhab iee(n)jaa adhab aamoz shudh
column3: Coming to this place (of noble persons), even the apostates become capable to teach lessons of reverence,

column2: e'ee(n) charaag(h) gul jahaa(n) apharoz shudh || 319 ||
column3: Here, even extinguished lamps begin to spread light throughout the world. (319)

column2: aai khhudhaa har be adhab raa dheh adhab
column3: O Akaalpurakh! Kindly bestow reverence even on the irreverent,

column2: taa guzaaradh umar raa dhar yaadh rab || 320 ||
column3: So that they can spend their lives in Your remembrance. (320)

column2: gar bayaabee lazate az yaadh uoo
column3: If you can relish the savor (sweet taste) of Waaheguru's remembrance,

column2: zi(n)dhaa baashee dhaimaa aai neka-khoo || 321 ||
column3: Then O good man! You can become immortal. (321)

column2: e'ee(n) vajoodh khhaak raa kaim badhaa(n)
column3: Consider this body of dirt as permanent for this reason

column2: kaim aamadh shauak uoo dhar hiraz jaa(n) || 322 ||
column3: Because the devotion for Him have established permanently in the fortress of your heart. (322)

column2: shauak maualaa zi(n)dhage'ee jaa(n) bavadh
column3: The love and elation for Akaalpurakh are the life-line of the soul,

column2: yaadh uoo saramaai ieemaa(n) bavadh || 323 ||
column3: There is a wealth of faith and religion in His memory. (323)

column2: shauak uoo dhar har dhile kai jaa kunadh
column3: How can the euphoria and elation for Waaheguru abide in every heart,

column2: dhar vajoodh khhaak kai maavaa kunadh || 324 ||
column3: And, how can He take refuge in the body made up of dirt. (324)

column2: shauak maualaa mar turaa choo(n) dhasatadhaadh
column3: When your fondness for Akaalpurakh supported you,

column2: dhaualat dhaim badhasatat dhara-phataadh || 325 ||
column3: Then, take it for granted that you will obtain control and have the divine eternal wealth. (325)

column2: khhaak raahash suramai sar asat
column3: The dust of His path is like a collyrium for our eyes and head,

column2: aariphaa(n) raa beh z taazo aphasar asat || 326 ||
column3: This dust is much more valuable than the crown and the thrones for the enlightened. (326)

column2: dhaualat dhuniaa nabhabaashadh paidhaar
column3: This worldly wealth is not ever lasting,

column2: dhar tareek aariphaan hak guzaar || 327 ||
column3: You should accept this according to the verdict of the true devotees of God. (327)

column2: yaadh uoo laazim bavadh dhaim turaa
column3: Meditation of Waaheguru is always absolutely essential for you,

column2: zikar uoo kaim kunadh kaim turaa || 328 ||
column3: And, the discourse about Him makes you steady and immovable forever. (328)

column2: aariphaa(n) dhaara(n)dh baa iraphaan khhesh
column3: The devotees of Akaalpurakh are intimately connected to the divine knowledge,

column2: haasal iraphaa(n) dharoon jaan khhesh || 329 ||
column3: And, the achievement of divine knowledge is completely absorbed inside their souls. (329)

column2: masanadh shauak ilaahee be-zavaal
column3: The throne of devotion for Akaalpurakh is permanent and indestructible,

column2: varanaa beenee pur zavaale har kamaal || 330 ||
column3: Although every peak has a trough. (330)

column2: be-zavaal aamadh kamaal zauak hak
column3: The marvel of the zest for God's love is eternal and non-destructible,

column2: taa k yaabadh zaraa az shauak hak || 331 ||
column3: Wish were it that we can get just one particle of His devotion. (331)

column2: har kase koo yaaphat uoo jaaveedh shudh
column3: Whosoever is lucky enough to obtain such a particle, he becomes immortal,

column2: dhar hakeekat saahib umeedh shudh || 332 ||
column3: In reality, his desire (to meet with Akaalpurakh) is fulfilled. (332)

column2: choo(n) umeedhash soorat haasal giraphat
column3: When he reached the stage of fulfillment,

column2: zaraa az shauak jaa dhar dhil giraphat || 333 ||
column3: That particle of the strong desire for His devotion gets seeded into his heart. (333)

column2: aab haivaa(n) meechakadh az mooi uoo
column3: The divine nectar oozes out of his every hair,

column2: zi(n)dhaa meegaradhadh jahaa(n) az booi uoo || 334 ||
column3: And the whole world, with his aroma, becomes alive and rises up. (334)

column2: aai zahe imasaan k hak raa yaaphataa
column3: Fortunate is that person who has attained the Provident;

column2: roo z yaadh gair hak bara-taaphataa || 335 ||
column3: And, who has turned himself away (detached) from every worldly items except the memory of God. (335)

column2: dhar libaas dhuniyavee phaarig(h) azaa(n)
column3: Even while living in worldly guise, he is detached from every materialistic thing,

column2: hamachoo zaatish aashikaa(n) raa uoo nihaa(n) || 336 ||
column3: Like the Entity of God, he maintains a hidden profile. (336)

column2: zaahirish dhar kaidh mushat khhaak hasat
column3: Outwardly he might be appearing to be in the grip of a fistful of dust,

column2: baatan uoo baa khhudhai paak hasat || 337 ||
column3: Inwardly, he is always engaged in talking about the chaste Akaalpurakh and abides with Him. (337)

column2: zaahir a(n)dhar mail faraza(n)dho zan
column3: Outwardly, he might appear to be immersed in love for his child and wife,

column2: dhar hakeekat baa khhudhai khheshatan || 338 ||
column3: In reality, he always abides (in thought and action) with his God. (338)

column2: zaahir a(n)dhar mail hiraso havaa
column3: Outwardly, he might seem to be inclined towards 'desires and greed',

column2: baatan uoo paak az yaadh khhudhaa || 339 ||
column3: But inwardly, he remains chaste and sacred in the memory of Waaheguru. (339)

column2: zaahir a(n)dhar mail asapo shutar
column3: Outwardly, he might appear to be paying attention to horses and camels,

column2: baatanash phaarig(h) z kaidh shoro shar || 340 ||
column3: But inwardly, he remains detached from the worldly hub-hub and noises. (340)

column2: zaahir a(n)dhar mail seemo zar asat
column3: He might appear to be involved in gold and silver outwardly,

column2: baatan a(n)dhar saahib bahiro bar asat || 341 ||
column3: But he is, in fact, master of land and water inwardly. (341)

column2: raphataa raphataa baatanash zaahir shudhaa
column3: His intrinsic worth gets revealed slowly and gradually,

column2: dhar hakeekat tibalai a(n)bar shudhaa || 342 ||
column3: In fact, he becomes a casket of fragrance. (342)

column2: zaahiro baatan shudhaa yakasaan uoo
column3: His internal and external selves become one and the same,

column2: har dho aalam ba(n)dhai pharamaan uoo || 343 ||
column3: Both the worlds become followers of his command. (343)

column2: ham badhil yaadh khhudhaa vaa raa zubaa(n)
column3: His heart and tongue are completely immersed in Akaalpurkh's remembrance at all times and  for ever,

column2: e'ee(n) zubaanash dhil shudhaa dhil shudh zubaa(n) || 344 ||
column3: His tongue becomes his heart, and his heart his tongue. (344)

column2: vaasilaan hak chunee(n) pharamoodhaa a(n)dh
column3: Those saintly  souls who have converged with God have said clearly,

column2: ba(n)dhaa haa dhar ba(n)dhagee aasoodhaa a(n)dh || 345 ||
column3: That persons of God remain comfortable and happy while they are in meditation. (345)

column2: saahibee baashadh musalam shaeh raa
column3: The mastery and splendor of our True King, the Waaheguru, is well known,

column2: kuranash man saalik iee(n) raeh raa || 346 ||
column3: I bow before the pedestrian who is walking on this path. (346)

column2: saalaak iee(n) raeh bama(n)zal raeh yaaphat
column3: The traveler on this path arrived at his destination,

column2: haasil umar dhil aagaeh yaaphat || 347 ||
column3: And, his heart became familiar with the real purpose and attainment of life. (347)

column2: ba(n)dhaa haa raa ba(n)dhagee dharakaar hasat
column3: Persons of God really need only His meditation,

column2: jaam shauak ba(n)dhagee sarashaar hasat || 348 ||
column3: And, the cup of the pleasure and elation of meditation continues to overflow for ever. (348)

column2: saahibee zebadh khhudhai paak raa
column3: The Mastery (of all creations in this world) is befitting and looks elegant only for the true and the chaste Master, the Akaalpurakh;

column2: aa(n) k zeenat dhaadh mushat khhaak raa || 349 ||
column3: And, it is Him alone who has blessed this fistful of dust the gaiety and prosperity. (349)

column2: shauak az yaadh hakash mumataaz karadh
column3: The fondness to remember the Waaheguru blessed him with prominence,

column2: sar pharaazo saahib har raaz karadh || 350 ||
column3: And, this tendency also blessed him with honor and eminence and made him familiar with His mysteries. (350)

column2: mushat khhaak az yaadh hak rauanak giraphat
column3: This fistful of dust, with the remembrance of Akaalpurakh, became bright and shiny,

column2: basak dhar dhil shauak yaadh hak giraphat || 351 ||
column3: And, the fondness to remember Him began to surge like a storm in his heart. (351)

column2: aai zahe kaadhar k az yak kataraa aab
column3: May we express our deep devotion for the Omnipotent who from just one drop of water

column2: khhaak raa(n) rauashan kunadh choo(n) aaphataab || 352 ||
column3: Gave this lowly fistful of dust the brightness and shine of the sun. (352)

column2: aai zahe khhaake k noora-apharoz shudh
column3: May we sacrifice ourselves for that dust that became enlightened and radiant,

column2: e'ee(n) saadhat haa naseeb a(n)dhoz shudh || 353 ||
column3: And, which was fortunate enough to deserve such boons and blessings. (353)

column2: aai zahe kudharat k hak baar aavuradh
column3: Wonderful is the Nature that brings in the fruits of truth,

column2: mushat khhaakee raa baguphataar aavuradh || 354 ||
column3: And, which blesses the humble fistful of dust the power to speak. (354)

column2: haasal iee(n) zi(n)dhagee yaadh khhudhaa-sat
column3: It is the meditation of Waaheguru that is the achievement of this life;

column2: aai zahe chashame k bar hak mubatalaa-sat || 355 ||
column3: May we sacrifice ourselves for the eye that becomes overawed and gets obsessed with the Truth (God). (355)

column2: aai zahe dhil k a(n)dharash shauakash bavadh
column3: How blessed is the heart that has an innocent eagerness for the love of God!

column2: dhar hakeekat saahib zauakash bavadh || 356 ||
column3: In fact, he becomes a fervent and fascinated devotee for His love. (356)

column2: aa(n) zahe sar koo baraahish dhar sajoodh
column3: Blessed is the head that bows to the real path of Truth, the God;

column2: ham choo(n) chauagaa(n) gue shauakash dhar raboodh || 357 ||
column3: And, who like the crooked stick with a grip, ran away with the ball of elation. (357)

column2: aai zahe dhasate k vasaphash uoo navishat
column3: Wonderful are those hands that have written His praises and lauds;

column2: aai zahe paae koo dhar kooish guzashat || 358 ||
column3: Blessed are those feet that have passed through His street. (358)

column2: aa(n) zabaane beh k zikar uoo kunadh
column3: Noble is the tongue that meditates on His Naam;

column2: khhaatare aa(n) beh k phikar uoo kunadh || 359 ||
column3: And, virtuous is the mind that concentrates its thoughts on Waaheguru. (359)

column2: dhar hamaa uzave k uoo a(n)dhar tanasat
column3: Akaalpurakh abides in every limb of our bodies,

column2: shauak uoo a(n)dhar sar maradho zan asat || 360 ||
column3: And, the zeal and ardor for His love is assimilated in the heads of all men and women. (360)

column2: aarazooe jumalaa shooi uoo bavadh
column3: All desires and wishes are concentrated in His direction,

column2: shauak uoo aagushataa dhar har moo bavadh || 361 ||
column3: And, fondness for Him is absorbed in every hair of our bodies. (361)

column2: gar too khhaahee saahib iraphaa(n) shavee
column3: If you want that you become master of divine thought,

column2: jaa(n) ba-jaanaa(n) dheh k taa jaanaa(n) (n)shavee || 362 ||
column3: Then, you should sacrifice your life for your Beloved Waaheguru, so that you will acquire the same shape and form that He has. (362)

column2: harach dhaaree kun hamaa kurabaan uoo
column3: You should sacrifice all that you have for your true Beloved,

column2: rezaa-cheenee kun dhame az khhaan uoo || 363 ||
column3: And, pick up scraps of food from His dining table just for a moment. (363)

column2: shauak iraphaanash agar kaamil bavadh
column3: If you become completely desirous of His true knowledge and enlightenment,

column2: gauahar makasoodh too haasil shavadh || 364 ||
column3: Then, you will, inevitably, achieve your purpose. (364)

column2: too ham az iee(n) umar yaabee bahirai
column3: You will receive your life's fruits,

column2: mihar iraphaanash choo bakhhashadh zarai || 365 ||
column3: When the sun of divine knowledge would bless you with just one ray of its radiance. (365)

column2: naam too a(n)dhar jahaa(n) garadhadh bula(n)dh
column3: Your name would become famous and illuminated;

column2: shauak iraphaanat kunadh bas arazama(n)dh || 366 ||
column3: And, your ardor for divine knowledge would make you extremely popular in this world. (366)

column2: shauak iraphaanish kase raa dhasatabaadh
column3: Whosoever developed special affection and fondness for divine love,

column2: kaz kuleedhash kuphal dhilahaa raa kushaadh || 367 ||
column3: With his key, all locks of the hearts got opened up (realities became known). (367)

column2: kuphal raa bikushaa vaa maal bekaraa(n)
column3: You should, too, open up the lock of your heart, and from the hidden

column2: dhar kaph khhudh aar az ga(n)j nihaa(n) || 368 ||
column3: treasure, should derive unlimited pleasure and elation. (368)

column2: ka(n)dharaa(n) laalo guhar biseeaar hasat
column3: In the nooks of your heart, numerous gems and diamonds are lying hidden;

column2: az matai lulooe shahivaar hasat || 369 ||
column3: And, your treasure and wealth contain many royal pearls. (369)

column2: har cheh meekhhaahee z ga(n)j beshumaar
column3: Then whatever you would desire to obtain from this infinite treasure,

column2: aaidhat dhar dhasat aai aalee tabaar || 370 ||
column3: O person of high status! You would be able to get. (370)

column2: pas bakhhaanee saahibaan shauak raa
column3: Therefore you should call upon the faithful devotees of Akaalpurakh,

column2: taa z haasil kunee(n) iee(n) zauak raa || 371 ||
column3: So that you would be able to inculcate such an ardor and zeal for Him. (371)

column2: zauak shauak hak gar baashadh turaa
column3: If you can acquire the strong desire for the love of Waaheguru,

column2: phaiz iee(n) suhabat asar bakhhashadh turaa || 372 ||
column3: Then, the blessing of their company is bound to influence you and your personality. (372)

column2: gar cheh baashadh dhilahaa nabhabaashadh juz khhudhaa
column3: Even though, there is nothing else but the Almighty abides in the hearts of every one,

column2: aariphaa(n) raa ma(n)zale baashadh uoolaa || 373 ||
column3: Still, the true and sincere enlightened persons have a high status and elevated destination. (373)

column2: g(h)air aariph vaakiph iee(n) haal neesat
column3: No one other than the knowledgeable is aware of the condition(s) of Akaalpurakh,

column2: aariphaa(n) raa g(h)air zikarash kaal neesat || 374 ||
column3: The enlightened do not speak any words other than the discourses and meditation of the Naam of Waaheguru. (374)

column2: baadhashaahaa(n) salatanat bi-guzaashatadh
column3: The kings abdicated their thrones, luxurious living and royal powers,

column2: choo gadhaayaa(n) koo bakoo bishataaphata(n)dh || 375 ||
column3: And they kept roaming around from street to street like beggars. (375)

column2: az barai aa(n) k yaadh kuna(n)dh
column3: For all of them, it is essential to continue to get engaged in the true memory of the Omnipotent;

column2: az makaaphaat dho aalam vaa raha(n)dh || 376 ||
column3: And, thus, get redemption from the cycles of births and deaths in both the worlds. (376)

column2: vaakaph iee(n) raeh agar dhasat aamadhe
column3: If ever one can come across some one who is familiar with this path and tradition,

column2: makasadhash dhar salatanat dhasat aamadhe || 377 ||
column3: Then, all aims and objectives of government administration would be fulfilled. (377)

column2: jumalaa lashakar taalibaan hak shudhe
column3: If all forces of the army were to becomes seekers of Divine Power,

column2: dhar hakeekat aaraph mutalik shudhe || 378 ||
column3: Then, in fact, they all can become enlightened persons indeed. (378)

column2: saalik iee(n) raeh agar dharayaaphate
column3: If we can run into a fellow traveler of this path, and ask him about its true  tradition;

column2: dhil azee(n) shaahee kujaa barataaphate || 379 ||
column3: Then, how can his mind turn away from this royal kingdom? (379)

column2: tukhham hak dhar mazarai dhil kaashate
column3: If the seed of Truth can be cultivated in the fields of mind,

column2: taa g(h)ubaar dhil z dhil baradhaashate || 380 ||
column3: Then, all suspicions and illusions of our mind will be eliminated. (380)

column2: bar sar takhhat nageen kaim budhe
column3: They can sit on a diamond studded throne for good

column2: zikar maualaa gar badhil kaim shudhe || 381 ||
column3: If they can inculcate the meditation of Akaalpurakh in their minds, (381)

column2: booi hak meeaaidh az har mui shaa(n)
column3: Fragrance of Truth is emitting from their each and every hair,

column2: zi(n)dhaa mee shudh har kase az booi shaa(n) || 382 ||
column3: In fact, every one is becoming alive and getting invigorated with the aroma of  the company of such people. (382)

column2: naam hak beeroo(n) na boodh az jisam shaa(n)
column3: Waaheguru's Naam would not have been outside their bodies,

column2: murashadh kaamil agar dhaadhe nishaa(n) || 383 ||
column3: If the perfect Guru had indicated to them with the information about His whereabouts and location. (In stead of looking outside, they could have attained His convergence from within their own hearts.)(383)

column2: aab haivaa(n) a(n)dharoon khhaanaa hasat
column3: The elixir of life is, in fact, inside the heart's so called abode,

column2: lek be-haadhee jahaa(n) beg(h)aanaa(n) hasat || 384 ||
column3: But the world would not know about this fact without a perfect Guru. (384)

column2: choo(n) z shahirag(h) hasat shaeh nazadheek tar
column3: When the True Master is nearer than even your main artery,

column2: choo(n) basahiraa meeravee aai be-khhabar || 385 ||
column3: O ignorant and amateur person! Then why are you roaming around jungles and wilderness. (385)

column2: vaakaph iee(n) raeh choo garadhadh raahanumaa
column3: When someone familair and well conversant with this path becomes your guide,

column2: khhalavate dhar a(n)juman baashadh turaa || 386 ||
column3: You will be able to achieve solitude within the company of noble persons. (386)

column2: har ch shaa(n) a(n)dhar khhilaaphat dhaashata(n)dh
column3: Whatever worldly possessions they have,

column2: jamalaa raa yak baarogee biguzaashata(n)dh || 387 ||
column3: They are willing to relinquish them in one instalment instantly. (387)

column2: az barai aa(n) k hak haasil kuna(n)dh
column3: So that they could achieve the Ultimate Entity,

column2: pairaveei aariph kaamil kuna(n)dh || 388 ||
column3: For this reason, they follow completely the perfectly enlightened persons. (388)

column2: aariph kaamil turaa kaamil kuna(n)dh
column3: Perfect saints can transform you also into perfect saints;

column2: har cheh meekhhaahee turaa haasil kuna(n)dh || 389 ||
column3: And, they can fulfill all your desires and wishes. (389)

column2: raasatee ieenasat raeh hak bageer
column3: The truth in it is that you should adopt the path leading towards the Lord,

column2: taa too ham garadhee choo khhurasheedh muneer || 390 ||
column3: So that you, too, can shine like the brilliance of the sun. (390)

column2: hak dharoon dhil k dhiladhaaree kunadh
column3: The true Akaalpurakh, abiding in your heart, extends His love to you;

column2: murashadh kaamil turaa yaaree kunadh || 391 ||
column3: And, the perfect and complete Guru like a true friend assists you in this process. (391)

column2: vaakaph iee(n) raeh agar aaree badhasat
column3: If you can run into someone who is familiar with this (divine) path,

column2: a(n)dharoo(n) yaabee matai har ch hasat || 392 ||
column3: Then, you will discover all types of material and non-material wealth and treasures inside you. (392)

column2: murashadh kaamil kase raa dhasat dhaadh
column3: Whosoever has come across a true Guru,

column2: taaj iraphaa(n) raa bapharak uoo nihaadh || 393 ||
column3: The true Guru will put on the crown of true divine knowledge on his head. (393)

column2: mahiram hak murashadh kaamil kunadh
column3: The true and perfect Guru can make one conversant with the mysteries and love of Waaheguru,

column2: dhaualat jaaveedh raa haasil kunadh || 394 ||
column3: And, helps in achieving the eternal divine wealth. (394)

column2: har dho aalam ba(n)dhai pharamaan uoo
column3: Persons from both the worlds obey his (the Guru's) command spontaneously,

column2: e'ee(n) jahaano aa(n) jahaa(n) kurabaan uoo || 395 ||
column3: And, both the worlds are willing to lay their lives for him. (395)

column2: maaneei ihasaan iraphaan khhudhaa-sat
column3: The real gratitude for Akaalpurakh is the (achievement of) true divine knowledge,

column2: aariphaa(n) raa dhaualat khhush roo numaa sat || 396 ||
column3: And, the immortal wealth emerges showing its face to the enlightened persons. (396)

column2: taa khhudhai khheshatan bishanaakhhatash
column3: When, by abiding the All-powerful in his heart, recognized His Entity,

column2: nakadh umar jaavidhaa(n) dharayaaphatash || 397 ||
column3: Take it that he achieved the treasure of eternal life. (397)

column2: uoo dharoon dhil too beeroo(n) mee-ravee
column3: He, the Almighty Lord, abides inside your heart, but you keep running around outside,

column2: uoo bakhhaanaa too bahaj choo(n) mee-ravee || 398 ||
column3: He is right inside your home, but you keep going (outside) for Hadj in search of Him. (398)

column2: uoo sat az har mooi too choo(n) aashakaar
column3: When He manifests Himself from each and every hair of your body,

column2: too kujaa beeroo(n) ravee bahir shikaar || 399 ||
column3: Where do you stray outside to track Him out (to hunt for Him). (399)

column2: a(n)dharoon khhaanaa-at noor alaah
column3: The splendor of Akaalpurakh radiates in your home-like-heart in such a way,

column2: taaphat choo(n) bar aasamaa(n) rakhhashi(n)dhaa maeh || 400 ||
column3: Just like the bright moon shines (during moonlit nights) in the sky. (400)

column2: a(n)dharoon chasham tar beenaa shudhaa
column3: It is the Provident who enables you to see through your tearful eyes,

column2: bar zabaanat hukam hak goyaa shudhaa || 401 ||
column3: And, it is His command that speaks from your tongue. (401)

column2: e'ee(n) vajoodhat rauashan az noor hak asat
column3: This body of yours is radiant because of the splendor of Akaalpurakh,

column2: rauashan az noor khhudhai mutalik asat || 402 ||
column3: This entire world is shining with His refulgence. (402)

column2: lek vaakiph neesatee az haal khhesh
column3: But you are not aware of your inside situation and condition,

column2: roozo shab hairaanee az aphaal khhesh || 403 ||
column3: You are distraught day and night because of your own actions and deeds. (403)

column2: murashadh kaamil turaa mahiram kunadh
column3: The perfect true Guru makes you Waaheguru's confidant,

column2: dharadh resh hizar raa maraham kunadh || 404 ||
column3: He provides ointment and dressing for the pain of the wounds of separation. (404)

column2: taa too ham az vaasilaan uoo shavee
column3: So that you can also become one of Waaheguru's close companions,

column2: saahib dhil garadhee vaa khhushaboo shavee || 405 ||
column3: And, you could become the master of your heart with a noble character. (405)

column2: az barai aa(n) k sara-garadhaa(n) shavee
column3: You have ever been perplexed and confused about the Akaalpurakh,

column2: aumar haa a(n)dhar talab hairaa(n) shavee || 406 ||
column3: Because, you have been troubled for ages searching for Him. (406)

column2: too cheh baashee aalame hairaan uoo
column3: What to speak of you alone! The whole world is perplexed indeed for Him,

column2: arasho kurasee jumalaa sara-garadhaan uoo || 407 ||
column3: This sky and the fourth firmament are all distressed about Him. (407)

column2: charakhh mee garadhadh bagiradh aa(n) k uoo
column3: This sky revolves around Him for the reason

column2: dhaaradh az shauak khhudhaa pharakhha(n)dhaa khhoo || 408 ||
column3: That it, too, can adopt noble virtues because of its fondness for Him. (408)

column2: jumalaa hairaana(n)dh sara-garadhaan uoo
column3: The people of the whole world are amazed and confused about Waaheguru,

column2: choo(n) gadhaa joidh uoo raa koo ba-koo || 409 ||
column3: Just like the beggars are looking for Him from street to street. (409)

column2: baadhashaeh har dho aalam dhar dhil asat
column3: The king of both the worlds is abiding inside the heart,

column2: laikan iee(n) aag(h)ishatai aabo gil asat || 410 ||
column3: But this body of our is mired in water and mud. (410)

column2: dhar dhil too nakash hak choo(n) nakash basat
column3: When the True Image of Waaheguru definitely made a stern image and abode  in your heart.

column2: jumalaa naphas shauak shudh aai haka-prasat || 411 ||
column3: Then O devotee of True Akaalpurakh! Your entire family, out of elation and euphoria, will be transformed itself into His image. (411)

column2: nakash hak yaanee nishaan naam hak
column3: The form of Akaalpurakh is really the symbol of His Naam,

column2: aab haivaa(n) raa banosh az jaam hak || 412 ||
column3: Therefore, you should drink the nectar from the cup of Truth. (412)

column2: aa(n) k uoo raa jusatam az har khhaanai
column3: The Lord that I have been looking for from home to home,

column2: yaaphatam naagaeh dhar kaashaanai || 413 ||
column3: Suddenly, I discovered Him inside my own home (body). (413)

column2: e'ee(n) tuphail murashadh kaamil bavadh
column3: This blessing is from the true and perfect Guru,

column2: har cheh mee khhaahee azo haasil shavadh || 414 ||
column3: Whatever I wanted or needed, I could get that from Him. (414)

column2: e'ee(n) muraadh dhil kase be aa(n) na yaaphat
column3: No one else can fulfill his heart's desire,

column2: har gadhai dhaualat sulataa(n) na yaaphat || 415 ||
column3: And, every beggar is not able to acquire royal riches. (415)

column2: naam be murashadh miaa var bar zubaa(n)
column3: Do not bring any name other than that of the Guru on your tongue,

column2: murashadh kaamil dhihadh az hak nishaa(n) || 416 ||
column3: In fact, a perfect Guru alone can give us the correct whereabouts of Akaalpurakh. (416)

column2: murashadh har cheez mee baashadh base
column3: There may be numerous teachers and instructors for every item (in this world),

column2: murashadh kaamil kujaa yaabadh kase || 417 ||
column3: However, when can one meet a perfect Guru? (417)

column2: aa(n) khhudhai paak dhil raa kaam dhaadh
column3: The chaste Waaheguru fulfilled the keen desire of my heart,

column2: e'ee(n) dhil bishakasataa raa aaraam dhaadh || 418 ||
column3: And provided succor to the heart-broken. (418)

column2: haasil hak murashadh kaamil bavadh
column3: To meet a perfect Guru is the real attainment of Akaalpurakh,

column2: zaa(n) k uoo aaraam jaano dhil bavadh || 419 ||
column3: Because it is him (Him) who can bestow tranquility to the mind and the soul. (419)

column2: avalan aai dhil phanai khhesh shau
column3: O my heart! Firstly, you must get rid of your vanity and ego,

column2: taa bayaabee raeh hak dhar kooi o || 420 ||
column3: So that you could get the correct direction from His street to the path of Truth. (420)

column2: vaakiph ar az murashadh kaamil shavee
column3: If you can get to know the perfect and complete true Guru,

column2: be takalaph saahib iee(n) dhil shavee || 421 ||
column3: Then, you can be the master of this heart without any (ritual) problems. (421)

column2: har k uoo khhudh phanai uoo na karadh
column3: Whosoever has not been able to eradicate his self ego,

column2: hak mar uoo raa saahib iraphaa(n) na karadh || 422 ||
column3: The Akaalpurakh does not divulge His mysteries to him. (422)

column2: har cheh hasat aa(n) a(n)dharoon khhaanaa asat
column3: Whatever is there, is inside the house, the human body,

column2: sair kun dhar kishat dhil iee(n) dhaanaa hasat || 423 ||
column3: You should walk around your heart's field of crops; the grain of enlightenment is there only inside it. (423)

column2: murashadh kaamil choo baashadh raahanumaa
column3: When the complete and perfect true Guru becomes your guide and mentor,

column2: baa khhudhai khhesh garadhee aashanaa || 424 ||
column3: You would then become very well informed and conversant about your Waaheguru. (424)

column2: gar dhil too jaanab hak aaradhat
column3: If your heart can be motivated and inspired towards the Omnipotent,

column2: az bun har mooi hak mee baaradhat || 425 ||
column3: Then, there would be a pouring showers of His Naam in every hair of your body. (425)

column2: ham dharee(n) dhuniaa ba-yaabee kaam raa
column3: Then, all your desires in this world would be fulfilled,

column2: khhaak bar sar kun g(h)m ayaam raa || 426 ||
column3: And, you will bury all the worries and apprehensions of the time. (426)

column2: beeroo(n) az jisam too nabhabavadh heech cheez
column3: Nothing exists in this world outside your body,

column2: yak dhame ham khheshatan taa kun tameez || 427 ||
column3: You should introspect just for a moment to realize your own self. (427)

column2: taa ba-yaabee iee(n) saadhat raa madhaam
column3: You will be bestowed with the Waaheguru's true boon for ever,

column2: gar bidhaanee hak kudhaamo man kudhaam || 428 ||
column3: If you can appreciate (the stark distinction) as to who you are and who God is? (428)

column2: man cheh zaraa mushate az khhaak g(h)reeb
column3: Who am I? I am just one particle of one fistful of dust of top-layer,

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa dhaualat z murashadh shudh naseeb || 429 ||
column3: All this blessing, due to my good fortune, was bestowed upon me by my true Guru. (429)

column2: aai zahe murashadh choo maa teeraa dhilaa(n)
column3: Great is the true Guru who has, blind minds like mine,

column2: karadh rauashan dhar zameeno(n) aasamaa(n) || 431 ||
column3: Made them refulgent on both the earth and the sky. (431)

column2: aai zahe murashadh k dhil raa shauak dhaadh
column3: Great is the true Guru who has blessed my heart with a keen desire and fondness,

column2: aai zahe murashadh k ba(n)dh dhil kushaadh || 432 ||
column3: Blessed is the true Guru who has broken all the limitations and shackles of my heart. (432)

column2: aai zahe murashadh k baa hak aashanaa
column3: Great is the true Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, who introduced me to the Lord,

column2: karadh phaarig(h) az g(h)m ra(n)jo balaa || 433 ||

column2: aai zahe murashadh k umar jaavidhaa(n)

column2: bakhhashadh az naam khhudhai be-nishaa(n) || 434 ||

column2: aai zahe murashadh k uoo az kataraa aab
column3: Great is the perfect and true Guru, who has

column2: aai zahe murashadh zahe ihasaan uoo
column3: Blessed is that true Guru and blessed are his numerous boons and bestowals,

column2: sadh hazaaraa(n) hamachoo man kurabaan uoo || 436 ||
column3: For whom millions of people like me are willing to sacrifice themselves. (436)

column2: dhar zameeno aasamaa(n) naamash bavadh
column3: His Naam pervades and is prevalent over the earth and the sky,

column2: har mureedhe saahib kaamash bavadh || 437 ||
column3: It is Him who fulfills all the strong desires of His disciples. (437)

column2: har k khhush baashadh z guphato gooi uoo
column3: Whosoever is elated and satisfied on hearing His conversation,

column2: hak hameshaa baashadh uoo raa roo-baroo || 438 ||
column3: Take it that he will be face to face with the Almighty for ever. (438)

column2: hak hameshaa(n) baashadh uoo raa dhar hazoor
column3: The Akaalpurakh is always present before him,

column2: zikar uoo baashadh mar uoo raa dhar sadhoor || 439 ||
column3: And, the meditation and remembrance of Waaheguru always abides in his heart. (439)

column2: gar hazooree baa khhudhaa baidh ba-tau
column3: If you have the yearning to be face to face to the Omnipotent,

column2: dhar hazoor murashadh kaamil birau || 440 ||
column3: Then, you should try to be face to face to the perfect and complete Guru. (440)

column2: soorat hak murashadh kaamil bavadh
column3: A perfect Guru is, in fact, the image of the Omnipresent,

column2: dheedhanash aaraam jaano dhil bavadh || 441 ||
column3: A glimpse of such a perfect Guru provides succor and serenity to the heart and soul. (441)

column2: surat hak maanee az murashadh bavadh
column3: The perfect and true Guru is, indeed, an image of Akaalpurakh,

column2: har k bara-garadhadh azaa(n) muratadh bavadh || 442 ||
column3: Anyone who has turned himself away from him, was discarded and thrown away like a trash. (442)

column2: murashadh kaamil bag(h)air az hak nabhaguphat
column3: The perfect and the true Guru does not utter anything but the truth,

column2: dhur iee(n) maanee bagair az aa(n) na guphat || 443 ||
column3: No one else but him has been able to pierce the pearl of this spiritual idea. (443)

column2: taa kujaa shukare z ihasaanash kunam
column3: How far and how much can I thank Him for His bestowals ?

column2: har cheh aaidh bar zubaa(n) iee(n) mug(h)tanam || 444 ||
column3: Whatever comes on my lips and tongue, I would consider that as a boon. (444)

column2: az g(h)ilaazat dhil khhudhaa choo(n) paak karadh
column3: When Akaalpurakh cleansed the heart from filth, profanity and muck

column2: murashadh kaamil ba-iee(n) idharaak karadh || 445 ||
column3: The complete and perfect Guru bestowed the good sense to it. (445)

column2: varanaa iee(n) raeh khhudhaa kai jaanadhe
column3: Otherwise, how could we find out the true path of God ?

column2: az kitaab hak sabak kai khhaanadhe || 446 ||

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa choo(n) az tuphail murashadh asat
column3: If all this is the bestowal of the true Guru out of his compassion and kindness,

column2: har keh murashadh raa naa-dhaanadh muratadh asat || 447 ||

column2: murashadh kaamil ilaaj dhil kunadh
column3: The perfect and true Guru removes the maladies of the heart,

column2: kaam dhil a(n)dhar dhilat haasil kunadh || 448 ||

column2: nabaz dhil choo(n) murashadh kaamil shanaakhhat
column3: When the perfect Guru correctly diagnosed the pulse of the heart,

column2: zi(n)dhageei umar raa haasil shanaakhhat || 449 ||

column2: zi(n)dhageei umar haasil mee shavadh
column3: Because of the perfect and true Guru, the human being gets an eternal life,

column2: dhar phiraakash vaalaa o shaidhaa shudhaa || 451 ||

column2: e'ee(n) mataa a(n)dhar dhukaan hak bavadh

column2: murashadh kaamil nishaan hak bavadh || 452 ||
column3: The complete and perfect Guru is the symbolic image of Akaalpurakh Himself. (452)

column2: murashadh kaamil dhihadh paakee turaa
column3: The perfect Guru, reference here is to Guru Gobind Singh Ji, bestows chastity and holiness upon you;

column2: mee kashadh az chaeh g(h)manaakee turaa || 453 ||

column2: murashadh kaamil ilaaj dhil kunadh
column3: The perfect and true Guru removes the maladies of the heart,

column2: e'ee(n) muraadh dhil badhil haasil kunadh || 454 ||
column3: With which, all the heart's desires are achieved (fulfilled) within the heart itself. (454)

column2: suhabat aariph ajab dhaualat bavadh
column3: The company of noble souls is, by itself, an extraordinary wealth,

column2: e'ee(n) hamaa mauakooph bar suhabat bavadh || 455 ||

column2: aai azeez man shinau az man sakhhun
column3: O my dear ! Please listen to what I have to say,

column2: taa bayaabee raeh a(n)dhar jaano tan || 456 ||

column2: taalib maradhaan hak raa dhoosatadhaar
column3: You should become friendly to the seekers of the Waaheguru's devotees,

column2: g(h)air zikarash bar zubaa(n) haraphe mayaar || 457 ||
column3: And should not bring any word other than the meditation of the Naam of Akaalpurakh on your tongue and lips. (457)

column2: khhaak shau maradhaan hak raa khhaak baash

column2: ne pe dhuneeaai dhoo(n) g(h)manaak baash || 458 ||
column3: And, do not worry about this frivolous and undignified world. (458)

column2: g(h)r too khhaanee nusakhhaa az shaan ishak

column2: meeshavee sar dhaphatar dheevaan ishak || 459 ||

column2: eishak maualaa mar turaa maualaa kunadh
column3: Love for Waaheguru transforms you into the very image of Waaheguru Himself,

column2: dhar dho aalam mihataro aaualaa kunadh || 460 ||
column3: And, makes you lofty and famous in both the worlds. (460)

column2: yaa ilaahee iee(n) dhilam raa shauak dhih
column3: O my Akaalpurakh! Kindly bless this heart of mine with Your devotion and love,

column2: lazate az shauak khhaaso zauak dheh || 461 ||
column3: And, also bestow upon me the savor of the euphoria of Your love. (461)

column2: taa ba-yaadhat biguzaradh roozo shabam

column2: dheh rahaiee ba(n)dhaa raa az ba(n)dh g(h)m || 462 ||

column3: Kindly bless me with such a treasure that should be permanent and everlasting,

column2: neeate aa(n) dheh k baashadh hak guzaar
column3: Kindly bless me with such intentions and purposes that should worship the Truth,

column2: hi(n)mate aa(n) dheh k baashadh jaa(n) nisaar || 464 ||

column2: e'ee(n) dhil birayaan maa raa shauak dhih
column3: Kindly bless our charred hearts with the fervor (of Your love)

column2: dhar g(h)ulem ba(n)dhagee raa tauak dheh || 467 ||

column2: zikar maualaa dham ba-dham dhar jaan uoo
column3: He meditates and describes His virtues every breath of his life,

column2: haasil iee(n) umar pesh murashidh asat

column2: murashadh kaamil bavadh dheedhaar hak

column2: soorat hak murashadh kaamil bavadh

column2: nakash uoo dhar dhil kas jaa kunadh
column3: When His image resides permanently in someone's heart,

column2: khhaasatam tarateeb iee(n) dhur dhaanaa raa

column2: aab haivaa(n) pur shudhaa choo jaam uoo
column3: (This compilation) Like a cup is filled to the brim with the divine elixir,

column2: kaz takalum booi iraphaa(n) aaidhash
column3: From his speeches emerges the fragrance of divine knowledge,

column2: har k khhaanadh az reh lutapho karam
column3: Whosoever recites this with the grace and compassion of Waaheguru,

column3: He receives laurels among the enlightened persons. (500)

column2: hasat zikar aariphaan paak raa

column2: aa(n) k uoo rauashan kunadh idharaak raa || 501 ||

column2: neesat dhar vai mu(n)dharaj aai baa-khhabar
column3: O informed person! In this volume,

column2: yaadh hak saramaayaa-i rauashan dhileesat

column2: yaa ilaahee har dhil pazamuradhaa raa

column3: O Waaheguru! Kindly help this person, yours truly,
